Poți renunța oricând din pagina înscrierii tale.» / “Optional. You can opt out any time from your registration page.” — «Opțional» leads the helper rather than trailing the sentence's full stop. It is never pre-ticked, never required, never folded (§59) and never blocking: consent is a clear affirmative act (art. 4(11), 7 GDPR). It is on every event, whether or not the event publishes a list. Every word a person or the club reads says «oferte și beneficii» / “offers and benefits”: the helper, the switches, the backoffice line, the export's column, the newsletter's fold, the `/admin/tasks` row, the guide, the legend and the notice.

**Stored with its moment, and the moment kept.** `registrations.promo_consent` (boolean, NOT NULL, default false) and `registrations.promo_consent_at` (the moment of the tick, or of the last change through a switch), expand-only migration `0113_promo_consent`. The notice version a form's tick was given under is the row's existing `privacy_notice_version`; a later yes from the person's own page is given under the notice in force at `promo_consent_at` (the version windows on `/admin/legal` say which) — no third column. Because a withdrawal rewrites `promo_consent_at`, the moment a consent was first given lives on the audit trail: a form that keeps a tick writes one row `registration.promo_consent_changed` `{ to: true, via: FORM }` in the registration's own transaction (a restarted or corrected form that takes a yes back writes `{ to: false, via: FORM }`; an unticked box on a row that never said yes writes nothing), as the declaration page's tick writes `via: DECLARATION` — so after a withdrawal the club can still show that, and when, the person consented (art. 7(1) GDPR).

**The gate (AGENTS.md §10.8, the §396 mechanism).** A new merge field, `{{promotionalMaterials}}`, is both the words and the switch: filled with the box's own label, quoted, club name included, from the catalogue the form reads (`registrations/promo-consent-words.ts`), and read by `describesPromotionalMaterials`. The form offers the box only while the privacy notice in force names it in every language (`cachedPromotionalMaterialsOffered`); `submitRegistration` keeps a tick only when the notice this registration records names it — so a `true` is always consent to a text that described it, and a value posted while the notice does not describe it is ignored, never refused. `/admin/tasks` carries an open, never blocking row `promoNotice` with the steps; `/admin/legal` says the same beside the socials' line (`legal.promoMissing`); the legal editor's token legend lists the field, its example the same sentence with a plain «club», since the legend never names the club (§369). No text in effect changes: production keeps its approved notice until the club approves a new version from the template, and until then no box is shown and nothing is kept.

**Who may give it.** Only the person. A staff «Înscriere nouă» and the desk never set it — the service ignores a posted value on a staff origin, and the staff form says «Oferte și beneficii: nu» with the reason, while the notice describes it. On a family's sitting (§543) the address holder's own form keeps it, and a minor's form keeps it (the parent consents for the child, as for the list); another adult's does not (§421: `withoutAnotherAdultsConsents` and `withoutAnotherAdultsDetails` drop it). That adult gives it on their own declaration: the declaration page — each step of the family's wizard (§471) included — carries the same optional box, offered while the notice describes it and the registration has not said yes; a tick there is written in the signing transaction and ignored, never refused, when the notice does not describe it. A test registration is kept exactly like a real one (AGENTS.md §12.6) and listed nowhere.

**Per registration, and the words say so.** The consent is a column of the registration, not of the person: a person who ticked at one event and not at another has said yes to one and not to the other. So every door speaks of «această înscriere», never of the person at large: «La această înscriere primești oferte și beneficii.» / “On this registration you receive offers and benefits.”, «La această înscriere nu ai bifat oferte și beneficii.» / “You did not tick offers and benefits on this registration.”, and the switches «Nu mai vreau oferte și beneficii pentru această înscriere» / «Vreau oferte și beneficii pentru această înscriere». A switch changes that registration alone. The notice says the same: «răspunsul îl dai pentru fiecare înscriere în parte».

**Withdrawal (art. 7(3)).** `registrations/promo-consent.ts`, the shape of `list-consent.ts`: one write — the row locked, `promo_consent` and `promo_consent_at` set, one audit row `registration.promo_consent_changed` carrying `to: true|false` and the door, never a name — and four doors: the manage page, per person (§547), with the switch and the state in words, and «Înscrierile mele» (§77), with the state in words and the way out only (below), the token read and never spent on either; the declaration page, a yes only; and an Administrator on the registration's page, a withdrawal only, for a person who wrote to the club («Retrage consimțământul» gains «Acordul pentru oferte și beneficii»; the audit row names the actor and the reason). A yes is accepted only while the notice in force describes it; a no always — so the way out is shown whenever a registration says yes, even under a notice that no longer names the field, and «Înscrierile mele» lists a closed registration that still says yes — in words of its own, «Ai bifat oferte și beneficii la această înscriere. Cât timp e închisă, clubul nu îți trimite nimic pentru ea; poți retrage acordul oricând.» (`Registrations.promo.closedYes`), since the newsletter's fold never lists a closed registration. The same answer twice writes nothing. An Administrator's withdrawal of the health note, the socials or the results together with this consent is one transaction (`withdrawOptionalData`): whole or nothing.

**Another adult on the address: from the holder's link, only the way out.** The manage page lists the address's registrations at the event (§547). On another adult's row — not the link's own registration and not a minor today by the guardian rule's calendar (`anotherAdultOnTheLink`; a missing or unreadable birth date counts as an adult, the safe side) — it offers «Nu mai vreau oferte și beneficii pentru această înscriere» while the row says yes, and otherwise no button, only «Acordul pentru oferte și beneficii îl dă doar persoana, din declarația ei sau din linkul înscrierii ei. De aici îl poți doar retrage.». The server refuses a yes posted for such a row through another registration's link (FORBIDDEN), whatever the page drew. A minor's row keeps the yes: the parent consents for the child, as on the form. The adult says yes on their own declaration or through their own registration's manage link. This reverses the first round's reading that the per-person doors «trust the inbox»: the notice says another adult gives it themselves, and the holder's page now does what the notice says.

**«Înscrierile mele» is a door out only (second fix round).** That page lives under the address's own link (`MANAGE_PROFILE`), not one person's: it lists every registration of the address, another adult's included, and cannot tell the holder from that adult — and the notice names it only as a way to withdraw. So it offers «Nu mai vreau oferte și beneficii pentru această înscriere» while a row says yes, and on a row that says no — while the notice in force describes the offers — only one sentence, «Acordul pentru oferte și beneficii se dă din pagina înscrierii (linkul din emailul ei) sau din declarație. De aici îl poți doar retrage.» / “The consent to offers and benefits is given on the registration's own page (the link in its email) or on the declaration. From here you can only withdraw it.” (`Registrations.promo.whereToSayYes`). The server refuses a yes through this door for every row, the holder's own included, as FORBIDDEN (`setPromoConsentFromMyRegistrations`), whatever the page drew; a no is accepted as before. The yes is given on the form, on the declaration, or on the registration's own manage link — which says whose registration it is. This replaces the first fix round's «left as it was».

**Two consents, two switches.** The newsletter (§445) and this consent are separate: a newsletter unsubscribe does not touch `promo_consent`, and a withdrawal here does not touch the newsletter. The person's page says so in one sentence.

**The notice template** (both languages, section 5 «E-mailurile»; the twelve sections and their numbers, which the code and the guide cite, are kept): a paragraph «Oferte și beneficii:» naming `{{promotionalMaterials}}` — offers and benefits from the club and from its partners (sponsors, shops, the events' partners), sent by the club alone to the registration's address, the partners never receiving the address or any other data; answered for each registration separately; consent, art. 6(1)(a) GDPR and art. 12 of Law 506/2004 (in English «Romanian Law no. 506/2004», as the section's other paragraphs say it); the box optional and unticked; given when registering, when signing the declaration or later from the registration's page; for another adult on the address, only that person, when signing their declaration or from their own registration's link; withdrawn any time from the registration's page, «Înscrierile mele» or by writing to <EMAIL DE CONTACT> (the English text: <CONTACT EMAIL>, so the English notice is never filled with the Romanian «sau» between two addresses), with no consequence for the registration; separate from the newsletter; the list seen only by the club's organizers and administrators, who may download it. Section 6's «Nu le vindem…» adds «nici partenerilor clubului, ale căror oferte și beneficii ți le trimite clubul însuși». Section 7: «Acordul pentru oferte și beneficii: până îl retragi, dar nu mai mult decât înscrierea.» The four placeholders are untouched (§29). The template's own header says what changed; `/admin/legal` sees the moved template by its hash (§532).

**The backoffice and the exports.** The registration's page: «Oferte și beneficii: da, din <data> / nu» (shown while the notice describes it, or while the row says yes). The registrations CSV and spreadsheet end with «Offers and benefits» — the moment of the yes, or empty — last, so no column moves. `/admin/newsletter` gains a second fold under «Abonați», «Participanți care au bifat oferte și beneficii» (the `partners` glyph, closed by default, its line the count with `countForm`): name, address, event, the moment, newest first, at most 500 rows drawn and the whole list in its own «Descarcă CSV» (`GET /api/admin/newsletter/promo`, `oferte-si-beneficii-<date>.csv`, UTF-8 with a BOM, `csvCell`, the audit row `newsletter.promo_consenters_exported` with the row count only). Listed: a real registration whose address is proved and which still stands (waiting for its declaration, on the waiting list, offered, confirmed) — never an unproved address, a cancelled, expired or test one. The readers are §550's: the Organizer, the Administrator and the Superadministrator (`canSendNewsletter`), asserted in the page, the route and the read; a volunteer, the Redactor, Tehnic and a member get nothing. The guide says one sentence in the Organizer's and the Administrator's newsletter steps, and the GDPR request's withdrawal step names the new group.

**Refused.** A pre-ticked box, or one required to register (not a consent). A box shown before the notice describes it, or a tick kept under an older notice (§10.8). The address holder consenting for another adult (§421), on the form or from the holder's manage link. Staff ticking it for a person. Folding it into the newsletter (two purposes, two answers — art. 7(2)). A third email-link door with its own token purpose (an enum migration for a door the manage page already is). A separate column for the notice version of a later yes (the version windows answer it). Giving the partners the list (the club sends; the notice says so). Renaming the column `promo_consent` or the merge field `{{promotionalMaterials}}` to the new words: a migration and a changed marker in texts the club may already have approved, for no reader — only the words people read changed.

Baseline `BR-V2.38-2026-09-27`.

## 563. The difficulty's number is the level of fifteen, the dots are the step

**The owner, 2026-09-29 14:10**, of two tooltips side by side, «Mediu 2 — nivelul 5 din 15» and «Ușor 2 — nivelul 2 din 15»: «ceva ciudat cu nivelurile, nu are cum și una grea și una ușoară să fie nivelul 2» … «vreau un scale mai clar» … «adică ușor: 1,2,3, mediu 4,5,6 și tot așa, în ordine». And at 14:18, of the tooltip: it must explain all the levels, not only the current band's — «Mediu — nivelul 5 din 15 · ușor 1–3 · mediu 4–6 · greuț 7–9 · greu 10–12 · foarte greu 13–15».

**Decision — the number is the level, the dots are the step.** The scale does not change (§526): five bands of three, one `events.difficulty_level` column 1–15, level = (band − 1) × 3 + step. Only the words change, everywhere the difficulty is said, and they come from one domain function, `difficultyWords(level, t)` in `events/domain/difficulty.ts`, which every public surface and every message reads:

- the pill (the listing card, the event page, the backoffice list — `buildRoutePills`, §388): «Mediu 5» / «Medium 5» — the band and the level, never «Mediu 2». The editor's closed line says the same thing in the same «{band} {level}» form, from the backoffice catalogue's own `editor.difficultySummary` with the band word the editor's select shows, rather than through `difficultyWords` — the same words, and one catalogue key fewer to move;
- where no gauge is drawn (the emails' facts block, §392; the calendar entry and the `.ics`, §107): «Mediu, nivelul 5 din 15» / «Medium, level 5 of 15». «Treapta 2 din 3» is gone from both catalogues;
- the pill's tooltip, two lines: «Mediu — nivelul 5 din 15», then the whole ladder, «ușor 1–3 · mediu 4–6 · greuț 7–9 · greu 10–12 · foarte greu 13–15» (`difficultyLadder`, every range from `difficultyBandLevels`, never typed). `GlyphChip`'s tooltip keeps a newline as a line (§257);
- a screen reader hears the shorter form once, as the chip's `srLabel` (§528): «Dificultate: mediu — nivelul 5 din 15 (mediu: 4–6)» — the level and its own band's range. The whole ladder in the name of every card would be read out once per card down a listing, so it stays in the tooltip, the editor's help and «Ghid».

The gauge keeps its band segments and its step dots (§526): the dots still show where inside its band the level stands; the number beside them is the level.

**The editor (amending §526 and §537).** «Treapta» becomes «Nivelul» / «Level». Its three segments show the chosen band's own three levels — Mediu → 4 · 5 · 6, Ușor → 1 · 2 · 3 — and follow the band select as it changes; with no band chosen they show their dots and a dash. Each segment is named «Nivelul 5 din 15» for a screen reader. What posts is still the step 1 · 2 · 3, so with the band it writes the same level column: no migration. The line under the toggle says the rule in one sentence, every number from the domain: «Nivelul e de la 1 (ușor) la 15 (foarte greu): fiecare categorie are trei niveluri — ușor 1–3, mediu 4–6, greuț 7–9, greu 10–12, foarte greu 13–15.» — «categorie», not «bandă», because it is the word the editor and «Ghid» already use for a band. The «?» keeps the owner's examples in level numbers: «mediu 4: alergarea de pe Tâmpa», «greuț 7–9: de la semimaraton în sus». §537's one centred axis is unchanged.

**The filter (§413)** still ticks a whole band; its boxes and its active chips add the range, «Mediu (4–6)», and a box's hover title stays «Mediu: nivelurile 4–6 din 15» (§528). **«Ghid»** → «Scara de dificultate a clubului» says the same ladder and its examples in level numbers: «Mediu 5», and «Greu» ticking all three of its levels, 10–12 (the guide-words test refuses a parenthesised label inside «…»). Its last two steps say what the pill says on a tap — the level, «Mediu — nivelul 5 din 15», and under it the whole ladder — two sentences, so each stays within 200 characters.

**Refused:** renumbering the steps or the column — the level already runs 1–15, only the words were wrong; the whole ladder in the screen reader's name of every listing card.

Baseline `BR-V2.38-2026-09-27`.

## 564. The documents say «eveniment montan» and «teren accidentat», never «trail»

**The owner, 2026-09-29 15:45:** "we need to rephrase a bit the declarations and documents: let's not call it «cursă montană» but «eveniment montan»; and don't use romgleză — don't use «trail» in a Romanian document, use «teren accidentat»."

**Decision.** A wording pass over every Romanian document the platform writes, with the English twins following. No rule changes and no new content: §556's texts keep every fact, every rule and every placeholder; only the words change. It amends §515 (the race declarations' titles), §523 (the group-run declarations' titles) and §556 (the shoes sentence).

- **The race declaration's title** is «Declarație pe propria răspundere — eveniment montan» (was «— cursă trail»); English "Self-declaration — mountain event" (was "— trail race").
- **The road one follows, for symmetry**: «Declarație pe propria răspundere — eveniment pe asfalt / în parc» (was «— cursă pe asfalt / în parc»); English "Self-declaration — road / park event". The brief kept it unless a sentence pairs the two; they are paired — «Sarcini»'s steps name the two cards one after the other, `/admin/legal` groups them as «Declarații de cursă», and the editor's select and its mismatch sentence («Traseul e pe «Asfalt», iar varianta aleasă e «Eveniment montan»: pentru el se potrivește «Eveniment pe șosea sau în parc»») set them side by side — so both say «eveniment».
- **The group-run pair is «asfalt» and «teren accidentat»**: «Declarație pe propria răspundere (alergare de grup, teren accidentat)». English keeps "(group run, trail)": "trail" is English's own word for the ground.
- **The shoes** (§556's grip sentence, kept): «încălțăminte adecvată terenului, cu aderență corespunzătoare (de preferat încălțăminte pentru teren accidentat)» in the race's mountain text and the group run's; English keeps "(preferably trail shoes)".
- **«montan» stays as an adjective**: «trasee montane sau de pădure», «teren montan», «serviciu de ghidaj montan».
- **Every Romanian sentence that names a document** follows the titles: the editor's race-declaration kinds («Eveniment montan», «Eveniment pe șosea sau în parc») and their help, the road fallback («semnează declarația pentru eveniment montan»), `/admin/legal`'s intro, its «Ce este» lines, its short filter names («Eveniment montan», «Eveniment asfalt / parc», «Grup teren accidentat»), the group-run box's «pe asfalt sau pe teren accidentat», «Sarcini»'s race-declaration row and its steps, the one-press approval's line, the guide's legal step, and the club's starting to-do list («declarația pentru teren accidentat»). Three sentences were reworded to stay within §511's 200 characters and six-word parentheses.

**Not changed, on purpose.** The surface's pill and filter «Trail» on the listing and in the editor's «Suprafață» select — UI, not a document — and so the lines that quote that label («declarație pentru Trail», «Textul în vigoare pentru Trail: …»); the enum values and code names (`TRAIL`, `EVENT_DECLARATION`, `GROUP_RUN_DECLARATION_TRAIL`, `declarationTrailRo`); the texts in the database. Nothing in effect changes with this release: the club regenerates from the templates («Regenerează din șabloane», or «Versiune nouă» → «Pornește de la șablon») and approves, as CLAUDE.md's item 16 already asks — the four declarations now show «Șablon nou». The sample seed takes the new titles by itself (it reads the templates) and keeps the placeholders (§29). No migration.

**Held by a test.** `tests/unit/legal-documents/romanian-words.test.ts`: no Romanian template title or body says «trail» (a whole word, any case) or «cursă montană»/«cursă trail»; the Romanian catalogue's one «Trail» is the surface pill `Event.surface.TRAIL`; `/admin/legal`'s names are the templates' titles in both languages; no English string about a declaration says "trail race" or "mountain race".

Baseline `BR-V2.38-2026-09-27`.

## 565. The club's legal name and CIF on the site: one line on the «about» pages and the contact page, a block under the footer's bar

**The owner, 2026-09-29:** «on the about pages and contact pages we need to show "<the club's legal name> (Brasov Runners) CIF <the CIF>" in order to meet legal requirements»; then «and also in the footer, more clearly»; then, with a screenshot of another running club's footer, «look at how other run clubs have this». Their footer: a light band, a row of page links, and three columns under it: the club's legal name as a heading with «C.I.F.» and the country under it; three social marks; «Contact» with a phone and an email.

**Decision.** One Server Component, `ClubIdentity` (`src/shared/ui/ClubIdentity.tsx`), in two shapes.

- **`line`**: «<legal name> (<site name>) · CIF <CIF>», one secondary line that wraps at 320 px. It sits at the end of every «about» page and of the contact page. The «about» pages are the club's standing pages (`/pages/[slug]`, where «Despre» is written) and «Echipa». On the contact page it is the page's last line: under the form, or under the address where there is no form, and under the newsletter's box. Without the CIF it reads «<legal name> (<site name>)».
- **`block`**: under the footer's bar on every page, never inside «Despre club». From `sm` it has three columns; on a phone they stack in small text. The first column is the legal name in the site's heading face, with the site's name in brackets, then «C.I.F. <CIF>» and «România» / "Romania". The middle column holds the club's social marks. They come from the bar's own list, now one helper (`clubSocialLinks`), and the column is hidden when none is set. The last column is «Contact», a paragraph in the heading's style rather than an `<h2>`, like the legal name: the block ends every page, the backoffice's too, and a «Contact» section in every page's outline would be noise. The column holds the address the club chose to show (§442), the public phone when one is set, and «Scrie-ne» to the contact page. Every link has its glyph and is 44 pixels tall. The block is not the bar, so §372's footer-only exception does not reach it.

**Composed, never typed.** The legal name and the CIF are `CLUB_LEGAL_NAME` and `CLUB_REGISTRATION_NUMBER`, read through `clubFactsFromEnv`: the same variables the legal texts are filled with (§132). The name in brackets is `CLUB_NAME` (§215, §369). The variable may carry its own label («CIF …», which is how the legal texts read it after a comma). `bareRegistrationNumber` (`club-facts.ts`) drops a leading «CIF», «C.I.F.», «CUI» or «C.U.I.», so the site writes the label once. The repository is public, so it holds none of the values. Unset (CI, a fresh checkout, the e2e run), the line is absent and so is the block's first column. The other columns keep their places. Two checks now enforce §132's «environment, never source». `yarn secrets:check` reads the three variables from the machine's environment and `.env.local` (`scripts/club-facts-values.mjs`) and refuses a commit whose tracked files carry a value, naming the variable and never the value. It looks for the CIF both as the variable holds it and bare, with the label dropped by the same rule as `bareRegistrationNumber`. The script repeats that rule because it cannot import TypeScript, and a test keeps the two in step. The bare number is what the site shows, so it is the form most likely to be typed. `tests/unit/legal-documents/club-facts-no-literal.test.ts` runs the same search over `src/`, `tests/`, `messages/`, `.release/`, `docs/`, `scripts/` and the root's documents. It also checks that the identity's sources and words carry no telephone-shaped number.

**«Telefon public».** No phone setting existed, so there is one optional setting under «Pagini» → «Contact», with its glyph and its «Salvează» behind the §384 confirmation. It is the Administrator's (`canManageClubSettings`, asserted in the action and in the service), like the other contact settings. It is a `platform_settings` row (a key-value store), so there is no migration. It is audited as whether a number is set, never the number, and the save expires the public pages. It keeps the number as typed and dials its digits. An empty box shows none.

**Refused.**

- *The block inside the sticky `<footer>`.* The bar is sticky and one row at every scroll position (§372, §385). Inside it, the block would ride along over every screen. The block follows the `<footer>` as its sibling instead. The bar's box, height and fold are what they were, and the block is what every page ends on. `footer.spec.ts` measures the bar without the block: from the bar's top to the block's top is the one row, and nothing follows the block.
- *The seat.* On many a club's certificate it is a person's address, and the owner asked for the name and the CIF. It can be added as its own line of the first column.
- *`CONTACT_FORM_TO`.* That is who receives the form's messages, not an address the club publishes. The block shows the chosen shown address (§442).
- *A serif heading like the example's.* The block uses the site's heading face.
- *Sample legal facts on the e2e server.* They would change every participant email's sender line (§323) across the suite. The render test sets made-up values («Asociația Exemplu», «RO00000000», a fake phone). The e2e specs check the line and the first column when drawn, and their absence when not, and never compare with a value.
- *A phone variable in the environment.* The club changes a phone without a deploy, like the shown address.

Baseline `BR-V2.40-2026-09-27`.

## 566. The difficulty pill says the band alone beside its gauge, and its tooltip is a block (amends §563)

**The owner, 2026-09-29 19:08**, of the pill reading «Mediu 5» beside its gauge: «don't put "Mediu 2" and "Ușor 2" on the pill, the sub indicator is enough». **The pill says the band alone** — «Ușor», «Mediu», «Greuț», «Greu», «Foarte greu» / «Easy» … «Very hard» — because the gauge beside it already draws the step in its dots and the tooltip says the level: a number beside them said it a third time. `difficultyWords(level, t).short` is `Event.difficultyValues.<band>`, and `Event.difficultyLevelShort` is gone from both catalogues. Nothing else moves: the tooltip («Mediu — nivelul 5 din 15» and the ladder), the screen reader's `srLabel` («Dificultate: mediu — nivelul 5 din 15 (mediu: 4–6)»), the words where no gauge is drawn (the emails, the calendar, the `.ics`: «Mediu, nivelul 5 din 15»), the editor's closed line («Mediu 5»), the filter's «Mediu (4–6)». «Ghid» says it: on the site the pill shows the band alone and the gauge's dots show the level within the band.

**The tooltip, set as a block** (the owner, 19:48: «vreau ca acest tooltip să fie formatat mai frumos», of «foarte / greu 13–15» split wherever the bubble ended): the level in bold on the first line, «Mediu — nivelul 5 din 15», then the ladder one band per row — the band's word on the left, its levels in an aligned column on the right, the level's own band bold, tinted and marked by a dot drawn in CSS — with no line that wraps; the same words and facts as before (`difficultyWords(...).block`, from the new `Event.difficultyLevelHead` and `Event.difficultyLevelRange`), handed to the client chip as data (`DifficultyTooltipBlock`), while the string form still times the tap and a screen reader still hears only `srLabel`.

**Amends §563**, whose pill said the band and the level, «Mediu 5»; everything else §563 decided stands.

**Refused:** keeping the number on the pill — the gauge and the tooltip already say it.

Baseline `BR-V2.40-2026-09-27`.

## 567. «Șterge» on a signed legal version retires and hides it; its text stays

**The owner, 2026-09-29, from `/admin/legal`** — a screenshot of a group-run declaration's «Versiunile» table: version 1 «Înlocuită», «1 semnături · 0 evenimente · 0 înscrieri», its action cell reading «Nu se poate nici retrage, nici șterge: 1 semnături, 0 evenimente și 0 înscrieri depind de această versiune» — and: «aș vrea să pot șterge (cu dublă confirmare) chiar și documentele care sunt deja semnate».

**The rule that binds.** A signed version is the club's proof of what a person accepted: §556 stores the version, the moment and the text's hash on every acceptance, the signed PDF renders the text from the version's row, and AGENTS.md §10.8 forbids losing what was in force. So a version's text is never destroyed while a signature, an event or a registration depends on it. What the owner can have is the version out of his way.

**Decision — «Șterge» on a version with dependants is retire-and-hide** (amending §181, §203, §418 and §556):

- **What it does.** One expand-only migration (`0114_legal_version_deleted`) gives `legal_documents` `deleted_at`, `deleted_by_staff_user_id` (FK `staff_users`, `SET NULL`) and `deleted_reason`, and a CHECK that a deleted row is also withdrawn and carries a reason. `deleteReliedOnVersion` sets the three and, in the same statement, `withdrawn_at` if it was not yet — so every reader that already skips a withdrawn version (the text in force, the effective dates the public cache waits for, the event editor's choices, the templates' «Șablon nou» and «Regenerează» comparison, the first notice that describes the list's states) skips it with no second condition. The row, the number and both texts stay; the acceptances keep pointing at it; the registration's page, the desk, the signed PDF and the version's own page read it by id and still find it.
- **Never in force again.** Not today, and not on a later effective date: a version approved ahead of its date and chosen by an event, deleted, stays out of force when its date comes (tested). No verb reaches a deleted version any more: withdrawal, approval, both real deletes and a second «Șterge» are refused (`deletionObstacle` gained `deleted`).
- **The numbering continues.** The row is kept, so `nextVersionNumber` counts it and the next draft never reuses a deleted number; nothing goes into `legal_document_numbering`.
- **Two confirmations, checked on the server.** «Șterge» on the row opens the version's delete screen, which asks in two steps: step 1 states the consequences with the real counts in words («1 semnătură, 0 evenimente și 0 înscrieri rămân valabile, iar textul rămâne în arhivă. Versiunea dispare din listă și nu mai poate fi pusă în vigoare.») and asks a required reason of 3 to 200 characters; step 2 asks the version's number typed by hand («6», a `v` in front forgiven) and carries «Șterg versiunea 6» with the bin glyph. The server checks the role first (the Administrator and the Superadministrator; the Organizer and the Tehnic role are refused), then the reason (refused naming «Motivul»), then the rule (so a number typed on the version in force comes back as in force, not as a wrong number), then the number (refused naming «Numărul versiunii», emptied and asked again), then the rule again inside the transaction. A page with two steps rather than a modal dialog, as §203's delete screen does: a refusal lands where the question is still shown, and the form works without JavaScript — then both steps are drawn together and posted at once.
- **The audit row** `legal_document_version.deleted` goes first in the transaction: the key, the number, the effective date, the approver, the hashes, the reason, the counts that stood on it (signatures, events, registrations, and for a terms version the registrations agreed inside its window) and `textKept: true` — never the text (§12.12). It is told apart from `legal_document.deleted`, which destroyed a version nothing relied on.
- **A version with no dependants keeps §203's real delete, as today**: the same screen with one confirmation — the typed phrase (`GDPR 2`) and a reason — and the number retired. «Șterge» there never hides instead: a version nothing depends on has no text to keep, and a press that finds nothing depending on it any more is refused with its own sentence so the screen offers the real delete.
- **The version in force is never deletable**, signed or not: approve the next version first. `removalPlan` asks it before the counts, so a version in force with signatures is refused as in force, with what to do.
- **«Versiuni șterse».** Under each text's versions, a closed fold, its count on the summary line like «Versiunile» above it («1 versiune»), with the swept-bin glyph, read-only: the version, who deleted it, when, the reason, the counts and «Citește textul» to its page, which says it was deleted and why. Nothing is restored from it: a deleted version must never come back into force by accident, and the same words again are a new version («Versiune nouă» from its page), approved like any other.
- **The words.** The count line and every refusal sentence take each noun's form from the count by the site's no-ICU rule (`countForm`, §341): «1 semnătură», «2 semnături», «0 semnături», «20 de semnături», «1 eveniment», «1 înscriere»; English "1 signature". The row of a relied-on version now says «Nu se poate retrage: … depind de ea. «Șterge» o scoate din listă; textul rămâne pentru cine l-a semnat.»

**Refused.** Destroying a signed version's text, even behind a double confirmation — it is the club's proof. A restore button on the fold. Hiding a version nothing depends on instead of deleting it. The phrase `GDPR 6` as the second step — the page already names the text, and a number is what a thumb types on a phone. Ticking relied-on versions into the batch delete — they stay under «Rămân», pointing at the row's «Șterge».

**Consequences.** An event whose chosen declaration was deleted keeps pointing at it; what a participant signs is read by the event's kind of course, never by that id (§515), and the editor asks for a new choice. A privacy notice that described the public list's states, once deleted, no longer counts as the first such notice (§421), so registrants under it lose their stage on the public list — the error errs towards showing less.

Baseline `BR-V2.40-2026-09-27`.

## 568. The declarations name death among the inherent risks and waive the claims for them within the law's limits

**The owner, 2026-09-29:** «vreau la declarații să fim acoperiți inclusiv în caz de deces».

**Decision.** The four declaration templates — the race's mountain and road/park texts (`EVENT_DECLARATION`, `EVENT_DECLARATION_ROAD`, one body since §515) and the two group-run texts (§393, §523) — say, in Romanian and English:

1. **The risks name death.** The race's first risk bullet of each course ends «…accidentare, agravarea unei afecțiuni preexistente, vătămare gravă sau deces» / "…serious injury or death"; the acceptance paragraph says where the inherent risks come from — the ground, the weather, the runner's own health, the other participants, animals, and traffic where the course uses or crosses roads — and «Aceste riscuri pot duce la accidentare, la vătămare gravă sau chiar la deces.»
2. **The runner takes part at their own risk and accepts those risks, death included:** «Particip de bunăvoie și pe propriul risc.» … «Le accept în cunoștință de cauză, inclusiv riscul de vătămare gravă sau de deces…».
3. **A waiver, separate from the acceptance, within the law's limits.** Art. 1355(4) says the acceptance alone is no waiver, and that sentence stays. After it: «Renunț însă, separat și expres, în limitele permise de lege, la pretențiile pentru prejudiciile ce decurg exclusiv din riscurile inerente, fără vina organizatorului, inclusiv vătămare gravă sau deces.» «Renunțarea privește pretențiile față de organizator, echipa lui de organizare, voluntarii și partenerii lui.» «Ea nu privește prejudiciile cauzate din vina acestora și nu înlătură obligațiile de siguranță ale organizatorului.» «Renunțarea îi obligă și pe moștenitorii mei, în limitele permise de lege.» English says the same, "to the extent the law allows" ("I do, however, separately and expressly waive, to the extent the law allows, my claims for harm arising solely from the inherent risks, without the organiser's fault, serious injury or death included.", "This waiver also binds my heirs, to the extent the law allows."). The waiver names death in its own words rather than only pointing back to the acceptance, because a clause the club drafts is read against the club (art. 1269 C. civ.).
4. **The minor's guardian.** The race's minors paragraph (14–17, §330, §515) adds: «Părintele sau tutorele legal care semnează alături de minor acceptă pentru el riscurile de mai jos, inclusiv pe cel de deces, și renunțarea de mai jos, în limitele permise de lege.» / "…death included, and the waiver below, to the extent the law allows." The group runs are adults only, so they have no such sentence.
5. **Nothing else changes:** the titles, the placeholders, the merge fields, the sections' order, the safety rules and the wild-animals sentence of §556, and the Romanian words of §564 («eveniment montan», «teren accidentat», no «trail»). The race's risk bullet reads «riscurile unei alergări pe…» in place of «riscurile participării la o alergare pe…», to keep it within 200 characters.

**The legal nuance, kept honest.** Under the Romanian Civil Code, liability for harm caused with intent or gross fault cannot be excluded or limited (art. 1355(1)), and liability for harm to the body or health — death included — cannot be excluded or limited by a clause at all, whatever the fault, except as the law provides (art. 1355(3)). A clause that frees the organiser from a death it causes would be void. So the text never says the club does not answer for a death it causes. The race text keeps, word for word, the sentence that nothing in the declaration excludes or limits the organiser's liability for intent, gross fault or harm to bodily integrity or health. The waiver therefore reaches only the claims for harm arising from the inherent risks that the organiser did not cause, and it says so in its own words — «ce decurg exclusiv din riscurile inerente, fără vina organizatorului» / "arising solely from the inherent risks, without the organiser's fault" — so the waiver and the preserved sentence read as one rule, not two. The runner assumes the inherent risks, death included, and waives the claims for harm arising from those risks alone, «în limitele permise de lege». The waiver says in so many words that it does not cover harm caused through the fault of the organiser, its team, its volunteers or its partners, and that it does not remove the organiser's safety duties. The race text's sentence that nothing limits the organiser's liability for intent, gross fault or bodily harm stays word for word. So do the club's duties: the general safety instructions it gives (§556), first aid and being stopped from the race, and the marked course. The heirs are bound only as far as the law allows. They inherit the runner's own claims, but their own claims as relatives after a death (art. 1390–1391) are not the runner's to waive. A guardian's waiver for a minor is likely weaker still: disposing of a minor's rights generally needs the guardianship court (art. 144–146). The words say «în limitele permise de lege» for exactly this reason.

**A Romanian lawyer must read the four declarations before the club approves them** (CLAUDE.md item 16 already says so), and this paragraph first. These notes are the platform's reading of the Civil Code, not legal advice.

**What changes on the sites.** Nothing, until the club acts. No migration and no data change. The texts in effect keep their words and their hashes. `/admin/legal` shows the four declarations as «Șablon nou» (§418). A text changes only when an Administrator starts a new version from the template and approves it. The terms (§5) and the privacy notice are untouched.

Amends §515, §523 and §556. Tests: `tests/unit/legal-documents/inherent-risks-death.test.ts` (new); `group-run-declaration.test.ts` now allows a waiver only in a sentence that carries the law's limit; the race declaration's length ceiling in `merge-fields.test.ts` moved from 9300 to 10300.

Baseline `BR-V2.40-2026-09-27`.

## 569. The page head is compact on a phone: no wordmark, a 24-pixel title, half the room above it (amending §292)

**The owner, 2026-09-29, on a screenshot of `/ro/calendar`:** «Textul ăsta de „Evenimente” e mult prea mare, pe mobil ia prea mult spațiu, la fel și la „Calendar”».

**What was there.** The listing, the calendar and the contact page open with the kit-face wordmark «BRASOV RUNNERS» (§292; `clamp(1.25rem, 4vw, 2rem)`, so 20px on a phone and 32px on a desktop), then the page's H1 at the theme's 2rem (32px) at every width, then the gradient bar under it (§166's `headingRule`, 56 × 3 pixels, 8 pixels under the words), then the intro. The H1 is drawn in the display role (Roboto) on the page's own background: there is no highlight box behind it in the code, so there was none to remove. On a phone the head was the brand twice (the sticky header's lockup, then the wordmark) and a 32-pixel title in front of the first card.

**Decision.**

- *The wordmark is not drawn below `sm`.* `shared/ui/Wordmark` carries `display: { xs: "none", sm: "block" }`: the header's lockup is on the same screen and already says the club's name, one brand per screen. It is hidden by CSS, not left out on the server, because the page is one static HTML for every width served from the CDN (§549), and nothing on the server reads the viewport. From `sm` it is drawn at a flat `1rem`, half its old height.
- *The H1 is one step smaller, in the theme.* `theme.ts`'s `h1` is `1.5rem` (24px, MUI's h5 step) below `sm` and `1.75rem` (28px) from `sm`, where it was 2rem everywhere. In the theme rather than on each page, so every public H1 that takes the theme's size follows at once: the listing, the calendar, an event page, the team page, the contact page, the standing pages (`/pages/[slug]`), the FAQ, the gallery and the members' zone, and the error screens. A page that states its own size keeps it (the participant's link pages at 1.5rem, sign-in, the backoffice shell's title). The H1 stays the page's one `<h1>` and its words do not change.
- *The room is halved on a phone.* The margin above the H1 on the listing, the calendar and the contact page is a new step of the phone density scale (§380), `DENSITY.headGap`, 4 pixels where it was 8; `sm` keeps 8. The gradient bar stays at every width, since it is the title's mark of identity, and its gap under the words is 4 pixels below `sm` (was 8). MUI's `gutterBottom` is `0.35em`, so it shrinks with the title by itself (11.2 → 8.4 pixels).

**The sizes.**

| | 320 | 360 | 768 | 1280 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Wordmark (was) | not drawn (20px) | not drawn (20px) | 16px (30.7px) | 16px (32px) |
| H1 (was) | 24px (32px) | 24px (32px) | 28px (32px) | 28px (32px) |
| Room above the H1 (was) | 4px (8px) | 4px (8px) | 8px | 8px |
| Bar under the words (was) | 4px (8px) | 4px (8px) | 8px | 8px |

**What was rejected.** *A shared page-head component* that every page renders: the heads are not one shape (the calendar's H1 shares a row with its «?» fold, §487, and the listing puts the last-good notice between the wordmark and the title), so one component would take props for each page's difference. The theme's variant and the density scale are already the one place. *Removing the gradient bar* to save its 7 pixels: it is what makes the title read as the page's start (§166). *Hiding the wordmark on the server by user agent*: the page is static and cached for everyone (§549). *Shrinking the H2s too*: not asked; on a phone the H1 and an H2 are now both 24px, and the bar under the H1 tells them apart.

**Tests.** Unit `tests/unit/theme/compact-page-head.test.ts` renders the wordmark and a theme H1 on the server and reads Emotion's CSS: `display:none` with `display:block` from 600px, `font-size:1rem`; the H1 an `<h1>` with its text at 1.5rem and 1.75rem from 600px; `DENSITY.headGap` on the three pages; the bar's phone gap; each page's H1 still reading its own key. `tests/unit/theme/wordmark.test.ts` pins the hide as CSS, never a client check. `tests/unit/theme/density.test.ts` has eight steps and the three new sites. E2e `tests/e2e/compact-page-head.spec.ts`: at 320 × 568 and 360 × 640, on `/ro/evenimente` the wordmark is in the HTML and hidden, the H1 is 24px, and the first card's top is at least 44 pixels above the bottom of the screen (measured on a production build with the sample data: 397.6 of 568 at 320, 374.6 of 640 at 360); on `/ro/calendar` the grid's first week row ends inside the screen (504.1 at both); on a desktop the wordmark is 16px above a 28px title on the listing, the calendar and the contact page.

Baseline `BR-V2.40-2026-09-27`.

## 570. The list for sponsors, behind a notice that says the partners may receive it; the public-list tick names the results; the «Acorduri» block compacted (amending §562 and §143)

**The owner, 2026-09-29 18:40–18:42:** «I need to be able to export the participants list but filter out just the ones who agreed to receive marketing emails so we can share it with our sponsors.» And: «"Vreau să apar pe lista de participanți — opțional" => "Vreau să apar pe lista de participanți & rezultate — opțional" cuz we will also have a results list.» **At 19:03**, of a screenshot of the form's «Acorduri» block: «Also these need to be more compacted!» **At 19:33**, of a screenshot of «Acorduri» on QA after approving the notice: «trebuie să scriem tot „— opțional” la „Vreau să primesc oferte” și la lista de participanți & rezultate trebuie să punem un trofeu ca iconiță pentru consistență; de fapt pentru fiecare bifă ne trebuie și o iconiță la început» and «e destul de importantă partea asta cu acordurile!» **Amends §562** (its notice said «Le trimite numai clubul: partenerii nu primesc adresa ta»; the fold on «Newsletter»), **§143** (the tick's words) and **§550** (the same readers).

**The list for sponsors.** One read, `registrations/sponsor-list.ts#readPromoConsentRows`, is the only query of who said yes to «oferte și beneficii»: a yes (`promo_consent`) on a real registration (`kind` in no other condition, AGENTS.md §12.6) whose address is proved and which still stands — waiting for its declaration, on the waiting list, offered a place, or confirmed (§562's `PROMO_LISTED_STATUSES`, now defined there and re-exported by the newsletter) — never an unproved address, a cancelled, an expired or a test registration. `sponsorList({ eventId? })` narrows it to what a partner may receive — a yes given under a sharing notice (below) **and never a minor**: a child's name goes to no third party's marketing, whatever the guardian ticked, so the participant must be 18 on the day the list is made (`domain/sponsor-share.ts#adultForPartners`, the guardian rule's `isMinorOn` against the download's moment), and a registration without a readable birth date (one the desk entered) is left out, the safe side; §562's club list is not narrowed, since the guardian's address receives the club's own sending — and is read by both doors: «Descarcă lista pentru sponsori» on an event's registrations page (with an event chosen) and the same button inside «Newsletter» → «Participanți care au bifat oferte și beneficii» for every event. One file, `buildSponsorListCsv`: Prenume, Nume, Email, Eveniment, Data acordului (ISO 8601) — never the birth date, the phone, the health note, the declaration's facts or the address holder's other people — through `csvCell`, CRLF, a BOM; named `sponsori-<slug-evenimentului>-<zi>.csv` or `sponsori-toate-<zi>.csv`. The route `GET /api/admin/registrations/sponsor-list?event=<id>` (no event = every event; an id that is not a UUID is 400) asserts `canExportSponsorList` — `canReadRegistrations`: the Organizer, the Administrator, the Superadministrator; Tehnic, the volunteer, the Redactor and a member are refused (403) whatever the link — and writes one audit row `registrations.sponsor_list_exported` with `{ eventId | null, count, recipient | null, registrationIds }` — the ids of the registrations the file held and whom it was given to, never a name or an address. The button is a plain GET form with one optional box, «Cui dai lista (opțional)» (`to`, control characters dropped, whitespace collapsed, at most 120 characters, `sponsorRecipient`), so the club can keep the notice's promise to say which partners received a person's data (art. 15 and 19 GDPR) long after its own copy of the file is deleted: a registration's page in the backoffice reads those rows back as «Dată partenerilor» — when, to whom (or «destinatar nenotat»), by whom (`audit/repository.ts#listPartnerShares`). The count sits beside the button («N persoane», `countForm`), read by `sponsorListSummary` — the same row rule over three columns, no join, and no count while the notice in force does not describe the sharing — with one caption: what the file holds (adults only, consents given under a notice that allows it), to write whom it goes to and to delete the file within 30 days. The main registrations export is untouched: the sponsor list is its own minimal file. §562's club list on «Newsletter» keeps its table and its «Descarcă CSV» in their place, read through the same query and written by the same writer (its CSV has the five columns now), because the club's own sending is covered by every yes, the partners' only by some.

**The gate (AGENTS.md §10.8, the §396/§562 mechanism).** A new merge field `{{promotionalMaterialsShared}}`, filled with the three data a partner receives in words («prenumele, numele și adresa ta de e-mail» / “your first name, last name and email address”, `Registration.promo.sharedData`), read by `describesPromotionalMaterialsShared`. `{{promotionalMaterials}}` stays the box itself, exactly as §562 reads it; the box's words do not change. The button is offered only while the notice in force names the new field in every language (`noticeDescribesPromotionalMaterialsShared`); otherwise it is a disabled button with «Nota de confidențialitate în vigoare nu spune că lista poate fi dată partenerilor.» and the route answers 409 — the page's state is the same rule, not the rule. And the list holds only the registrations whose yes was given under a text that described the sharing: `domain/sponsor-share.ts#sharedWithSponsors` asks **both** the notice the registration recorded (`privacy_notice_version`) **and** the notice in force at `promo_consent_at` (a later yes from the person's own page is given under the notice of that moment, §562) to be in the exact set of approved, not withdrawn versions that name the field in every language (`findSponsorShareVersions` — a set, not §421's lower bound, so a later version that drops the marker never lets its registrants through). A yes given under §562's «partenerii nu primesc adresa ta» never reaches a partner, even once a sharing notice is in force; a person who registered under it and said yes later under the new one is left out too, the safe side. No migration: the columns exist.

**The notice template** (both languages; the twelve sections kept; the four placeholders untouched; no text in effect changes — production keeps its approved notice until the club approves one from the template). Section 5: §562's «Le trimite numai clubul: partenerii nu primesc adresa ta…» is gone, and a paragraph «Lista pentru parteneri:» says the club may give its partners — the club's sponsors and the partners of its events, named as a category — `{{promotionalMaterialsShared}}`, so they send their own offers; nothing else; never sold; the consent covers the club's messages and the partners'; a partner uses the data as a separate controller under its own notice and may be asked directly to stop; the list is given only with consents given under a version that says so; a withdrawal stops every later sharing and the club asks the partners that hold the data to stop writing and delete it; art. 6(1)(a) GDPR and art. 12 of Law 506/2004; on request the club says which partners received the data (art. 15, 19); the complaint to ANSPDCP (section 9). The paragraph also says «Datele unui minor nu le dăm niciodată unui partener: lista îi cuprinde doar pe participanții care au împlinit 18 ani în ziua în care e făcută.» and, after the art. 15/19 promise, «pentru fiecare listă, clubul păstrează cui a dat-o și ce înscrieri a cuprins.» Section 6: «Nu le vindem și nu le dăm nimănui altcuiva, cu o singură excepție…» names the partners and the field. Section 7: «Lista dată partenerilor: copia clubului, ștearsă în cel mult 30 de zile de la descărcare; la partener, cât spune nota lui de informare, iar când îți retragi acordul îi cerem să îți șteargă datele; cui am dat-o și ce înscrieri a cuprins rămân în jurnalul echipei, fără fișier.» The template's header says what changed; `/admin/legal` sees the moved template by its hash (§532) and says «Nota în vigoare nu spune încă că lista pentru sponsori…» (`legal.sponsorMissing`); the legend lists the field; `/admin/tasks` carries the open, never blocking row `sponsorNotice` with the steps, done by itself the day such a notice takes effect.

**What the person reads.** On the manage page and «Înscrierile mele», a registration whose yes may reach a partner reads «La această înscriere primești oferte și beneficii de la club și de la partenerii săi. Clubul le poate da partenerilor prenumele, numele și adresa ta, ca să îți scrie ei.» (`Registrations.promo.yesShared`); every other yes keeps §562's sentence, still true for it — and a minor's row always does. **Where the yes is given** (art. 7(2) and 13 GDPR: the information at the point of consent), while the notice in force names the new field (`cachedPromotionalMaterialsShared`, the same reading in every language), the box's caption adds «Clubul le poate da partenerilor prenumele, numele și adresa ta.» (`Registration.promo.shared`) on the form and on the declaration page, and the manage page says «Dacă îl dai, clubul le poate da partenerilor prenumele, numele și adresa ta.» (`Registrations.promo.optInShared`) beside its «Vreau» button; the box's own words do not change.

**The tick's words (amending §143).** «Vreau să apar pe lista de participanți & rezultate — opțional» / “I want to appear on the participants & results list — optional”, the ampersand as the owner wrote it, wherever the tick is named: the form, the manage page's and «Înscrierile mele»'s switch («Vreau / Nu vreau să apar pe lista de participanți & rezultate»), the confirmation email's link, the staff form («Persoana vrea să apară pe lista de participanți & rezultate»), the event list's note and the editor's help, AGENTS.md and BUSINESS.md. The notice's section 4 quotes the new words and its results sentence names one disclosure behind one tick: «Rezultate cu nume nu publicăm încă. Când le vom publica, vor apărea în ele doar cei care au bifat aceeași „vreau să apar pe lista de participanți & rezultate” — o singură bifă pentru listă și pentru rezultate, pe care o retragi la fel — iar această notă va spune dinainte ce arată rezultatele.» — replacing «te vom întreba separat», which contradicted the tick's new words. No FAQ template names the tick; the guide does not quote it.

**«Acorduri», compacted.** `shared/ui/consent-density.ts#CONSENT_DENSITY`, read by `CheckboxField`'s `dense`, by `ReadAndAgree` and by the density test: MUI's small box (20 px) with `CHECKBOX_TAP_TARGET`'s 12 px around it — 44 by 44, still the thumb's target (BR-REQ-041-01 criterion 6), where the medium box was 48; the label in `body2`, top-aligned, 12 px above and below; the block its own `Stack` with no gap. A row is `max(44, 24 + 20 × lines)` px, where it was `max(48, 24 × lines) + 16`: five one-line rows are 220 px where they were 304, and every line of the block is 20 px where it was 24. Each helper — the list's states, the socials', the offers' «Opțional…» — is a caption directly under its label, 4 px below the words, and the box's `aria-describedby`. The race's conditions are a regular-height button (44 px, `TAP_TARGET`) with the book glyph, as wide as its words, the small box inside it, and its hint a caption; the gate is unchanged — unread, a press on the box opens the text and does not tick it (§195, §422). No word the legal reviews fixed (§425, §556) changed; the terms sentence stays one flow, its version and clauses inline. Measured in the browser on the seeded race, a glyph on every box (the plain conditions box, the terms, the fitness and privacy boxes, the offers box and its caption): the block is 532 px tall at 320 px and 252 px on a desktop; the e2e spec holds it under 580 and 280 px, every box still 44 by 44.

**Round 2: a glyph on every box, and « — opțional» on every optional one** (the owner, 19:33). One label layout for every box of the block, `CONSENT_DENSITY.labelSx` through `CheckboxField`'s `dense`: the glyph — a 20-pixel `text.secondary` icon, the size of the site's row glyphs (§318, §521) — in its own column at the label's left edge, on its first line, 6 px before the words; a wrapped line starts under the words, never under the glyph, and each caption starts under the words too (59 px, where it was 33). One meaning, one glyph: the race's conditions the book (`MenuBook`, as on its button), the terms a document (`Description`), «Declar pe propria răspundere că sunt apt medical…» the medical case the form's health fold already wears (`MedicalServices`), «Am citit nota de confidențialitate» the shield (`Shield`), «Vreau să apar pe lista de participanți & rezultate» the **trophy** (`EmojiEvents`, the owner's word), the socials the share glyph of their fold (`Share`), «oferte și beneficii» the megaphone (`Campaign`). Each glyph is made by the Server Component as the label's first child and `aria-hidden` — never an element passed as a prop — so a box's accessible name is its words. The glyph is no longer an inline icon nudged by hand (`verticalAlign: -0.2em`, `mr`), which is what drew the megaphone apart from its words; nothing stands between a glyph and its words now. The three optional boxes end « — opțional» / “ — optional” through one prop (`optional`, `Registration.optionalSuffix`), in the label's own flow. **The offers box keeps the owner's full stop**: «Vreau să primesc oferte și beneficii de la Brașov Runners și partenerii săi. — opțional» — the sentence is what the notice quotes through `{{promotionalMaterials}}` and what the club may already have approved, so its words do not move; and its helper loses the «Opțional.» that §562 put at its head, which the label now says: «Poți renunța oricând din pagina înscrierii tale.» The required mark is drawn by the dense label itself, after the last word (the input is still `required`, through its own slot): MUI's own mark wrapped the label in a `<div>` where an inline label lost its padding and a flowing mark fell to a line of its own. The declaration page's copies — «Am citit și accept declarația de mai sus…» (the quill, `HistoryEdu`) and the offers box of the family's signing steps — are drawn the same way, dense, the offers box with « — opțional» and its caption under it. Tests: every box in the block starts with its glyph, one per meaning; the three optional ones end with the word through the prop and the four required ones never; a render of the dense label reads glyph, words, « — opțional», and a required one carries one mark after its last word and a required input; the e2e spec checks a visible glyph in every label of the block and the offers label's text.

**Refused.** Adding the sponsor columns to the registrations export (a file that leaves to a third party must hold the minimum, art. 5(1)(c)). A lower-bound version gate (§421's documented hole). Giving a partner a yes given under §562's text, even "only the names". Renaming `{{promotionalMaterials}}` or changing the box's words (texts the club may already have approved). A separate consent box for the sharing: the owner asked for one list of those who agreed, and the notice now says the one box covers both; the box's own sentence already names «partenerii săi». Leaving whom a file went to outside the application (the first draft's choice): the notice promises to say which partners received a person's data, and the club's copy of the file is deleted within 30 days — only the audit row can keep that promise, so it holds the registrations' ids and the recipient the download named, never a name or an address. A partner's list with a minor in it, even with the guardian's yes. Dropping the offers sentence's full stop so the dash reads better: the box's words are the notice's quoted text. A glyph table looked up by name for the boxes: a public page would ship every glyph in it (§318); each page imports its one icon file per box.

Baseline `BR-V2.42-2026-09-27`.

## 571. «Ordinea meniului»: one order for every entry of the site menu (amending §537)

**The owner, 2026-09-29, from a screenshot of «Pagini» → «Paginile clubului»:** «la paginile clubului, vreau să pot seta ordinea la orice pagină, inclusiv cea de evenimente, calendar, contact». Until now only the custom pages carried an order (the «Ordinea» column and its ↑ / ↓, §537), the platform's own sections had the places `SECTIONS` in `SiteNav` gave them (§537, after §251), and a rule stood between the two groups.

**Decision: one order for every entry the menu can carry.** Each entry has a stable key — `events`, `calendar`, `contact`, `gallery`, `team`, `faq`, `members`, and `page:<id>` for a custom page (its id, never its address, which differs per language). «Galerie» is in the list too: it is an entry of the same menu, and leaving it out would have left one entry with a place nobody can change. The club's order is one list of those keys, first to last, stored as one `platform_settings` row, `menuOrder` — no migration, the table takes any key (§100). The save is audited (`menu_order.changed`, from and to).

**The merge rule** (`src/modules/content/menu/order.ts`, the one function the header, the footer and the backoffice card all call): the stored list rules; an entry it does not name — a fresh site with no list, a page written after the last save, a section a later release adds — falls to the end in today's default order (the sections as §537 lists them, then the custom pages); a key for something that no longer exists (a deleted page) is dropped. So a fresh site and a new page need no setting up, and a new page appears last until it is moved.

**One truth with the old «Ordinea» column.** The stored list is the order. The `nav_order` column stays only as the fallback order of the pages the list does not name yet, which is the order the site showed before this change — so the first view of the card is today's menu, and the first «Salvează ordinea» stores the whole list, after which the list rules. Nothing is copied by a migration. The page editor's «Ordinea în meniu» box is gone (a posted `navOrder` is ignored), the list's ↑ / ↓ on each custom page and `movePageInNav` are gone, and a new page is written with `nav_order` one past the largest, so a page the list does not name is last rather than first. Dropping the column would be a contract migration of its own; nothing needs it now. The published pages are read in `nav_order`, then the date they were written — no longer the title after the number, which sorted two equal numbers differently in each language.

**The screen.** On «Pagini» → «Paginile clubului», between the standard pages and the custom ones, a fold «Ordinea meniului» (its glyph a reorder mark, §521) lists every entry in the current order, each with its number, its glyph and its name, a custom page marked «pagină personalizată». «Sus» and «Jos», each with its arrow and named with the entry for a screen reader, move one place; the focus stays on the pressed button (its twin at an end), a polite status says the new place, and a line says the order is not saved yet. One «Salvează ordinea» posts the whole list behind the §384 question («Schimbi ordinea meniului?»); a refused save keeps the order as moved (§315). The buttons are the way to reorder — a keyboard and a thumb reach them alike — so there is no drag, and no dependency. An entry the menu leaves out today (a draft standard page, «Echipa» with no card on the site, an unpublished custom page, «Contact» with nowhere to write, «Galerie» with no published album) keeps its place, greyed, «nu apare încă»: the card asks the header's own questions (`src/modules/content/menu/on-site.ts`, moved there from `SiteHeader`), so it never disagrees with the site. The custom pages' table shows each page's place in the whole menu («Locul în meniu») in the same order.

**Who.** A club setting, the Administrator's (§450): `saveMenuOrderAction` asks `canManageClubSettings` at the door and `saveMenuOrder` asserts it again; an Organizer or a Redactor sees the list without its buttons and a line saying the Administrator sets it (BR-REQ-060-01). A post that is not a list of keys is refused as a forged one.

**The readers.** The header's row and its ☰ menu sort their entries by the stored order — the members' entry still only while «Beneficiile membrilor» is on the site (§524), each other conditional entry by its own rule, the active entry as before — and the rule between the platform's sections and the club's pages is gone: the menu is one list. §537's order (criterion 158 of BR-REQ-041-01) is now the default the merge rule falls back to, not the only order. The footer's fold carries two of the menu's entries, «Întrebări frecvente» and «Contact»: «Întrebări frecvente» stays on the first line after the terms and «Înscrierile mele» while the order puts it first, and follows the contact line when the club puts it after «Contact»; the rest of the fold is not the menu and keeps its place. The order is read through the public cache under `settings` with the last good copy (§333, §447), so a database that cannot answer is today's default order, never a page that fails over its menu; a save expires `settings`, so every public page shows the new order from the next view (§549).

Baseline `BR-V2.42-2026-09-27`.

## 572. The members' texts translate in one press, and their two languages are tabs «RO» | «EN»

**The owner, 2026-09-29 20:50, with a screenshot of «Pagini» → «Membri» → «Scrie zona membrilor»:** «În zona de membri, butonul de traducere nu merge, și partea bilingvă trebuie să fie per tabs.» The Romanian editor held «Salutare colegii!», the English one was empty, the save was refused naming «Zona membrilor (engleză)» (§352), and «Copiază și tradu tot: RO → EN» (§482) answered «Nu e nimic de tradus: scrie întâi textele în română.»

**Why the press found nothing.** It never read a stale value: it reads every box by name at the moment it is pressed, a rich text through the hidden box its editor keeps in step (§464). But it fills only the English boxes on its allowlist (`translate/domain/fields.ts`, §482), and «Membri»'s two texts (§524) post `benefitsRoBody` / `benefitsEnBody` and `zoneRoBody` / `zoneEnBody`, names added after the list was written and never put on it. With no English box it was allowed to fill, the press said there was nothing to translate. Both names are on the list now, as rich texts with their Romanian twin found by the `…RoBody` / `…EnBody` spelling «Echipa» already uses. The server checks names against the same list, so it now accepts them as well. The translation arrives in the English editor as content, through the same fill event the other editors use.

**Decision: tabs «RO» | «EN» in one card.** The two editors of each members' text sit in one `LocaleTabPanels` strip inside its fold, the same strip the event editor, the standing pages, the album form and «Întrebări frecvente» already use (§350), with one editor on screen at a time. The other language's editor stays mounted and hidden, so the save still posts both languages (§352). The tabs read «RO» and «EN». The English one says «gol» («empty») while its editor is empty, re-read as the person types (§350). The strip learnt to watch names spelt `zone{Locale}Body` as well as `translations.<locale>.<field>`. «Copiază și tradu tot» stays above the tabs, visible whichever tab is on top (§482). A refusal naming the English box brings the English tab forward with the box it names, through the reveal every strip already answers (§47, §350).

**After a translate press.** Every strip whose English panel holds a box the press filled, in the form that pressed, brings the English tab forward. This works for «Copiază și tradu tot» and for a card's own «Tradu cardul» (§514), because the press announces the names it filled and each strip checks its own English panel. It announces only the boxes it actually filled: an answer for a name the form has no box for moves no tab. A translation hidden behind the Romanian tab is one nobody reads before «Salvează». The English tab then also says «tradus — verifică» («translated — check it») until the person types, pastes or deletes there (`beforeinput`, which a fill does not fire). This applies to every strip: the word is the strip's own, `Translate.tabTranslated` in both catalogues, so the event editor, a standing page, an album, the FAQ and the newsletter wear the same mark as «Membri» with no word passed. A strip may still pass its own (`translatedMark`).

**The language glyph on every tab.** Each language tab, on every strip, carries the flag the header's language switcher shows beside the language's name or code (Romania for Romanian, the United Kingdom for English). It is never the label: the image is `alt=""` and the tab's name stays the words (§521, the owner's glyph rule). The map moved from `LocaleSwitcher` to `Flag.tsx` (`LANGUAGE_FLAG`) so both read one list. Below `sm` the tabs are a little narrower to make room for it. The empty mark is one short word so the row fits: at 320 px, with both languages empty, «RO · gol» | «EN · gol» and their flags sit on one row without scrolling. A longer mark (the event editor's «2 obligatorii lipsă», or «tradus — verifică» beside a code) may still scroll the row sideways, the strip's own behaviour, rather than wrap.

**One fold across the tabs.** A rich text's fold inside a strip is twinned with its other-language fold (§363). The twin key now also removes the language from the `…RoBody` / `…EnBody` spelling (`zone*Body`), so the members' text opened under «RO» is also open under «EN». The same now holds for «Echipa»'s and the FAQ's rich texts.

**Screens that change:** «Membri» (both texts: tabs, marks, the press). Every strip gets the flags and the English tab after a press. **Not changed:** «Echipa»'s cards, which already had their own strips, and the newsletter composer. No dependency and no migration.

Baseline `BR-V2.43-2026-09-27`.

## 573. The group run's signing page types its birth date day first, as the registration form does

**Context.** §561 (BR-V2.35) replaced the browser's own `type="date"` box on the registration form and the desk with `BirthDateField`: typed day first, «11.05.1990», whatever language the browser speaks, the date in words with the age on the event's day as the box's helper, the minimum age refused live under it, and the server reading the typed text with `normalizeTypedDate`. The public group-run signing page (§393), which asks a birth date only when the run's minimum age is above eighteen (§440, §515), still drew the native date box — so an English phone showed it month first, the defect §561 fixed everywhere else.

**Decision.** The signing page draws the same `BirthDateField` (id and name `birthDate`, so the refusal summary's link and the sealed draft keep working): the same `DD.MM.YYYY` / `ZZ.LL.AAAA` placeholder and unreadable-date words from the `Registration` catalogue, the same echo template, the oldest bound a hundred and twenty years back as on the registration form, the youngest the run's own (`latestBirthDateFor` on the run's day, today at the latest). At rest the helper is the page's own «Pentru vârsta minimă a alergării…» line with the date in words under it; a whole date under the run's minimum turns the box red and puts the page's «Vârsta minimă pentru această alergare este {age}…» sentence first, and the server's refusal reads the same until the box is typed in again. The action reads the box with `normalizeTypedDate`, so the service still gets `YYYY-MM-DD` — or what was typed, trimmed, for `birthDateRefusal` to name — and a browser without JavaScript posts what it typed and is read the same. No new words: every string the box needs was already in both catalogues.

**Not done.** No MUI picker (it stays off public pages, `pickers-backoffice-only.test.ts`), and no change to what the service refuses or stores: the date is still counted against the run's minimum and dropped (§440).

Baseline `BR-V2.43-2026-09-27`.

## 574. The calendar's period is in the address's path: the arrows, the selects and the swipe show the month again

**The owner, 2026-09-29 22:45**, with a screenshot of `/ro/calendar`'s controls («Luna: Septembrie», «Anul: 2026», «‹ Azi ›», «Lună | An», «Calendar | Listă»): «nu pot schimba luna din săgeți (deși se schimbă în query params) dar nu văd evenimentele din octombrie; de asemenea s-a stricat și la swipe pe telefon».

**The cause, measured.** Of the three suspects the brief named, it was none as stated and closest to the first: the page was right, the router never asked it.

- *Not the server.* On production, `curl /ro/calendar` answered the static page (`X-Vercel-Cache: HIT`, `X-Matched-Path: /[locale]/calendar`, «septembrie 2026») and `curl /ro/calendar?month=2026-10` the live twin (`X-Matched-Path: /[locale]/live/calendar`, `private, no-store`, «octombrie 2026», October's events in the HTML). The same on a local `yarn build && yarn start`. A direct link to October showed October.
- *Not the island.* Nothing on the client reads the query; the month is server HTML, and a soft navigation replaces it only if the router fetches it.
- *Not BR-V2.40 or the footer hotfix.* `git log -8 --stat -- 'src/app/[locale]/calendar'`: the compact head (2dcaa109) and the release commit changed a few `sx` lines. The break came with §549 (BR-V2.24, b52cae56), which made the bare calendar static and every other month a query the proxy rewrites to the twin.
- *The router answered from a prefetch.* A headless Chromium on production, from `/ro/evenimente`: the header's «Calendar» link prefetched `/ro/calendar` (`Next-Router-Segment-Prefetch: /_tree`), the click showed September, and › put `?month=2026-10` in the address, **sent no request**, and left September on screen; a second › went to `?month=2026-10` again, because the arrows on screen were still September's. From a direct load the first › worked, and the second showed September under `?month=2026-11`, once the header link's prefetch had arrived. Vercel answers that segment prefetch with the page's whole flight data (94 412 bytes, `X-Matched-Path: /[locale]/calendar.rsc`, `X-Nextjs-Prerender: 1`); `next start` answers it with the tree alone, which is why no local run and no end-to-end test ever saw it. Answering the prefetch the way Vercel does (a Playwright route) reproduced the owner's screen on a local build exactly; aborting the prefetch of the bare page made every arrow work. Next 16.3.4 says why in its own client: a static prefetch "never include[s] search params, so [it] can be reused across all possible search param values" (`segment-cache/vary-path.js`), and it "optimistically assume[s] that rewrites for the requested pathname do not vary on the search string" (`segment-cache/cache.js`). A static page cannot read its query, so to the router its copy answers every query; the proxy's rewrite by `?month=` is exactly what that assumption forbids.
- *The swipe* pushes the arrows' own addresses (§475), so it broke with them: the address changed out of sight and the month stayed.

**Decision.** A period lives in the path, never in the query:

- `/ro/calendar` is this month as a grid; `/ro/calendar/2026-10` October; `/ro/calendar/2026-10/list` October as a list; `/ro/calendar/2026` the year (a year has no layout). The same words in both languages, like `/calendar`. One route, `app/[locale]/calendar/[...period]/page.tsx`, renders the bare page's component with the segments; `events/domain/calendar-path.ts` reads and builds them (pure, tested). A malformed period, a year with a layout, a third segment or a period more than two years away is a 404 — the bound the selects and the old `?month=` had.
- Every control builds its address with `calendarAddress`: the arrows and so the swipe (`calendarStepHrefs`), «Azi», the two selects, «Lună», «An», «Calendar», «Listă» and the year's month headings. The bare path is used only for this month as a grid with nothing filtered; everything else spells its period, this month included.
- The filters stay in the query, on the period's own path: `/ro/calendar/2026-10?type=RACE` is the period's live twin (`live/calendar/[...period]/page.tsx`). The filter form's action and its chips always spell the period, even for this month, so no filtered address is a query on the bare path — the one address the header prefetches. Measured on a local build with Vercel's prefetch answer: a filter, › with it, clearing it and «Azi» all showed the period and the filter they named.
- The old addresses are answered by the proxy before anything renders: `?month=`, `?year=` and `?view=list` on the bare calendar are redirected to the same period's path, every other key kept and Next's `_rsc` dropped (`i18n/calendar-redirect.ts`), with the old readings (`?year=` wins, a bad or distant month is this month). Only a GET or a HEAD; a POST keeps its address. A filter alone on the bare path is still the bare page's twin.
- The redirect is permanent only where the address alone fixes its target. A valid `?month=2026-10` or `?year=2027` is a 308 to that period's spelled path — this month's too (`?month=2026-09` → `/ro/calendar/2026-09`, never the bare page, whose meaning moves with the clock). `?view=list` alone, or a month that is malformed or too far away, means "this month": its target changes on the first of the next month, and a browser keeps a permanent redirect with no cache header of its own, so a bookmark would stay on the month it first resolved to. Those answer a 307 with `Cache-Control: private, no-store` (`legacyCalendarAddress` returns the address and whether it is `fixed`). Refused: a 307 with a short public `max-age` for every old address — the named month's target never changes, and a permanent redirect is what tells a search engine the old address is gone.
- Static like the bare page (§549): `revalidate` the day's ceiling, no params at build, expired by the events' writes, held to Brașov's midnight. `PREFETCHED_PATHNAMES` names `/calendar/[...period]`, so the proxy gives its answer the browser's header off Vercel; the calendar's own links still never prefetch (a month nobody opened today is a render). Its canonical is the bare calendar (§342), and robots.txt disallows `/ro/calendar/` and `/en/calendar/`, so a crawler does not walk five years of months and wake the database.
