So §372's pinned copy is superseded and §365's rule returns at every width.

**The decision.** One `BuildBadge` render per page, the last line of the fold's panel, at every width and in every environment; on screen only once the fold is open. The chip, its words, the 44-pixel box and the staff entrance (§34: double-click, long press or Enter; a single click or tap does nothing) are unchanged; nothing else on the bar moves. The pinned `footer-build-badge-pinned` box is deleted and the fold's copy loses its `md: none`; the test id `footer-build-badge-panel` stays. With one copy left, `BuildBadge` loses its `phoneTarget` prop: the fold's box (24-px line plus 20-px reach on a phone, 44 from `sm`) is its only shape.

**What stays measured.** The phone panel's heights of §480 (the stamp's 24-px line with its 20-px reach above) do not change; the bar's row is untouched.

**Tests.** `site-footer.test.ts`: the stamp is rendered once, inside `<details>` after its `<summary>`, `app-ver` once, and `footer-build-badge-pinned` nowhere in the markup; the chip assertions iterate the panel only. `build-badge.spec.ts`: the «not on screen until the fold is opened» test runs on both projects; one desktop test covers hidden-when-closed, single click does nothing, double-click and Enter open sign-in; the chip test covers click and double-click on both projects, so the mobile single-tap and double-click/Enter tests, now repeats, are gone, and the phone's long-press test stays with its true skip reason. `footer.spec.ts`: the closed bar shows no stamp at any width, and a 1280-px test checks it hidden, then visible inside the footer and not wider than the screen once the fold opens. Playwright was not run in this round, by the owner's rule that E2E stays in CI.

*Rejected:* hiding the pinned chip with opacity or on hover (still a layout item and still read by assistive technology, and a hover is not a thumb); keeping the pin only above some wider breakpoint (the owner's screenshot is a wide desktop); showing the stamp only to signed-in staff (the stamp is the door to signing in).

Baseline `BR-V2.55-2026-10-01`.

## 609. The shared card is a brand card, drawn from a design object the club will be able to change

**The owner, 2026-10-01:** «poza descărcată pentru Instagram trebuie să fie un pic mai frumoasă, și pe viitor configurabilă» — the picture downloaded for Instagram should be a little prettier, and configurable later.

**What was there.** Since §90 every event has a card drawn on the server from its own facts: the 1200×630 picture Facebook, WhatsApp and every link preview show, and the same card as a square for Instagram, which takes no link. §90 chose facts over a photograph on purpose — an event has no cover picture, and a card that says when and where is what a runner wants from a share. §140 made the square a button called «Instagram», and §299 made that button hand the picture to the phone's own share sheet where it can. The card itself had not changed since §90: a flat diagonal blue, the club's name in spaced capitals behind a small orange bar, a translucent pill with the event's type, the title, «Sâmbătă, 21 nov. 2026 · 10:00» on one line, the place, the distance and the climb with orange dots between them, and the site's address. Correct, and plain: no logo, and nothing told the eye where to look first except the size of the title.

**What changes, in what a person sees** (`events/share-image.tsx`):

- *The club's own logo* at the top left — the white lockup, mountains and «BRASOV RUNNERS», the same file the race numbers carry — instead of the name typed out, 150 pixels tall on the square and 100 on the wide card: the square is seen at about 400 pixels wide on a phone, where a 100-pixel lockup left its wordmark about 14 pixels high and the brand on Instagram is the point of the picture. The type pill is centred on the logo's height. The name is therefore the artwork's letters: `CLUB_NAME` is no longer typed onto the card, and a card with the logo switched off carries no name, only the address in the band (the criteria that read the club's name from `CLUB_NAME`, BR-REQ-052-02 11 and BR-REQ-053-01 15 (§357, §369), are both amended to say so).
- *A background with depth*: the same blue diagonal, a soft light at the top right, and one large circle of the kit's orange, faint, half off the bottom-right corner. Nothing busier: no pattern, no stripes, no stock photograph.
- *A hierarchy*: the type pill is a quiet tint of the words' colour with a thin line round it, so that the one solid orange pill on the card is the cancelled one's; the title is larger, at most three lines, under it a short orange rule; then the date with **the time as the headline** — the day in regular weight and the hour large and bold beside it, an orange dot between; the meeting point with a pin; the distance and the climb as two rounded chips, each with a small drawing (a route, a mountain).
- *A white band at the foot* with the site's address in the club's blue and the club's mountains at its right — the site's address is what turns a saved picture back into a visit.
- *Optional, and off by default*: a short line in the club's handwriting face under the title (a tagline), and a photograph behind everything under a blue veil that keeps the words legible — on any photograph, a near-white one included: the veil holds 0.72 of the base colour over the top quarter, behind the logo and the pill (white reads there at about 5:1 over pure white), eases to 0.6 at the middle, where the title is large and the photograph shows most, and deepens to 0.88 at the foot behind the facts; over a photograph the radial light is left off and the type pill is a shade of the blue rather than a tint of white, both of which would lighten the corner the pill sits in. At a quarter of the base, as first written, the white logo and pill over a pale photograph read at about 1.5:1.

A cancelled event keeps what it had on the old card — always, even with the type switched off, because a cancellation is a fact the card must state, not a label the club may hide — the pill that is solid orange with the word «Anulat» (dark letters on the kit's orange, white on a dark accent the club may choose later) while a scheduled event's pill is only a tint — the colour says it before the word is read, and a test holds the two apart; a date, a time or a place not yet announced says so in the same words as before (§328, §533), and only an announced time becomes the headline.

**The design object, and why it exists before anything stores it** (`events/share-card-design.ts`). «Pe viitor configurabilă» is a promise about later, and the cheapest way to keep it is to make the drawing take every decision from one place now. `ShareCardDesign` holds them: the look (`brand` — the blue, the default; `ink` — near-black with a blue glow; `paper` — the page's off-white with dark words and a blue band), the accent colour (the kit's orange), whether the logo, the type, the place, the route and the address are drawn, the tagline (at most 60 characters) and the background picture (an absolute `https:` address, or none). `readShareCardDesign` reads anything — an old row, a typo, garbage — as a design, field by field, and never throws: a card that fails to draw is worse than a plain card, the reasoning of the race number's design (§249). Every element that can be switched off leaves no gap behind it. Today nothing stores the object and every caller passes the platform's defaults. **The next step, named and not built:** a `share_card_design` JSON column on `events`, read through `readShareCardDesign`, and a box in the event editor beside the race number's — exactly the pair `bib_design` is (§249) — when the club asks for it. A picture address is `https:` only and nothing narrower for now; limiting it to the pictures this site stored, as the bibs do, belongs with that box and is recommended there — today nothing stores an address at all. `eventShareImage` runs whatever design it is handed through `readShareCardDesign` before drawing, so a caller that one day hands it a stored design cannot skip those rules, and the renderer itself fetches `https:` only and takes no `data:` address.

**What Satori decided.** `next/og` draws through Satori, which lays out with flexbox only, wants every element with children set to `display: flex`, and draws every line of text it is given — it never shrinks a text to fit, so a title, a place or a tagline that runs long pushes what is under it, the band included, off the card's foot. The review measured exactly that on the wide card: a three-line title with a place that wrapped to a second line left a 66-pixel band of 80, and a tagline beside a long title 69. So the card is laid out before it is drawn (`events/share-card-layout.ts`, pure). Each letter's width is Roboto's own advance, measured once from the bundled files and kept as a table (the wider of the regular and the bold, so neither weight is ever narrower than it says); `lineCount` wraps a text at its spaces the way Satori does, line by line (`textWrap: balance` evens the lines without adding one); `titleRoom` adds up, from the same numbers the drawing uses, the height of everything on the card but the title — the paddings, the band, the logo's row, the rule and the tagline, the date line, the place, the chips (and whether they wrap to a second row) — each only when it is drawn; and `shareTitleSize` picks the largest size whose lines, three at most, fit what is left. On the square that is about 375 pixels with the platform's card, so a title is drawn at 92 pixels up to about sixty characters and a sentence-case title of 85, 100 and 110 characters at 64, 56 and 50 — never smaller than the date line beside it, which it was at 44 when the room was guessed at 300; an all-capitals title of 110 goes to 40 to stay on three lines. On the wide card the same arithmetic within its 630 pixels: two lines from about 50 pixels up, and a tagline beside the rule takes its line from the title's room, so the title steps down rather than the band. The place is cut by length, at a word, with «…» (`clampPlace`, sixty characters), and shorter still while it is wider than its line beside the pin — the square's larger letters hold fewer — and drawn `nowrap` with an ellipsis as the last guard; the title is cut past 110 characters the same way (`clampTitle`). Should the arithmetic ever be wrong, the facts' column clips what overflows rather than move the band. The logo and the mountains are handed over as data, read once per process (and named in `outputFileTracingIncludes` for the two routes, so the build ships them); a read that fails is not remembered, so one transient error at a cold start does not draw every card of that instance without the club's identity — the next card reads again, and the handwriting face the same. When it cannot be read, the tagline is drawn in Roboto and the layout budgets its lines in Roboto's wider letters, so the title steps down rather than the band moving. A tagline is balanced like the title, so a sentence on the square does not end on an orphaned word. A background picture is fetched on each render, behind the route's hour-long cache, at an `https:` address only, without following a redirect, with a five-second deadline and a four-megabyte ceiling checked on the announced length first and again while the body is read, and anything that fails draws the card without it, the unread body of a refused answer cancelled. The chips keep the long words, «circa 10 km» and «350 m diferență de nivel» (§585, §598), not the pill's «≈ 10 km»: the bundled Roboto has no «≈», a missing letter makes Satori download a font from Google in the middle of drawing, and re-subsetting the font for one sign is not worth what it would add to every card. The handwriting face (Caveat, already in the repository for the signed declaration) is loaded only for a card that has a tagline (and if the file cannot be read the tagline is drawn in Roboto), because Satori parses every font it is handed and the file is six times Roboto's.

The site's own card (`[locale]/opengraph-image.tsx`) shares no code with the event's and is unchanged.

**Tests.** `tests/unit/events/share-card-design.test.ts` — the defaults, garbage read as the defaults, a bad accent read as the orange, a `javascript:`, `http:` or `data:` picture read as none, each palette accepted, the tagline cut at its ceiling, the colours of each palette and of a picture (no light, the pill a shade of the base), the veil's three stops giving white 4.5:1 at the top and the foot and 3:1 at the middle over pure white, the pill letters on a light and a dark accent, the title's and the place's clamps. `tests/unit/events/share-card-layout.test.ts` — the measured widths, the wrap, the chips' rows, the title's size never growing with its length, a sentence-case title of 85 to 110 characters at 50 pixels or more on the square, and, for the review's cases on both shapes (a 110-character title with a 93-character place, a long title with a sixty-character tagline, both at once, the date held back, nothing but the facts), the title's lines at its size within three and within the room; the place cut at a word to what its line holds. `tests/unit/events/share-image.test.ts` — the real `next/og` drawing both shapes to a PNG whose header says 1080×1080 and 1200×630, with every element switched off, for a cancelled event and for a date and place to be announced, over a background picture, in the ink and paper looks and with a tagline; the PNG's own pixels read back through `sharp` for the review's cases and an all-capitals one, on both shapes: the paper band fills exactly its last 104 rows on the square and 80 on the wide card, and the logo stands where the plain card has it (an overflow, clipped, would push it up — the test fails when the title is not sized by its room); a near-white photograph, served like every picture through a stub of `fetch` at an `https:` address, leaves 4.5:1 for white behind the wordmark and the pill; a `data:` address is drawn as the plain card without a request, and so is a picture announcing more than four megabytes. The existing tests of the picture's words (§328, §349) pass unchanged.

*Rejected:* a photograph picked automatically from the event's description — which picture represents an event is the organizer's choice, and it is what the future setting is for. A third shape for stories (1080×1920) — not asked; the design object can carry a shape later. Fetching a picture from the gallery at render time — a network call inside a cached image route, and the club has not chosen a picture to fetch. Any new font or library — the card uses the Roboto and the Caveat already in the repository and `next/og`, already installed.

Baseline `BR-V2.55-2026-10-01`.

## 610. «Cât costă» says each service's cost per month and per year, and Vercel's plan is a setting

**The owner, 2026-10-01**, with two screenshots of «Setări» → «Costuri»: «la costuri vreau să văd defalcat pe lună și per serviciu!» and «aici nu e clar ca e per an...». The first screenshot was the header of «Cât costă»: «Astăzi clubul plătește 306.29 USD + TVA pe an.», with «Din care baza de date e o estimare la ritmul lunii (× 12), nu o factură.» under it. The second was the Mailgun row's «Cost azi»: a bare «180 USD + TVA».

**Why a bare yearly figure misleads.** The club's treasurer pays monthly invoices — Mailgun's month, Neon's month, and since 2026-09-30 Vercel Pro's — and one yearly invoice, the domain's. A yearly figure with no period beside it reads as a price, and «180 USD + TVA» is no invoice anybody will ever receive: it was Mailgun's 15 a month multiplied by twelve inside `platform-plans.ts` and printed with nothing to say so. The yearly sentence summed that, a year of Neon's estimate and the domain's fee into one number with the word «pe an» at its end, which the owner did not see.

**Decision.**
- **The money model keeps the vendor's own period.** A paid cost (`PlanCost`, renamed from `AnnualCost` so nothing is called annual that is not) carries the figure its invoice carries and `billed: "monthly" | "yearly"`: the domain's 10.97 a year, Mailgun's plan price a month (no longer × 12), Vercel Pro's 20 × seats a month. Two pure helpers derive the other figure — `perMonth` (a monthly invoice as it is, a yearly one's twelfth to the cent, a usage plan's estimate) and `perYear` (a yearly invoice as it is, twelve monthly ones, twelve months of the estimate) — both null for a usage plan nothing measures. `annualCostToday` sums `perYear`; the new `monthlyCostToday` sums `perMonth`, with the same shape and the same rule that unmeasured usage adds nothing and marks the total estimated. The header's currency rule stands: every amount in the vendor's currency, no exchange rate, except §511's one euro total on the month card.
- **«Cât costă» says both periods, per service and in total.** The sentence is «Astăzi clubul plătește {month} pe lună, adică {year} pe an.», with «circa» only when an estimate is in it and «+ TVA» on each amount VAT comes on top of; the estimate's note drops «(× 12)». Under it, a breakdown (`PlanCostTable`, a Server Component): one line per service in the cost table's order, «Serviciu» · «Pe lună» · «Pe an», then a bold «Total». A free service says «gratuit» in both cells, an estimate is prefixed «≈», VAT is said per cell, and a usage plan whose pace is unmeasured says «ritm nemăsurat». It is a CSS grid of three columns, never a table that scrolls sideways at 320 pixels; a «?» says that one column is the invoice's amount and the other is worked out from it. The name column is `minmax(min-content, 1fr)` and the cells wrap at spaces, because with `minmax(0, 1fr)` and break-anywhere the names collapsed to nothing at 320 pixels once the amounts took their width.
- **Each service row's «Cost azi» names both figures and which one the vendor bills**: «20,00 USD/lună + TVA, facturat lunar · 240,00 USD pe an + TVA» for a monthly invoice, «10,97 USD pe an + TVA, facturat anual · circa 0,91 USD/lună + TVA» for the domain (the period is said in words and VAT sits on both figures, so the row and the table agree), «circa … USD/lună, la consum · circa … USD pe an» for Neon Launch.
- **When nothing new is coming, the page says so.** `nextSpend` returns null once the domain, Mailgun and Vercel are all paid; the alert then says «Nu urmează nicio cheltuială nouă: ce e luat temporar se poate opri după cursă.» (date-free: the Vercel card's note says when and why) instead of printing nothing.
- **The verdict names what is paid.** «se plătesc domeniul și baza de date… restul gratuite» is false once Mailgun or Vercel is paid, so a new verdict `paysForPlans` comes whenever any row besides the domain is `paid` (after `notFree` and `freeButAtALimit`, as before; `paysForUsage` stays for the Neon-only case). Its sentence is built from the paying rows, never fixed: «Se plătesc: {services}; restul serviciilor sunt pe planuri gratuite.», each service a short name with its plan (`freeVerdict.paidName.*`), joined with the locale's `Intl.ListFormat`.

**Vercel's plan became a setting now.** The club pays Vercel Pro since 2026-09-30 (the function quota before the 21 November race), and the page printed Hobby, a free Vercel row, and «Prima cheltuială care urmează: Vercel Pro». The plan is `platform_settings.vercelPlan` — Hobby or Pro and the developer seats (1–20) with a note — set by an Administrator on a new card, «Planul Vercel (găzduirea)», right after the database's card and before «Cât costă», and audited as `vercel_plan.changed` (from and to, with the seats, and the note) under its own fixed entity id. Hobby is the default, so a deployment that never set it reads exactly as before. On Pro the Vercel row is paid monthly at 20 × seats with VAT on top (the invoice decides; the treasurer adds it as for Mailgun), nothing is reached and the row is "ok" (the non-commercial clause no longer applies), there is no next plan, the bump is temporary, and its sentences (`services.vercel.pro.*`) say what Pro gives — the seats at $20 a month and $20 of usage credit included, as `docs/PLATFORM.md` quotes them — that its ceiling is not measured here, that usage beyond the credit is billed on top, and that it can be given back after the race, with no date in the sentence. «Luna aceasta»'s Vercel line on Pro is the seats' price so far and projected, with VAT, last month the same plan's price (as Mailgun's is), and the build minutes counted with no ceiling, because Pro's is not recorded and none is invented.

**Copied from §100 and §326, and what differs.** The shape is the Mailgun plan's (§100) and the Neon plan's (§306/§326): a key–value row with no migration, a strict zod schema whose unreadable value falls back to the default, the service asserting `canManageClubSettings` as the action does, the same confirm words and `RecallField`s, a refusal handed back as the form's state. Two things differ. Pro is priced per seat, so the setting carries the seats and the card says who set it and when. And Vercel's API is not asked: the setting is the plan. The follow-up is §326's shape — Vercel's own answer first, the setting as the fallback.

**Tests.** `diagnostics/platform-plans.test.ts`: `perMonth`/`perYear` both ways (15 a month → 180 a year, 10.97 a year → 0.91 a month, two seats → 480 a year, 9.61 a month of usage → 115.32, unmeasured → null), both totals with the domain, Mailgun Basic, Vercel Pro and Neon Launch all paying, the Vercel row on Hobby and on Pro, `nextSpend` null when everything is paid, the `paysForPlans` verdict and its order, and every key the page reads in both languages. `diagnostics/month-costs.test.ts` and `month-costs-read.test.ts`: the Pro line and the totals with it. `diagnostics/vercel-plan.test.ts` (the schema) and the PGlite `integration/diagnostics/vercel-plan.test.ts` (the default, an Administrator's save, the refusals, the audit row, the cost table following it). `diagnostics/plan-cost-table.test.ts` renders the breakdown. `e2e/tasks-cost.spec.ts` asserts the new sentence, the two column headers, one line per service and the Vercel card.

*Rejected:*
- **A lei conversion.** The file's currency rule: no vendor invoices in lei except the registrar, at a rate nobody knows in advance; §511 keeps its one euro total on the month card, and nothing else converts.
- **Hiding the free rows.** The owner asked per service: a free service is a row that says «gratuit», so the table is complete and its total visibly sums all of it.
- **Reading the plan from Vercel's API in this change.** The endpoint and its answer could not be verified from the phone session; §326's shape — Vercel's answer first, the setting as fallback — is the follow-up.
- **Counting Vercel's $20 usage credit as a cost.** It is included in the seat's price, not billed on top of it; only usage beyond it is, and the page says so in words rather than as a figure it cannot measure.

Baseline `BR-V2.55-2026-10-01`.

## 611. The past events have their own «Filtre», independent of the cards ahead (amending §602)

**The owner, 2026-10-01 on QA:** «Mi-ar trebui aceleași filtre și pentru evenimentele din trecut». **And the same day, after §602 shipped:** «Am zis că vreau un filtru și la evenimentele trecute, la fel ca la cele curente».

**What §602 did, and why it was not what he meant.** §602 sent the listing's one filter state through the past section too: the top panel's ticks narrowed the cards ahead and the past window alike, the top panel read its offer off the past window as well, and a filtered page opened the past fold. Three things followed. There was one state for two lists, so a reader could not look for last spring's races without also hiding the runs ahead. There was no control at the past section itself — the «Filtre» button sat at the top of the page, far from the list it now also narrowed. And «Înscrieri deschise» was offered whenever any past event existed, because ticking it hid the past, which no reader means by "where can I register". The owner asked for a filter at the past events, like the one at the current events: a control of its own, with its own choices.

**Decision.**
- **Two scopes, one address.** The top panel keeps §413's parameter names (`type`, `surface`, `difficulty`, `distance`, `cost`, `partner`, `night`, `registration`). The past section's panel uses the same groups and flags under a `past-` prefix (`past-type`, `past-surface`, …, `past-registration`), read in both of §413's shapes — the form's repeated parameters and comma-separated values, any case, `-` for `_` (criterion 77). `events/domain/listing-filter.ts` gains `FILTER_SCOPES`, a pure `scopedParams(params, scope)` (the `upcoming` scope is the unprefixed names and ignores every `past-` name; the `past` scope is the `past-` names with the prefix stripped), `parseListingFilter(params, scope = "upcoming")` and `listingFilterQuery(filter, scope = "upcoming")`. `activeFilterCount` is unchanged. `?type=FOO` and `?past-type=FOO` still mean no filter.
- **Independent lists.** The cards ahead (the lead's included) and the undated section follow the upcoming scope alone; `matchingPastEvents` takes the past scope alone. The past heading, its `open`/`data-filtered` and its count follow the past filter alone: «Din trecut, după filtre (N)», «Din trecut — Concurs (N)» when one kind is all that is ticked, «N evenimente trecute» otherwise. The row the lead shows between seasons (§167) is still left out by its id.
- **Each panel offers its own rows.** The top panel's offer is back to the dated and the undated cards; §602's side effect — «Înscrieri deschise» offered because a past event exists — is gone. The past panel's offer is `offeredFilters` over the past window alone (less the lead's row), under §413's rule (criterion 75): a box only where ticking it narrows the past, or where the address ticks it. No past event has an open door, so «Înscrieri deschise» is not offered there unless the address ticks it. The past section's control does not follow criterion 75's rendering rule, and this is deliberate: the owner asked for a control at the past events, and a control that is absent whenever last season was uniform — which is the case on production, where the past window is one weekly series — reads as missing, not as honest. So the past panel renders whenever the section has at least one row (the lead's row left out), and with nothing to narrow and nothing ticked its fold holds one sentence instead of a form: «Toate evenimentele trecute sunt la fel — {values} — așa că nu e nimic de filtrat aici.» / "Every past event is the same — {values} — so there is nothing to narrow here." (`Events.filter.pastNothingToNarrow`), the values being the kind, the surface, the difficulty band, the distance band and the cost where every past event shares exactly one, joined with the locale's list formatting (`singleValues`). The «Filtre» button keeps its words and opens the fold (a native `<details>`, no script). The boxes' own rule stands — no box that narrows nothing — and the top (upcoming) panel keeps it untouched: it renders only when it offers something or the address ticks something (§413 criterion 75, and criterion 180 of §602, which said the panel offers a value the past carries, are amended for the past scope only). The live QA and production windows were not readable from the build session; the e2e seed's one past group run is a uniform window, which now shows the button and the sentence.
- **Its place and plumbing.** The past panel renders inside the past `<details>`, right after its heading and before the cards, so it is reachable only when the fold is open — and with a past tick the fold is open. `ListingFilterPanel` gains `scope` and `carry`: `carry` is the other scope's ticks, kept as hidden inputs in the form and in every chip link, so a tick in one panel — submitted natively or by `FilterAutoApply`, which builds the address from the form's own fields — keeps the other's. Its boxes, its «Scoate filtrul: …» links and its «Șterge filtrele» use the scope's names; its form is named «Filtrele evenimentelor trecute» / "Filters for past events" and its row of active chips «Filtre active pentru evenimentele trecute» / "Active filters for past events"; its button still says «Filtre (N)», counting its own scope. `FilterAutoApply` remembers which scope was ticked, so only that panel reopens after a remount (§549), and it reopens every fold around the panel too — a reader who unticks the past section's last box is not left with the section shut over the panel they were using. When a past tick matches nothing, the section stays, open, with its panel and «Niciun eveniment nu se potrivește filtrelor alese.»
- **The live twin.** A `past-` tick changes what the listing shows, so the listing's twin rule (`i18n/live-twin.ts`, §549/§577) is now "either scope ticks something". `?past-foo=1` and `?past-type=FOO` stay on the CDN.
- **The calendar is left alone.** It draws no past section: it reads the upcoming scope only, a `past-` name on a calendar address is not a twin, and its links drop it.

**Why one address with two scopes, not two addresses or a client state.** A link still says everything the page shows: a reader can share "last year's trail races" or bookmark it, the GET form still works with no script (criterion 79), and the twin rule stays one parser over one query. A prefix is the smallest change that keeps every existing address meaning what it meant.

**Why the lists are independent.** A panel that shows unticked boxes while another panel narrows its list would lie about what is in force. Each list now answers to the panel next to it, and each button counts exactly the ticks that narrow its own list.

**What stays.** The window: one cached read of the latest 60 past events, 12 cards shown, the same data-cache entry whatever is ticked, narrowed in memory (§413, §602) — no new query, no new cache key. The calendar. §267's closed fold when nothing is ticked in the past scope. The undated section follows the upcoming scope, as before.

*Rejected:*
- **No past panel when nothing narrows (this entry's first version).** The owner's complaint was exactly the missing control; on a uniform window it read as absent. A button that opens onto an honest sentence replaced it.
- **Two panels sharing one state** — the owner's words, «la fel ca la cele curente», ask for a control of its own with its own choices; two buttons over one state would each claim the other's ticks.
- **A panel beside the past heading, outside the fold.** The fold is closed by default (§267), and a control for hidden content misleads: ticking a box would change a list nobody can see.
- **A wider window or a pager.** §602's reason stands: either costs a read, and the calendar is the archive.

**Tests.** Unit `events/listing-filter.test.ts`: both scopes of `scopedParams`/`parseListingFilter` (the upcoming scope ignores `past-*`; the past scope reads `past-type` repeated and comma-joined, any case, `-` for `_`, kilometre and legacy aliases), `listingFilterQuery(filter, "past")` round-trips and is nothing to the other scope, `withoutValue` on a past filter, and the top offer no longer holds a box only the past carries (§602's test reversed, its reason kept in the comment). Unit `events/past-events-filter.test.ts`: a past filter narrows the past and leaves the cards ahead alone, and the other way round; the past offer comes from the window and never offers «Înscrieri deschise»; with a past tick the section is open, draws only the matches and says «Din trecut, după filtre (N)», «Din trecut — Concurs (2)» for one kind; an upcoming tick leaves it folded and whole; a past tick that matches nothing keeps the section, its panel and the way back; the past panel sits between the heading and the cards, its boxes are named `past-…` and its hidden inputs carry the upcoming scope; the top panel's hidden inputs carry the past scope and its chip links keep it. Unit `i18n/live-twin.test.ts`: `?past-type=RACE` is the listing's twin, `?past-foo=1` and `?past-type=FOO` are not, `?type=RACE` still is, and the calendar ignores `past-`. `theme/density.test.ts` records the panel's gap. E2E `listing-filters.spec.ts`, both projects: the bare listing's past fold always has the «Filtre» button, with boxes or the sentence whichever the window is; and from an address ticking two past kinds, the past panel unticks «Concurs» — the address carries `past-type=GROUP_RUN` alone, the heading says «Din trecut — Alergare de grup (N)», the cards ahead are untouched — then «Concurs» in the top panel narrows the cards ahead and leaves the past heading as it was. Unit `events/past-events-filter.test.ts` also covers a uniform window (button and sentence with the right values in both languages, no checkbox), a mixed one (boxes, no sentence) and no rows (no section). `FilterAutoApply`'s memory of the ticked scope (`ui/filter-reopen.ts`, unit `events/filter-reopen.test.ts`) now carries the address the tick goes to, so a later mount on another address ignores it; it is also spent after the commit that answers the tick, whichever panel asked, and dropped after ten seconds: a past panel that stopped rendering (its last box unticked over a window with nothing else to narrow) can no longer leave a stale "past" that opens a later past panel, reached from a shared link or the back button, unasked.

Baseline `BR-V2.55-2026-10-01`.

## 612. The card says a place is offered, not waiting; the job wakes when a family's reservation lapses and sweeps free places while somebody waits (amending §587 and §104)

**The owner, 2026-10-01**, with a phone screenshot of the published race's card («Înscrieri deschise până … · **2 locuri libere** din 10 · 1 pe lista de așteptare»): «Nu ar trebui să intre oamenii automat din lista de așteptare în înscriși? Parcă așa am zis». Places free, and somebody still waiting for one: it looked like a place nobody was given.

### What the investigation found

**1. The card counted an offer as somebody waiting.** The race had 10 places: 7 taken and 1 place offered to the head of the waiting list, its offer open. The one formula (`domain/capacity.ts`, §10.6) is free = capacity − occupied − WAITLISTED. An open offer is occupied, so 10 − (7 + 1) − 0 = 2 free. Nothing was wrong with the count. The words were wrong: §587's «N pe lista de așteptare» is `waitlistLength`, the people waiting **plus the open offers** (`domain/waitlist.ts`), so the person who had been offered the place was said as «1 pe lista de așteptare». The allocator had done its job, and the card said it had not.

**2. The job had a gap: a place could stay free while somebody waited.** Two cases.
- **A family's reservation that lapsed.** A family's reservation (§543) frees its place at the sitting's fixed deadline, with no write. The maintenance job did clear it once somebody waited. But the job's plan (`jobs/next-work.ts#nextMaintenanceWork`) scheduled only the offers' and the declaration holds' deadlines, not a family's. The form's save woke the job once. The run that followed promised a quiet to the daily window (04:00, §577) and slept through the lapse. The place came back in the count, and nobody waiting was offered it until the next sign-up or 04:00.
- **No clause for free places while somebody waits.** The job's scan (`findEventsNeedingMaintenance`) had no clause for that. Each of its clauses names a row whose deadline has passed. So a place freed with no such row was never swept. The plainest case is a race cancelled and put back on. Somebody withdraws while it is cancelled, the place is released, and `fillAvailableSpots` offers nothing on a cancelled event (§331). Once the race is back on, nothing wakes for the free place.

### Ruled out, and why
- **A backlog from before BR-V2.50.** `unregister`, a staff cancellation and an erasure already offered the freed place in their own transaction (§596). A cancellation never leaves a place free while somebody waits.
- **A capacity raise.** The editor's save offers the new places in its own transaction (`capacityRaised` → `fillAvailableSpots`, §147). It is unchanged here.
- **A family on the waiting list.** Its people are `WAITLISTED` and the card already read «3 pe lista». They are not a free place.
- **An address not confirmed yet.** It is never `WAITLISTED`. It takes no place and joins no line until the address is confirmed.
- **Declaration holds expired by the job.** They are released only as far as the line needs (§160). The same pass offers each released place, so none is left free.

### Decision
**The card names an offered place as offered.** `readPublicPlaces` returns the line's two halves beside its length: `offered` (the open offers, `OccupiedCounts.unexpiredWaitlistOfferedHolds`) and `waitlisted` (the `WAITLISTED` rows, `countEligibleWaitlisted`). Both come from the two counts it already made, so there is no new query. `cachedPublicAvailability` carries both in the same entry. An entry cached before this release has neither and reads them as nought until it expires. The door (`registrationCta`) carries them in the open state. Each surface says the line after the free places, in this order, each only when it has anybody:
- «N loc(uri) oferit(e) din lista de așteptare» / "N place(s) offered from the waiting list", the new `cta.offeredCount`, with its three forms through `countForm` and never an ICU plural;
- then «N pe lista de așteptare» for the people with no offer yet.

The card joins them with a middle dot and puts none of them in bold (§472). The event page draws one line each. The full-race thank-you (§587) and every other wording stay. The backoffice's queue panel gains «Oferite» / "Offered" between «Libere» and «În așteptare». It is the same `countOccupied` field the card reads, so the panel and the card say the same number.

**The job wakes at a family's lapse, and sweeps free places while somebody waits.**
- The plan now also schedules the deadline of every family reservation (a `PENDING_EMAIL_CONFIRMATION` row with `hold_expires_at`). It also schedules every `family_place_holds` row that holds a place, on a scheduled event. A cancelled event's are left out, as its other deadlines are (§331).
- The scan gains one clause: a scheduled, capped event, before its close, with a `WAITLISTED` row and fewer places occupied than its capacity. The occupied count is the allocator's own (`countOccupied` → `computeOccupied`), read without the lock, never a formula in SQL. Such an event goes through the job's existing locked `fillAvailableSpots` (`maintenance.ts`), which counts again under the lock.
- The cost is one read per scheduled capped event with somebody waiting, per run, and nothing on every other event. The plan's two new deadline reads do not look for a waiting person, so a sitting's deadline on an event where nobody waits wakes the job once for nothing (§334): family sittings are rare, and a join before the deadline is a write that wakes and replans the job anyway.
- `capacityRaised` and `capacity.ts` are unchanged.

### The rules kept
- **No second path offers a place.** Every offer is still `fillAvailableSpots`, under the event-row lock, so there is no overbooking under concurrent load.
- **No offer at the wrong time.** None after the close (the offer's deadline would be behind it, §420), and none on a cancelled event (§331).
- **Never more offers than free places.** One free place gives one offer, to the oldest in the line.
- **`kind` is in no condition** of the allocator, the formula or the new clause (§30). A test registration is swept exactly as a real one, and can exist nowhere but QA. The public counts include it, as the free places always have (`publicFill`'s note).

### Tests
- `tests/unit/events/card-registration-line.test.ts`: 7 taken, 1 offered, capacity 10 gives «2 locuri libere din 10 · 1 loc oferit din lista de așteptare» and the English line. One waiting gives «… · 1 pe lista de așteptare». Both give both, offered first. §587's case is restated in the two halves.
- `tests/unit/events/registration-cta.test.ts`.
- `tests/integration/registrations/card-registration.test.ts`: the card and the page, through the public cache.
- `tests/integration/registrations/queue-panel-zone.test.ts`: «Oferite» equals the card's `offered`.
- `tests/integration/registrations/family-reservations.test.ts`: after the lapse and the run, the card says «loc oferit». A new case shows the job's plan is the family's deadline, and the run at that instant offers the place with no hand call.
- `tests/integration/jobs/next-work.test.ts`: a reservation's and a held place's deadline are scheduled, and neither is on a cancelled event.
- `tests/integration/registrations/maintenance.test.ts`: a cancelled race put back on gets its one free place offered to the oldest on the next run. After the close, nothing. Still cancelled, nothing. A full race, nothing. A `TEST` waiting list gives the same transitions and counts as a `REAL` one.

The two-connection suite (`yarn test:concurrency`, `tests/concurrency/capacity.test.ts` among it) was run against a PostgreSQL 16 database of this branch's own: 5 files, 14 tests passed, none skipped (`tests/concurrency/capacity.test.ts`, `cms-conflict`, `desk-race`, `family`, `spare-bibs`).

### Rejected
- **Offering the next person while an offer is open.** Two promises for one place is overbooking by another name.
- **Counting an offered place as free.** A place promised is not free. The card would advertise a place the next person cannot get.
- **A sweep on every public render.** That would be a read on every visit for a rare lapse. The job has the lock and the clock, and a page render decides nothing (§10.6).

Baseline `BR-V2.55-2026-10-01`.

## 613. The public list shows the race number, behind the privacy notice, settled numbers only (amending §396 and §214)

**Amends §396 and, for the list, §214's rule on which number may be published.** The owner, 2026-10-01: "In the public participants list, I also want to show the BID as a column, not just the index in the table."

**What the list shows today, and what the notice in force says.** «Cine vine» is a table of a row index, the display name and the club (§250), with the states (§396) and the socials (§500) each behind their own marker in the privacy notice. No race number is selected or shown. The notice in force describes a list of names and clubs, and says the waiting list is shown «fără loc numerotat»; it says nothing of a race number beside a name.

**The gate.** The public list is a disclosure (§32), so the number goes on it the way the states and the socials did, and only that way. A new merge field, `{{participantListNumbers}}` (`LIST_NUMBERS_MERGE_FIELD`, `describesListNumbers`), is both the switch and the words. It is filled, when the notice is shown, with the column's own heading words, quoted, read from the catalogue the heading reads (`registrations/list-number-words.ts`, `Event.startList.columnNumberFull`): «„numărul de concurs”» / «“race number”». The list shows the column only while the privacy notice in force names the field in every language (`cachedListNumbersDisclosed`, the same cached reading as §396 and §500; `noticeDescribesListNumbers` is the backoffice's uncached twin). A notice approved before it does not name it, and the list under it is exactly today's: not a cell of difference, and no number is even selected. Switching it on is the club's one press in `/admin/legal` (§29, §95): no setting, no deploy. The texts in force keep their words until then.

- The platform's privacy notice names the field in section 4, in a sentence of its own after the states', in both languages: «Lângă numele fiecărui participant confirmat apare și {{participantListNumbers}} — cel pe care îl poartă în cursă. Un participant confirmat care nu are încă număr apare fără el. Cei care nu și-au confirmat încă locul, cei de pe lista de așteptare și cei care nu apar cu numele nu au număr pe listă. Numărul face parte din apariția ta pe listă: îl retragi odată cu ea.» Section 4's first sentence names «numărul de concurs al celor confirmați» among what the list shows.
- The terms name it in their list sentence, beside the states and the socials, so the two texts the club approves together agree, and neither says «nimic altceva» of a list that shows more. In the terms the number stands before the per-registration clause («clubul, {{participantListNumbers}} al celor confirmați și, dacă nota … o prevede, stadiul înscrierii …»), so that clause conditions only the states: the list shows every confirmed runner's number whatever notice they registered under.
- The legal editor's legend lists it. The legal pages, the declaration page and the signed PDF fill it wherever they fill the socials' field.

**Whose consent the number rests on: the owner's decision, 2026-10-01.** The owner: "Vreau sa afișez BID-urile la toți, forțat!" — the number is shown for every confirmed runner, whichever privacy notice their registration recorded. The first version of this change gated the column a second time per runner, on the notice each had been given (§421's rule for the states), and showed «—» for anyone registered under an older notice; the owner overruled that. The reasoning the club owns: the race number is the one on the runner's chest and in the results on race day, so it is not a secret the list newly reveals; the runners who registered under the earlier notice are told by the club before the new notice is approved (the first step of the `/admin/tasks` row: «Trimite un mesaj participanților» on the event, saying their number will appear beside their name on «Cine vine» and that they withdraw by pressing «Nu vreau să apar pe lista de participanți & rezultate» in «Înscrierile mele» or from the manage link); and the gate by the notice in force remains, so nothing is shown until the club has approved a notice that describes it. The number is tied to the listing: it leaves with the name, because a runner who withdraws the tick is not a row at all. **The states keep §421's per-runner rule unchanged** (`findFirstStatesNoticeVersion`, `cachedFirstStatesNoticeVersion`): a pending or waiting registration is listed only for a tick given under a notice that described the states. For the numbers there is no first-version lookup, no per-runner condition in the query and no version in the cached page's key; the key carries only whether numbers are asked for. The column is still decided per page, from the page's own rows: on an event where only some runners are numbered it can be present on one page and absent on the next; a per-event decision was left out as not worth a further cached count.

**Which number.** Only `bib_number`. Never `provisional_bib_number`: §214's reason stands — the provisional number was printed nowhere and emailed to nobody precisely so that it could move, and a number published beside a name is a number that cannot. Since §548 a number is drawn at the confirmation and nothing writes the provisional column any more, so in practice every confirmed real runner already wears the number that goes on the list; the brief's premise that numbers settle only at the close is §214's, which §548 replaced. The query is unchanged in that respect, and the privacy test now refuses the provisional column on every public start-list query by name.

**Which rows show what.**
- The column («Nr.», «No.»; the whole word in the heading's `aria-label` and an `abbr` title) sits after the index and before the name, right-aligned, in tabular figures, as narrow as its widest number. The index column is unchanged.
- A named confirmed runner: their number. A named confirmed runner with none (confirmed before a number existed, or a number the §548 data step could not keep, until «Alocă numerele» gives one): «—».
- The pending and waiting rows (§396's groups): «—». No number exists before the confirmation (§548), and `listPublicStartListOthers` selects nothing new.
- A hidden row («Participant (nume ascuns)»): an empty cell. Nothing about it is read (§186), not even a dash that would set it apart.
- The column appears only when the page's confirmed rows carry at least one number. An event that numbers nobody keeps today's three columns rather than a column of dashes.
- The caption under the table names the number only while the column is there (`captionNumbers`, `captionStatesNumbers`).

**The query.** `listPublicStartList(db, eventId, page, { socials, numbers })`: `numbers` adds `bibNumber` to the select, for every confirmed row, the way `publicSocialColumns` adds the socials. Without it the keys are exactly today's; `tests/privacy/public-surface.test.ts` pins both. The cached page carries the flag in its key. A number typed by hand (`setBibNumberByStaff`), «Alocă numerele» (`assignBibNumbers`) and the one-off step that keeps a legacy number (`releaseLegacyHeldNumbers`, from the maintenance run) now expire the public «places» cache after their commit, as a confirmation already does through `transitionRegistration`, so a replaced number does not stay up.

**The task row.** `/admin/tasks` carries `listNumbersNotice`, the twin of `listStatesNotice`: open, never blocking, while the notice in force does not name the field; done by itself once one does. Its «done» sentence, kept to the backoffice's 200-character cap, says the column shows for every confirmed runner who has a number, «—» for one without; its steps start with the message to the runners registered under the earlier notice and name the withdrawal control, then the same press in `/admin/legal`, which says the same beside §396's and §500's lines: an info line, `listNumbersMissing`, while a notice is in force that does not name the field. CLAUDE.md's «Still owed» item 16 gains the sentence.

**Tests.** `tests/privacy/public-surface.test.ts` (a confirmed runner's number is read whatever notice their registration recorded; no number key unless asked; with the flag the one key `bibNumber`, null for a runner with none; a hidden runner's number never read; `provisionalBibNumber` read by no public start-list query, by behaviour and by source). `tests/integration/registrations/start-list-numbers.test.ts` (the column with the right number beside the right name, «—» for a confirmed runner without one and for the pending and waiting rows, an empty cell for a hidden row, in both languages; without the states' marker; a provisional number never shown; no number on the page gives markup identical to a notice without the marker; an older notice gives markup identical to rows wearing no number; an older-notice runner's number shown, in both languages, and «—» for an older-notice runner without one; one language's marker is not enough). `tests/integration/registrations/bib-cache-expiry.test.ts` (the "places" cache is expired after a hand-typed number and after «Alocă numerele» assigns one or more, and not when none is assigned; the maintenance run's one-off legacy step expires it when it kept a number and not when it kept none). `tests/integration/registrations/start-list-render.test.ts` (no notice: no column). `tests/unit/registrations/list-numbers.test.ts` (the marker, the templates, the legend, the words from the catalogue). `tests/unit/diagnostics/owner-tasks.test.ts` (the row's open and done; the message step comes before the approval and names the opt-out control). `tests/e2e/public-list-states.spec.ts` gains a step — the seeded runners wear no number, so no «Nr.» header, whatever the notice names — and its notice without markers drops this one too, and `/admin/legal` names it missing.

*Rejected:*
- **Showing the provisional number.** §214: it was published nowhere so that it could move.
- **Showing the number without a notice change.** The rule in CLAUDE.md's table: a public list is never a wider disclosure than the approved privacy notice describes.
- **Gating each runner on the notice they registered under (the first version, §421's rule).** The owner overruled it on 2026-10-01: the number is on the chest, the earlier runners are told by the club's message, and the notice in force still gates the column.
- **The number in place of the index column.** The owner's «not just the index» could be read that way, but the index is the row's position and is how a page link and a reader find a place; replacing it also puts the number on a row's only identifier. The two stay side by side.
- **A per-event switch.** The list is already a disclosure behind one notice; a second setting per event would be a second thing to forget and would not change what a runner agreed to.
- **A column of «—» when nobody on the page has a number.** An empty column says nothing to a reader.

No migration.

**What «Sarcini» says.** The row `listNumbersNotice` in `/admin/tasks` names, as its first step and before the approval, the message the club sends to the runners registered under the earlier notice («Trimite un mesaj participanților»), and, as its second, the control by which a runner withdraws («Nu vreau să apar pe lista de participanți & rezultate» in «Înscrierile mele»); from approval on, the list shows the «Nr.» column for every confirmed runner who has a number, «—» for one without.

Baseline `BR-V2.55-2026-10-01`.

## 614. The journey's third step says where the declaration is: in the email just sent, below, or in the email received — never a «here» that leads nowhere

**The owner, 2026-10-01:** «Mic bug, trebuie să avem că declarația vine pe mail, acel link nu duce nicăieri» (a small bug: the declaration has to come by email, that link leads nowhere). The screenshot shows the confirmation page, the word «aici» of «citește și semnează declarația — aici, sau pe hârtie…» selected and the browser offering a web search for it.

**Why it happened.** `RegistrationJourney` (§91) wrote one sentence for the third step on every page that shows it, and the sentence was written for the page that has the form, the declaration page. The confirmation page shows the same step right after the address is confirmed, and there the declaration is not on the page: `confirmEmail` has just queued the `COMPLETE_DECLARATION` email, and the signing link lives only in that email. «Aici» was not a link and the component renders none.

**The decision.** The component takes a `declaration` prop, required at the `declare` step and absent at the others (the type says so), with four values, and a sentence for each, in both languages: `emailJustSent` — «din emailul pe care tocmai ți l-am trimis»; `onThisPage` — «mai jos»; `emailReceived` — «din emailul pe care l-ai primit»; `emailHeldUntil` — «declarația ți-o cerem pe email cu {opens} înainte de start», with `opens` the phrase `daysPhrase` builds, as `CheckYourEmail` builds it for the same sentence (§377, §513). The messages are `now.declare.<where>` and `now.declareScheduled.<where>`; the scheduled-delivery clause (§513) is kept and chosen as before, by the wait the data cache reports. Each page passes what is true, and shows the step only where there is something to sign: the confirmation page after a successful press says `emailJustSent`, but for a registration that landed on the waiting list (`done=waitlist`, redirected by `confirmEmailAction`) it shows no stepper, because the email queued is WAITLIST_JOINED and not a declaration (§202); a spent or moved-on link on the confirmation or the declaration page says `emailReceived`; the declaration page says `onThisPage` only when its form renders (`formBelow`, the render's own condition), and shows no stepper at all for a refused link with no notice (unknown, expired, erased, or an event with no approved declaration); the family pages say `emailJustSent` (one person confirmed through the family's link) and, after the sitting, `onThisPage` only when the wizard's button to the declarations is on the page — with no wizard everyone joined is waitlisted and there is no stepper.

**The held case.** `emailHeldUntil` exists for an event whose declaration email waits for its window. Today no page can say it truthfully: a single address's `confirmEmail` queues the declaration email at once, whatever the participation window says (the window decides when the *hold* is asked and owed, and the email invites the person to sign earlier), and only a family's one-press confirmation holds it, for minutes, while its wizard is on the screen. So no page passes it yet; the variant and its sentence are tested and ready for the day the email is held on the single path.

*Rejected:* making «aici» a real link on the confirmation page. The signing link's token is hashed at rest and lives only in the email; minting a second token from a GET is refused by §12.8 (a GET never mutates), and minting it in the confirmation POST changes the flow, which is a different decision. One sentence for every page was the bug, so it is not the answer either.

**Review round.** In the scheduled delivery timing (qa's and production's default, §513) the declaration email waits for the round like every other, so `now.declareScheduled.emailJustSent` no longer says «tocmai ți l-am trimis» / «we have just sent you»: it says the email is on its way and leaves within {wait} at the most, naming the wait once; the immediate-timing sentence keeps «tocmai». The confirmation page's `done=waitlist` redirect and the waiting-list landing have an integration test (`link-actions-audit.test.ts`): a full event, the second registration confirmed, WAITLIST_JOINED queued and COMPLETE_DECLARATION not. On the family sitting page «mai jos» points at the button that opens the declarations, because the email is held for the family's pass and the forms are one press away.

The confirmation page's `done=waitlist` landing, which shows no stepper, now carries one info alert, `confirm.doneWaitlist` — «Ești pe lista de așteptare. Dacă se eliberează un loc, îți scriem pe email cu ce ai de făcut.» — so the person is told where they stand rather than only that the address is confirmed; the family page's `doneWaitlist` is its counterpart. *Accepted edge:* a spent confirmation link whose registration is still PENDING_DECLARATION says «din emailul pe care l-ai primit»; under scheduled delivery a second tab opened within the wait may arrive before that email has left. It is rare and the sentence is true a moment later, so it is not given a page of its own.

Baseline `BR-V2.55-2026-10-01`.

## 615. Automatic offers from the waiting list are a setting; «Trimite-i oferta» hands a place to the person the organizers name, on the terms' grounds; newcomers queue while anyone waits (amending §104, §587, §589)

**The owner, 2026-10-01**, in his own words, as relayed with the request: «The option to auto-assign from the waiting list should be a config, because now if I increase the limits from 150 to 200 it will auto-draw from the waiting list, right?» · «noi avem 200 de medalii (oficial am zis că sunt 150) dar cu marjă de eroare».

**The owner, 2026-10-01** (in three points, as relayed with the request): the race has **200 medals** and announces **150 places**, a margin the club keeps on purpose; once the waiting list forms, the places beyond 150 should be handed out by the organizers (to an invited runner, an organizer who runs, a pacemaker, a partner, or somebody whose registration an outage disrupted; otherwise in the order of the forms) rather than go to the head of the line the moment they exist; and the people who are waiting must not be overtaken by somebody who registers later.

### What happened until now

Every freed or added place went to the line at once. `fillAvailableSpots` is the one offering path: a cancellation, an offer's expiry or decline, an erasure, a late signature's release, the maintenance job's sweep — and the capacity raised in the editor (§147), which offers the new places **in order, at once, in the save's own transaction**. So raising 150 to 160 while ten people wait sends ten offers in the same second. «Dă-i un loc» (§67, §589, §592) seats one person on a paper declaration at the desk, into a place that is free under the lock; on an open race every free place had already been offered, so it met «full». There was no way to give a place to a chosen person by email.

### The decision

1. **The setting.** A column on the event, `events.waitlist_auto_offer boolean not null default true` (migration `0117`, expand-only): every existing event reads «Da», so nothing changes for the weekly run or the race until an organizer says so. In the editor's «Participare și înscrieri» box, under the capacity: «Ofertele din lista de așteptare pleacă automat» — «Da» / «Nu», with one sentence of help and the rest behind «?» (§511): on «Da» a place freed or added is offered at once to the first person waiting; on «Nu» places stay free until the organizer hands them out, from «Coada de înscrieri» with «Trimite-i oferta» or at the desk with «Dă-i un loc», and while anyone waits newcomers join the list too. A save that does not post the select changes nothing (the partners' discipline, §554). The series' scoped save carries it like the places (`SERIES_COLUMNS`), a copy and every date a series makes keep it, and every change writes `event.waitlist_auto_offer_changed` with `from` and `to` on each date it reached.
2. **One gate.** `fillAvailableSpots` offers nothing when the event's `waitlist_auto_offer` is false. The gate reads the column off the event's row inside the caller's transaction, after the caller took the event lock — so every caller obeys it with no check of its own and no caller's copy of the event can be stale. What `expireStaleHolds` released stays released: a lapsed offer or hold frees its place either way, and the place waits for the organizer. `findEventsNeedingMaintenance`'s free-place sweep also filters `waitlist_auto_offer = true`, so a manual event is not locked on every run to do nothing. Nothing else offers a place automatically. `domain/capacity.ts` is untouched.
3. **Newcomers queue while anyone waits.** In the allocator's opening (`placeForNewcomer`, shared by `allocateOrWaitlist` and a family's reservations), a new registration joins the waiting list whenever the event has a `WAITLISTED` row, even with a place free — under the same lock, from the count just taken (`domain/waitlist.ts#newcomerJoinsLine`). The §160 branch for a full line follows it too, so a full line with people waiting in it refuses rather than seating a newcomer past them. **An open offer is not somebody waiting** (§160's own reading): its holder already has a place, which the offer occupies, and a newcomer taking a *different* free place overtakes nobody. The request named open offers too; counting them was built and dropped, because it changes what «Da» does — the existing test of §160 (a full line's lapsed hold goes to the newcomer) failed, and a newcomer after a raise past the line was offered a place instead of holding one — while protecting nobody: once every waiting person has been offered, the places left over are open registration again under either reading, a day later at most. A family that arrives while anybody waits reserves nothing and joins the line whole once its address is confirmed (§543); a family that arrives with nobody waiting reserves as before.
4. **The public card and page.** While anybody waits (`waitlisted > 0`, or a cache entry's `waiting` from before the halves were counted — the same rule the allocator follows, so the door never promises what the press will not give), the open state no longer prints «N locuri libere din C»: it prints «**Locurile se dau din lista de așteptare** · M loc(uri) oferit(e) din lista de așteptare · N pe lista de așteptare» (the bold part, §472; the counts through `countForm`), and the door is the waiting list's — «Intră pe lista de așteptare», the hourglass, the same door the full state shows. The event page's `RegistrationCta` says the same line above that door, and no free-place count. With the line at its limit, or no list at all, the door is §348's refusal even with places free, since the newcomer would be refused at the end of the form. With nobody waiting — an open offer alone included — today's line and door, the offer named after the free places («2 locuri libere din 10 · 1 loc oferit din lista de așteptare», as this morning's section has it).
5. **«Trimite-i oferta».** A staff verb beside «Dă-i un loc» on the registration's own page, and on every waiting row of «Coada de înscrieri» on the event's page: `offerPlaceToByStaff`, modelled on `promoteFromWaitlistByStaff` up to the transition. Under the event lock it refuses a cancelled or finished event, expires the stale holds, requires `WAITLISTED`, refuses after the close (an offer then would be born lapsed — `OFFER_AFTER_CLOSE`, «La masă, folosește «Dă-i un loc».»), and requires a counted free place (`computeOccupied(counts) < capacity`, else §589's `NoFreePlaceError` and its sentence). Then it moves the row to `WAITLIST_OFFERED` with the ordinary deadline (`offerDeadline`: the club's hours, capped by the close and the start), queues the ordinary `WAITLIST_SPOT_OFFER` through the same function the automatic offer uses (`queueSpotOffer`, marked to leave now, §596), calls `fillAvailableSpots` once in the same transaction, as `promoteFromWaitlistByStaff` does (the stale-hold expiry above may have released another place; on «Nu» the gate makes it a no-op), writes `registration.offered_by_staff` (who, to whom, `aheadOf`: how many waited before them) in the offer's own transaction, and wakes the job for the deadline. It confirms nothing: the runner signs the declaration from the email. The Administrator's (`canManageRegistrations`, asserted in the action, the admin service and the service): «Dă-i un loc» is wider because the desk is every role's, but an offer changes a registration, which the Organizer reads and does not change (§289). The dialog: «Îi trimiți oferta?» — «{name} primește emailul «S-a eliberat un loc» și are până {deadline} să semneze; sare înaintea celor dinaintea lui.», the email's name and the deadline read from the catalogue and the event, in both languages. The «i» of §592 says why a press on a full event will be refused, as for «Dă-i un loc». A full event's refusal on the event's page names who holds the places, as on the registration's page.
6. **Nothing else moves.** «Dă-i un loc» stays the desk's paper confirmation into a free place — the verb for a walk-in, and for after the close. The automatic offer's order (oldest first) stays. Cancellation, expiry and erasure still release through the allocator.

**The recipe for the race.** Keep the capacity at 150 with «Da». When the list forms, set «Nu», raise the places by as many as you are about to hand out (not straight to 200), then send the offers one by one with «Trimite-i oferta»; walk-ins on the morning get «Dă-i un loc». Mind the end of the line: once nobody is `WAITLISTED` (an open offer does not count), the places still free go to whoever registers next, so raising 150 to 200 with ten waiting offers all ten and leaves forty open to the next newcomers. Written into `SETUP.md` §39 beside the capacity.

### Why one gate inside `fillAvailableSpots`

It is already the one path every freed or added place takes (§10.6); a check at each caller would be six checks that drift, and a caller added later would offer by default. Reading the column under the caller's lock makes the setting changed a moment ago the one obeyed.

### Why newcomers queue unconditionally

With automatic offers on it is almost never visible — a freed place is offered in the transaction that frees it, so nobody is left waiting beside a free place; the visible case is the desk after the close, when no offer is made and a walk-in now queues behind the people waiting (the desk's «Dă-i un loc» seats the person standing at the table with a signed paper). With offers off it is the rule that keeps the queue honest: a place the organizer has not handed out yet is not the next stranger's. One rule for both values is one rule to test.

### Why the card stops advertising free places while anyone waits

A newcomer cannot take them: the button would lead to the waiting list whatever the count said. «2 locuri libere din 10» beside «1 pe lista de așteptare» is what the owner's screenshot showed this morning (the section before this one); the card now says how places are given, and the door is the line's.

### The rules kept

No overbooking: a staff offer, like the automatic one, is made only under the event lock into a counted free place, and the offer occupies it (`countOccupied` counts an open offer), so a second press for the same place meets the full count. A new concurrency case in `tests/concurrency/capacity.test.ts`: offers by hand, one free place, two staff offers racing on two connections for two different people — exactly one is made, the other refused with `NoFreePlaceError`, one trail row. `kind` is in no new condition (a TEST registration is offered exactly as a REAL one, tested). Staff never bypass the declaration: an offer still needs the runner's signature.

*Rejected:*
- **An organizers' reserve inside the capacity formula** (places counted as held by the club). It would change the one formula every count reads (§10.6). Named as the follow-up if raising the capacity after the list forms proves clumsy.
- **A club-wide setting.** A race and a weekly run differ; the weekly run keeps offering on its own.
- **Letting newcomers take free places while people wait.** A queue nobody can trust.
- **A staff offer without a free place.** Overbooking by promise: two people told «the place is yours» for one place.

**Consequences.** Migration `0117_waitlist_auto_offer`; `db/schema/events.ts`; `registrations/service.ts` (`fillAvailableSpots`' gate, `placeForNewcomer`, the §160 branch, `queueSpotOffer`, `offerPlaceToByStaff`); `registrations/repository.ts` (`offersWaitlistAutomatically`, the sweep's filter); `registrations/domain/waitlist.ts` (`newcomerJoinsLine`, `OFFER_AFTER_CLOSE`); `registrations/admin-service.ts#offerPlaceByStaff`; `admin/registrations/actions.ts#offerPlaceAction` (back to the event's page from the queue); `registrations/give-place-tip.ts#offerDeadlineIfMadeNow`; `ui/OfferPlaceButton.tsx`, `ui/QueuePanel.tsx`, the registration's page, the event's page; `content/events` (fields, the save, the series, the copy, the trail, `RegistrationBox`); `events/domain/registration-cta.ts` (`fromWaitlist`), `RegistrationDoorButton`, `CardRegistration`, `RegistrationCta`; audit actions `registration.offered_by_staff`, `event.waitlist_auto_offer_changed`; `messages/{ro,en}.json`. Tests: `integration/registrations/waitlist-offers-setting.test.ts` (new), `integration/cms/capacity-raise.test.ts`, `integration/registrations/card-registration.test.ts`, `unit/events/registration-cta.test.ts`, `unit/events/card-registration-line.test.ts`, `concurrency/capacity.test.ts`, `unit/shared/confirmed-actions.test.ts`, `unit/shared/action-icons.test.ts`, `unit/shared/form-constraints.test.ts`, `unit/registrations/single-row-test-kind-email.test.ts`. No dependency.

### After review: the two doors that disagreed, and the recipe

- **The submit-time check follows the allocator.** `assertWaitlistCanTakeOneMore` returns on direct availability only when nobody waits (`!newcomerJoinsLine`), as `placeForNewcomer` does: with «Nu», a full line and the places raised above it, the form refuses WAITLIST_FULL before any email, rather than sending a confirmation the allocator would refuse.
- **The registration form asks the card's question.** `newcomerWouldQueue` (`events/domain/registration-cta.ts`) — no free place, or somebody WAITLISTED (the line's length for an older cache entry) — chooses the form page's waiting-list notice, with the offer hours, or its WAITLIST_FULL / NO_WAITLIST refusal, so someone arriving from «Intră pe lista de așteptare» on an open event is told what the list is.
- **The recipe warns of the end of the line.** Once everybody waiting has been offered nobody is WAITLISTED (an open offer does not count), and the free places go to whoever registers next: raise the places by as many as are about to be handed out (`SETUP.md` §39). Whether open offers should count as waiting stays the owner's question.
- **A staff offer sweeps what its own expiry released.** `offerPlaceToByStaff` ends with `fillAvailableSpots` in its transaction, so on «Da» a second lapsed hold freed by the same expiry is offered to the next in line at once rather than at the maintenance job's next sweep; on «Nu» the place stays free. Tested with two lapsed holds and two waiting, both settings.
- **Open question for the owner, before the race recipe is used:** `newcomerJoinsLine` counts only `WAITLISTED` rows, so once every waiting person has been offered, the places still free are open to the next newcomer. Should an open offer count as somebody waiting? Built and dropped (§3 above); his word decides.
- **The places line says what the two numbers are.** The owner, 2026-10-01: «Consistency bug: cum putem avea 105 înscriși și doar 87 vin?» — the screenshot's two readings being «105 înscriși din 150 de locuri · 45 de locuri libere» above «Cine vine (86)». Both are right: the line counts the occupied places — confirmed registrations plus a pending declaration, an open waiting-list offer and a family's hold (`computeOccupied`) — while the list shows the confirmed. Now the page's places line, in every state that shows it (open, full, waiting list full, no waiting list, and the while-anyone-waits line with free places), says so whenever something is in progress: ro «105 înscriși din 150 de locuri — 86 de confirmați, 19 în curs de confirmare», en «105 registered of 150 places — 86 confirmed, 19 completing their registration» («în curs de confirmare» covers a declaration, an offer and a family in progress alike); with nothing in progress the line is as before. `readPublicPlaces` returns `confirmed` (`OccupiedCounts.confirmed`, `kind` in no condition) and `occupied` — **the count `availablePlaces` is built on** (`occupiedForNewcomer`, which frees a lapsed declaration hold when the line has no room), not the raw `computeOccupied`, so occupied + free = capacity whenever a free line shows; the cached public read carries both. **One rule for the first number, in every state and whether or not anything is pending:** `publicFill` makes it `taken = min(occupied, capacity)` — the registrations holding places, confirmed and in progress — never capacity minus the free places; in progress is `taken − confirmed` (≥ 0); and the waiting list's claim on free places (§615's «Locurile se dau din lista de așteptare»), `kept = (capacity − free) − occupied` floored at nought, is its own part. The clause after the dash lists the parts that exist: «N confirmați» and «M în curs de confirmare» when anything is in progress, and «K locuri păstrate pentru lista de așteptare» / "K places kept for the waiting list" when kept is above nought (`cta.fillKept`, one/few/other through `countForm`; `cta.fillParts` joins them). 4 confirmed, 2 pending declarations, 4 waiting, capacity 10, automatic offers «Nu» → «6 înscriși din 10 locuri — 4 confirmați, 2 în curs de confirmare, 4 locuri păstrate pentru lista de așteptare» under «Mulțumim! Toate cele 10 locuri s-au ocupat — 4 așteaptă deja un loc.»; with 6 confirmed and nothing pending → «6 înscriși din 10 locuri — 4 locuri păstrate pentru lista de așteptare»; an open race with nobody waiting and nothing pending is the plain «105 înscriși din 150 de locuri». (An earlier round let the first number swing between 6 and 10 with the pending count, and counted a lapsed hold twice when the line had no room.) An entry cached before the fields existed shows the plain line, taken = capacity − free as before. `fillPhrase` picks the plurals through `countForm`; the Romanian «86 de confirmați» takes the «de» from twenty on, as the page's other counts. The listing card counts free places, not registered ones, so its text is unchanged. **On QA, where TEST rows exist,** «N de confirmați» counts them (`kind` is in no condition of the capacity formula, §12.6) while the «Cine vine (N)» heading counts REAL rows only (`countPublicStartList`): the two can differ there by the test rows, which is not the bug above; production cannot have a TEST row.

Baseline `BR-V2.55-2026-10-01`.

## 616. An unticked declaration box is named at the box and in the summary, before and after the press

**The owner, 2026-10-01, from his phone, with a screenshot of the declaration page:** "There is a small bug here, if you don't check this box you don't get a validation message".

**Why nothing showed.** The box is `<CheckboxField name="accepted" required dense>`: a MUI checkbox whose native input carries `required` and is visually hidden by MUI. On a phone the browser's own validation bubble for a hidden input either does not show or vanishes at once, so the press looked dead. When a press did reach the server (a browser that ignores `required`, or no script), the action sent it to `?invalid=1` and the page said the generic `declare.pressFailed` sentence at the very top, far from the box and possibly a screen above it, never at the box.

**Decision.**

1. *The server says it at the box.* The unticked box is its own refusal, like §314's name and §330's document: `signDeclarationAction` reads `accepted` from the form before the service is called (the form already says it) and redirects to `?invalid=accept#accepted`, the box's id (`DECLARATION_ACCEPT_BOX_ID`). What was typed comes back sealed, as for the other two. The page renders, for `invalid=accept`, a summary line («Bifează caseta „Am citit și accept declarația…” ca să poți semna.») linking to the box, and under the box a `FormHelperText` in the error colour, named by the input's `aria-describedby`, with `aria-invalid="true"` on the input; the generic sentence is no longer shown for this case, and `declare.pressFailed` is reworded in both languages so it no longer asks for a tick (it now only shows after a press whose box was ticked: a lost race or another field): «Încearcă din nou — linkul tău este în regulă.» / «Try again — your link is fine.» When the box is not the form's first invalid control, the island does not take focus, so the browser's bubble for the earlier field is kept. A dead link still lands on the dead-link page: the flag only reads on a live one.
2. *The client says it before the round trip.* `UntickedBoxSummary`, a small client island, is the summary in both ways: rendered from the server's refusal it is in the HTML with no script; with a script it listens for the form's `invalid` event on the box, shows the same summary at once and focuses it, and takes it away when the box is ticked. `CheckboxField` does the same under the box through a new `requiredMessage`. The native `required` still stops the submit, and only its bubble is replaced; the server path covers a browser that ignores it.
3. *`CheckboxField` gains `error` and `requiredMessage`*, with the `aria-*` wiring; without either, its markup is what it always was (checked against a golden captured from the previous revision). The group run's declaration page (`events/[slug]/declaration`) had the same box and the same silence — its server summary already named the box, but nothing sat under it and no script said it first — and the family confirmation page's «fitnessAcknowledged» box likewise: both use the same two props.
