*One root, whatever the state (found in review).* A box that can ever show a message (it has `help`, `error` or `requiredMessage`) is always wrapped in the same `<Box>`; returning the bare label when nothing is shown and a wrapper when it is would have changed the root element on every flag change, and React would have unmounted the uncontrolled input and mounted a new unticked one, losing the person's first tick after the message. Callers passing none of the three props still print the golden markup byte-for-byte.

**What stays.** The native `required` on the box; the label's words; the service, the signed PDF and the audit, untouched. The minor's second signature is a typed name, not a box (§330), so it has no unticked state of its own and no second code.

**Tests.** An integration test presses the action unticked in both languages (the redirect, nothing spent) and renders the page for `invalid=accept` (summary, helper text, `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`, no generic sentence) and for the other refusals (none of it); a unit test for `CheckboxField` with and without `error`, and for the stable root (the unit environment has no DOM, so the first tick after the message is proved by the e2e step that ticks it and expects the box to stay ticked); one e2e test on both projects, run against a production build.

*Rejected:* dropping `required` and relying on the server alone (a round trip for a tick, and a dead press without the round trip's script); a toast (a message far from the box is the very bug); changing the label's words (the legal reviews fixed them).

Baseline `BR-V2.55-2026-10-01`.

## 617. The running cost is written down: three paid plans and the consoles' first readings

**The owner, from his phone (2026-10-01), with Neon's billing page and Vercel's usage panel:** «you can put this in the docs for devs and admin to know what the costs are».

**What the two pages said.** Neon, organisation-wide, on the first day of the October period (Oct 1 – Nov 1): plan Launch, 1.28 compute hours, $0.14 charged, $0.14 of the $15 spending notification; the page confirms the rates `docs/PLATFORM.md` already carried ($0.106/CU-hour, $0.35/GB-month of storage, $0.20/GB-month of instant restore) and the plan's shape (free limits removed, autoscale to 16 CU, scale to zero after five minutes, 100 projects, 10 branches and 500 GB of transfer per project). Vercel, 28 days left in its cycle: $0.29 of a $20 included credit, $0 on demand — build minutes $0.21, Fluid Active CPU, observability events, function storage, ISR writes and provisioned memory a cent or two each, everything else $0.00. Deployments are the spend; serving the site is cents.

**Decision.** `docs/PLATFORM.md` § Cost is the ledger: one row per paid plan with the day it was taken and the day it is to be dropped, and a reading now and then, so the December review (§280) compares invoices with a record. Three plans are paid now, and the page said so in one place only before this: Neon Launch since 2026-09-22; one Vercel Pro seat since 2026-09-30, taken for the function quota before the race and to be returned to Hobby after the 21 November race (`docs/QUEUE.md` § Waiting on the owner); Mailgun Foundation since 2026-10-01 ($35 a month, read from the owner's Mailgun console). § Subscriptions records the readings of 2026-10-01, corrects the Mailgun and Vercel rows, and dates its heading; `SETUP.md` §40, the administrator's page for Neon's limits, points at the ledger. The `$20` credit is Pro's seat allowance: the credit absorbs the usage, the seat is the bill.

**Mailgun's tier.** The console says Foundation, taken 2026-10-01; the advice is Basic for November once Mailgun lifts the probation, and Free again from December. The platform still has to be told the tier on «Setări» → «Emailuri» (§100): until it is, the outbox defers everything past Free's hundred a day.

*Rejected:*
- A cost page in the application. The figures are the invoices' side; «Setări» → «Costuri» already shows Neon's live consumption as money (§335, §516), and a page cannot read Vercel's or Mailgun's invoice.
- Keeping the screenshots in the repository. A picture cannot be grepped or diffed, the repository is public, and a billing page names the organisation; the words carry everything the pictures said.
- Writing the advised tier instead of the bought one. A ledger records what was bought: Foundation.

Baseline `BR-V2.55-2026-10-01`.

## 618. The terms say the club may refuse or cancel a registration, on objective grounds only (amending §418)

**The owner, 2026-10-01**, on the race's first day of registrations: «Pe viitor trebuie să spunem că ne rezervăm dreptul de a accepta sau refuza un participant, să evităm situații de genul». The dispatcher's brief gave the sentence for the terms: «Organizatorul nu refuză și nu anulează o înscriere pe niciun criteriu interzis de lege.»

**What the terms in force say today.** No general sentence about the club refusing a registration. Three narrow ones: §4 «o înscriere cu o dată a nașterii care arată mai puțin este refuzată» (the minimum age), §4's stopping or excluding on the course («poate fi oprit sau exclus pe loc, fără despăgubire»), and §8 «Clubul poate anula o astfel de înscriere, refuza înscrierile viitoare ale persoanei și limita temporar accesul la platformă» (automated registrations, somebody else's data, a false identity document). Nothing names the grounds together, nothing says the person is told why, and nothing says what happens to the place.

**Decision.**

1. **The terms' template says it, in §3 «Anularea» / "Cancelling", as its last paragraph, in both languages.** «Clubul poate refuza o înscriere sau o poate anula după ce a fost făcută doar pe un motiv obiectiv:» — the event's participation conditions not met (the minimum age, the declarations it asks for, the statement of medical fitness where the event asks it); false, incomplete or another person's data; the event's capacity or safety (the weather, the course, the number of volunteers); conduct contrary to the event's rules or dangerous to others; a registration made against these terms. «Îți spunem motivul pe e-mail — sau pe ecran, când chiar formularul refuză înscrierea —, iar locul eliberat, când este cazul, trece la lista de așteptare, după regulile obișnuite.» (the «când este cazul» because a refusal on the capacity ground frees no place) (the allocator of §104 and §587; nothing new). «La un eveniment gratuit nu este nimic de restituit; dacă ai plătit clubului o taxă de participare, se aplică regulile de restituire de mai sus.» And last: «Clubul nu refuză și nu anulează o înscriere pe niciun criteriu interzis de lege.» / "The club refuses or cancels no registration on any ground the law forbids." The sentence says «Clubul» where the brief said «Organizatorul»: the terms name their party «clubul» (§1), and on another organiser's event the club is not the organiser, so «Organizatorul» would be a word the text never defines. No article number in the paragraph, no club fact, no merge field.
2. **Why §3, not a new section.** Cancelling a registration already made is the club ending the agreement on its own, which Codul civil art. 1203 lets a standard clause do only when it is accepted expressly. §3 is already among the clauses §1 says are accepted by the form's separate box, so §1's list now reads «3 (anularea înscrierii sau a evenimentului ori modificarea evenimentului)» / "3 (cancelling a registration or an event, or changing an event)". The sections keep their numbers, so no cross-reference moves. **The form's box keeps the words the legal review fixed (§421)**: «…clauzele despre anularea sau modificarea evenimentului de către club, …». Whether it must also name the cancelling of a registration is the lawyer's question, not a change made here; CLAUDE.md «Still owed» item 16 asks it.
3. **The declarations: nothing added.** The four declaration templates were read for any sentence about the organiser refusing or cancelling. They say the organiser may change, shorten, stop or cancel the event for safety, and may refuse the start only for missing mandatory equipment. Neither contradicts the terms: both are about the event and the start line, not about refusing a registration. The right to refuse belongs in the terms; the declarations stay the participant's own statements.
4. **The app says the same.** A staff cancellation had no reason kinds: one free-text reason, kept in the audit row and never sent to the person, whose email said only «a fost anulată». The participant's own reasons (§558: injury, other plans, another reason) are the person's, not the club's. So the registration's page in the backoffice gains one box under the cancel form: «Clubul refuză înscrierea, potrivit termenilor: motivul scris mai sus îi este trimis persoanei pe e-mail», with a caption under 200 characters (§511): «Doar pe un motiv obiectiv din termeni: condiții neîndeplinite, date false, capacitate sau siguranță, conduită. Niciodată pe un criteriu interzis de lege. Nebifat, motivul rămâne doar în jurnal.» Ticked, the same verb runs (`cancelRegistrationByStaff`, `kind: "REFUSED_BY_ORGANIZER"`): the same state check, the same allocator releasing the place to the front of the waiting list, Administrator-only as every cancel (§67), asserted in the service. The reason the Administrator typed is the ground. It is written into the cancellation email's payload (never onto the row), and the email gains, before «Locul a fost eliberat.», «Clubul a refuzat această înscriere. Motivul: „…”.» / "The club refused this registration. The ground: “…”." It also links «Termenii și condițiile» in each half's language, from `APP_BASE_URL`. The email says nothing about what the terms allow and names no section number: the terms in force may be a version without the new paragraph or with other sections, and a sentence describing them would then misstate the document it links. The audit row keeps who and why as today, with `kind: "REFUSED_BY_ORGANIZER"` beside the reason. A refusal with an empty ground is refused (`VALIDATION_ERROR` on the reason). The row menu's cancel confirm (`cancelBody`) and bulk cancel's help (`bulkCancelHelp`) say a refusal under the terms is made from the registration's own page. The list's row menu and the bulk cancel post no box and stay ordinary cancellations: a refusal is one person's, with its own ground. No migration, no new verb, no new enum value.
5. **`/admin/tasks`: nothing new.** Its notice rows (`listStatesNotice`, `promoNotice`, `sponsorNotice`, …) each detect one merge field in the notice in force. A paragraph of plain text in the terms has no marker to detect, and «the terms' template moved after the version in force» is already what `/admin/legal` shows as «Șablon nou» (§532), by the template's hash. CLAUDE.md «Still owed» item 16 gains one sentence instead (the approval, and the box's words).

**What changes on the sites.** The texts in force keep their words and their hashes until the club approves the terms from the new template in `/admin/legal`. The staff box works today. Until then its email states only the fact and the ground and links the terms, and the terms in force only cover a refusal through §4's age rule and §8's misuse rule; the email asserts nothing the terms in force do not say.

**A Romanian lawyer reads this paragraph first** (§3's last), as §568's risks paragraph. The paragraph speaks to the person in the second person throughout, as the rest of the terms do («conduita ta», "your conduct"). These notes are the platform's reading of the Civil Code, not legal advice.

*Rejected:* the owner's own wording as a bare, unconditional reservation, «ne rezervăm dreptul de a accepta sau refuza un participant». It protects the club less than the terms with grounds: a right with no stated ground is the one a court reads against the party who wrote the clause (Codul civil art. 1203 and the rule on unfair terms), and it is the very situation the owner wants to avoid, a refusal nobody can explain. So the terms keep his intent, the right to refuse or cancel, and give it the objective grounds and the duty to tell the ground. A per-event setting: the right is the same for every event. Refusing silently: the person must be told. A separate staff verb «Refuză»: the same transition as a cancel, and §67 allows no new verb. A list of grounds to pick from on the staff form: the terms' grounds are broad categories, and the person is owed the concrete fact, which only the typed reason carries.

Amends §418. Tests: unit `tests/unit/legal-documents/terms-refusal.test.ts` (new); the terms' length ceiling in `merge-fields.test.ts` moved from 11000 to 12000; integration `tests/integration/registrations/staff-crud.test.ts` (the refusal's email, place and audit row; a refusal without a ground; an ordinary cancel's email carries no reason).

Baseline `BR-V2.56-2026-10-01`.

## 619. A link replaced by a newer email says so — and the pages that wait for an email point at Spam (amending §13.2's generic response and the spent-link decision)

**What happened.** An Administrator's resend — or the participant's own «Retrimite linkul» — queues the message again, and the outbox mints its link when it sends it (`notifications/render.ts`): `issueActionToken` invalidates the previous live link of the same purpose and scope and writes the new one, so two emails never carry two working links (BR-REQ-036-02 criterion 5). A person who then pressed the *older* email landed on «Acest link nu mai este valabil. Îți putem trimite unul nou, pe aceeași adresă de email.» — the very words a guessed or mistyped address gets — and read it as "something broke". **The owner, 2026-10-01, during the Mailgun incident, after resending links to participants:** «când retrimit, primul link devine invalid? Userul trebuie să știe asta când îl deschide! Și trebuie să le spunem clar să verifice în spam».

**Why it was generic.** §202 gave a spent link (`ALREADY_USED`) a page that says where the registration stands, and kept `INVALIDATED` generic on purpose: `invalidated_at` held two facts in one column — superseded by a newer link (innocent, common) and revoked for cause (a decision to stop a link working) — and a page that coached its holder toward a fresh link would have treated both the same. The strict reading won "until the column can say which happened" (`domain/link-status.ts`).

**Decision.**

1. *The database tells the two apart.* `email_action_tokens.superseded_by_token_id uuid null references email_action_tokens(id) on delete set null` (migration `0117`, expand only: a column, its foreign key and the partial index). `issueActionToken` sets it in the same transaction, right after the insert, on exactly the rows its own UPDATE invalidated (by id, from `RETURNING`): two statements rather than one, so the reference never points at a row not yet written. Nothing else sets it; an invalidation from anywhere else is a revocation and leaves it null. `REGISTER_ANOTHER_PERSON` is never superseded (§420), so it never carries one. When the newer row is swept by retention (§322) the pointer goes null and the older row reads as revoked — generic, the strict reading, long past anybody's inbox. The column has a partial index on the non-null pointers (`email_action_tokens_superseded_by_idx`): the `set null` action runs as an UPDATE on it for every deleted row (retention, erasure cascades), which would otherwise scan a table that grows with every email sent (§327, §549). The foreign key was kept: the partial unique indexes ignore an invalidated row, so it did not collide with them.
2. *The evaluation names it.* `evaluateActionToken` returns `SUPERSEDED` (code `TOKEN_INVALID`) for an invalidated row that carries the pointer and `INVALIDATED` for the rest. The order is unchanged: purpose first (a link replayed at another endpoint stays indistinguishable from an unknown one), then superseded/revoked, used, expired. `readSupersededActionTokenScope` — the sibling of `readSpentActionTokenScope`, read-only, re-evaluating the row itself — gives a page the scope and one instant: when the token `superseded_by_token_id` names — the one that actually replaced this link — was created, which is when its email was rendered (the newest of the scope would be wrong for the list switch, whose press mints a token that goes into a redirect, never an email). Never the newer token's id, hash or secret.
3. *The page says it.* For a superseded link of every purpose a newer link can replace — confirm address, declaration, waiting-list offer, manage, the public list's switch and «Înscrierile mele» (`MANAGE_PROFILE`) — the token page shows, in an `info` box in place of the generic warning, «Acest link a fost înlocuit. Ți-am trimis un email mai nou, cu un link valabil (trimis marți, 29 sept. 2026, la 10:00). Deschide cel mai recent email de la noi — dacă nu-l găsești, caută în Spam și în Promoții.» / "This link has been replaced. We sent you a newer email with a working link (sent …). Open the latest email from us — if you cannot find it, check Spam and Promotions." Two keys (`replaced`, `replacedAt`) chosen in code, the time on Romania's clock, the replacing email's, the one the column names. The resend button stays under it, narrowed to the event as the spent page's is; «Înscrierile mele» keeps «Cere un link nou». The argument is §202's for `ALREADY_USED`, and it is structural: only an exact match on `token_hash` — SHA-256 of 32 random bytes — reaches the row, so whoever reached it holds the secret from that email, and "a newer email has the working link" tells them nothing the email in their hand did not, except which email to open. It reports no state.
4. *What stays generic, and why.* An unknown token has nothing to report; a link opened at another endpoint must stay indistinguishable from it; an expired link's only next step is the resend path the generic page already carries; a link revoked for cause must not coach its holder toward a fresh one. No code path revokes today — the column keeps the two facts apart for the day one does. `AGENTS.md` §13.2 now says both exceptions in one sentence.

**Spam, visibly.** The pages that tell somebody to wait for an email show one `info` box (the list is `tests/unit/registrations/spam-hint.test.ts`; not every page of the journey), the same words everywhere and none of them a time, because the sentence above may say the email has not left yet (`Registrations.spamHint.body`). The box names its object, so it reads on its own wherever it stands: «Nu găsești emailul nostru? Caută în Spam și în Promoții și mută-ne în Inbox, ca să primești și următoarele.» / \"Can't find our email? Look in Spam and Promotions and move us to your inbox so the next ones arrive.\" It stands on the screen after the registration form (in place of the grey «Nu a venit? Uită-te și în Spam.»), under the sentence of the registration's resend form and of «Înscrierile mele»'s once sent, under the newsletter's «Verifică-ți căsuța de email» and its unsubscribe-link answer, under the family confirmation page's «Gata…» and its waiting-list answer (`done` = `declare` and `waitlist`: each waits for an email with a link to press, the declaration's or the offer's), under the group-run declaration's done page, under the event page's interest form once the address is taken (the announcement of the opening is an email still to come; the answer is the same for a new and a known address, so the box is too), on the address-confirmed page (one done branch, reached by `done=1`; its words are «Adresa a fost confirmată» and «Adresa de email a fost confirmată.») and under the race declaration's done page (both outcomes: the confirmation email with the QR, or the waiting list's offer). On the address-confirmed page the box comes after the list of people and its `confirm.next.*` sentences, which name the email, so «Nu găsești emailul nostru?» follows the sentence that says one is coming. Those sentences lost their trailing «Verifică inclusiv folderul de spam» / «Nu îl găsești? Uită-te și în dosarul Spam.», which the box now says once. The replaced-link sentence names Spam itself and gets no second box; the spent waiting-list link's «primești un email…» (`Registrations.spent.waitHelp`) deliberately has none either: it reports a link's own state, as the token pages above do. The short screen after a first form (§536) carries the box too, under the bold «Emailul … pleacă» line and above the offer of another person: it is the screen most registrants see, since every non-member form ends there, not only a family's.

**Accepted:** the replaced-link sentence says the newer email has «un link valabil» without looking at the newest token: if that link was already used, expired or its registration cancelled since, the person opens the newer email and meets the spent or expired page, which says so and offers the resend. Checking would add a second read to a page that exists to be cheap, for a case that ends one click later on a truthful page.

The interest form's done answer reads a little awkwardly with it: no email exists yet (the announcement may be weeks away) and the box ends «ca să primești și următoarele». Accepted as is — one key worded the same everywhere is the design.

**Nothing else moves.** Which links are invalidated and when, the purposes, the resend's limits and the throttle are as they were; every page reads with a GET in read-only transactions and changes nothing.

**Tests.** Unit: `tests/unit/tokens/action-token-state.test.ts` (SUPERSEDED only with the pointer, INVALIDATED without it, PURPOSE_MISMATCH still first, superseded before expired), `tests/unit/tokens/spent-link-status.test.ts` (`mayReportReplaced` opens for SUPERSEDED on every purpose but the family link, and for nothing else), `tests/unit/registrations/spam-hint.test.ts` (the box on the screen after the form, on its short variant after a first form, on both resend forms once sent, on the newsletter's two answers, on the family page's two answers, on the group run's done page, on the event page's interest form, on the address-confirmed page (once, `done=1`) and on the race declaration's done page, in both languages). Integration on PGlite: `tests/integration/tokens/action-tokens.test.ts` (the pointer set on exactly the invalidated rows, profile tokens too, never on a used row or a family link; the reader's answers, its time that of the row the pointer names, not the newest of the scope; a swept newer row reads as revoked) and `tests/integration/tokens/replaced-link-page.test.ts` (through the real Administrator resend and the real renderer: the earlier link's row points at the newer one; its confirmation page says «înlocuit» with the newer email's time in Romanian and English and keeps the resend path, and two GETs change no token; a revoked link, an unknown token and the replaced link opened at the declaration endpoint get the generic page; a replaced «Înscrierile mele» link says it too). e2e: `tests/e2e/registration-link-status.spec.ts` gains one test (a second link minted, the first opened: the box names a newer email) — compiled, not run.

*Rejected:* keeping the older link alive until the newer one is used — two working links in two emails, which BR-REQ-036-02 criterion 5 forbids; a sentence for every invalidated link — a revoked link would coach its holder toward a resend, undoing the revocation; the Spam hint only in the email — the person who cannot find the email never reads it.

Baseline `BR-V2.56-2026-10-01`.

## 620. The guide covers the October releases: the hourly limit and the Gmail road, the bulk resend, the chosen offers, the places line, the numbers column (amending §441)

**Amends §441.** The owner, 2026-10-01, on the race's first day of registrations, from his phone: «Trebuie să actualizăm și documentația live pt voluntari». Three releases had shipped or were shipping that night — the outbox's hourly pace for Mailgun (§605), the bulk resend of the declaration (§606) and the batch with the costs page (§610), the offered place on the card (§612), the numbers column (§613), the journey's step (§614), the chosen offers and the places line (§615) and the declaration box (§616) — and «Ghid» said nothing of any of them. Of the chosen offers he had said the same morning: «Basically I wanna hand pick people from the waiting list and give them a seat».

**Decision.** «Ghid» (`/admin/guide`, `Admin.guide` in both catalogues) describes exactly what this tree does, as §441's jobs — a title and short numbered steps, the screen's own words in «…», roles never people — and nothing that is not built (no Gmail takeover, no public delay notice, no page for a replaced link).

- **«Planul Mailgun, înainte și după cursă»** (Administrator) is rewritten to match the screen: the plan dropdown and the note; «Limita pe oră» — how many leave through Mailgun in an hour, the rest waiting in the queue and none lost, write 90 while Mailgun keeps the account limited — the box is pre-filled with the stored value, 100 by default, which is the hard limit with no margin, so the step uses the box's own verb (its help says «pune 90») rather than "leave" — and on QA, which shares the domain, about 10, as `SETUP.md` §35 asks; raised or cleared once the limit is lifted; «Salvează planul», after which «Costuri», «Trimise în ultima oră:» and «Trimite acum» follow it; «Prin ce pleacă emailurile: Mailgun sau Gmail-ul clubului», the road per group, with «Limita Gmail pe zi (destinatari)», the pause and «Salvează drumurile»; and after the race, Free again.
- **«Emailurile întârzie sau Mailgun a refuzat»** (new, Administrator): where to read «Trimise în ultima oră:» and «În coadă:», what a red «Întârziat…» row means, how a pause Mailgun asked for shows («Ultimul răspuns al furnizorului:» starting "paused by the provider") and that it spends no attempt, when «Trimite acum» helps (Gmail's road, an hour with room) and when it cannot, what to tell participants (Spam and Promotions), and when to write to a Superadministrator, or the club's owner, as the guide's troubleshooting line already says (a row «Oprit după toate încercările», red rows still there an hour later, a last hour stuck at 0 while the queue grows). Only verbs the Administrator has.
- **«Retrimite declarația celor care nu au semnat»** (new, Administrator): the event's «Înscrierile primite» → «Retrimite declarația tuturor care nu au semnat», the dialog's counts and who is skipped, the «La coadă:» banner, three presses an hour, the "i" that says why a press would be refused, and the two warnings — the earlier link stops working, and people should look in Spam and Promotions. The single resend stays «Retrimite emailul» on the registration's page.
- **«Alege tu cine primește un loc eliberat»** (new, Administrator, after «Deschide înscrierile la o cursă»): set «Ofertele din lista de așteptare pleacă automat» to «Nu» *before* raising «Număr de locuri», by as many places as are about to be handed out; «Trimite-i oferta» on a waiting row of «Coada de înscrieri» or on the registration's page; the ordinary «S-a eliberat un loc» email with the club's offer deadline and its «Confirmă locul»; a lapsed offer frees the place again; a free place is needed and the "i" says why a press would be refused; after the close the desk's «Dă-i un loc», with the person there, on paper; what the others see («Locurile se dau din lista de așteptare», newcomers queueing while anyone waits, «Lungimea maximă a listei de așteptare»); and the end of the line — once nobody is `WAITLISTED`, the places still free go to the next newcomer (§615's recipe warns of it). «Deschide înscrierile la o cursă» names the setting, and the cancellation lines (the Administrator's, the participant's) say that on «Nu» the place stays free.
- **«Ce NU se poate face»** gains: nobody gets a place without their own signature (a parent's, for a minor: until the new templates are approved the minor's own second signature stays off, §330) — an offer is accepted and signed by the person from their email, and «Dă-i un loc» confirms only on the paper declaration signed at the desk. The race-day «Nu s-a înscris deloc» says a walk-in also queues when somebody is already waiting, and that «Dă-i un loc» needs a free place.
- **The Organizer.** «Vezi cine s-a înscris» gains the places line as §615 left it: the first number counts the registrations holding a place in every state — the confirmed plus those still completing (a declaration not signed, an offer not accepted, a family's hold) — and after the dash the line names only the parts that exist, the confirmed, those in progress and the places kept for the waiting list, as in „6 înscriși din 10 locuri — 4 confirmați, 2 în curs de confirmare, 4 locuri păstrate pentru lista de așteptare” (composed from `Event.cta.fillParts`, `fillConfirmed`, `fillInProgress`, `fillKept` and `countForm`'s forms); the kept places are the free ones the waiting list claims, and a step of its own gives both cards the code shows beside them — more places free than people waiting: «Locurile se dau din lista de așteptare» and no free place counted (`Event.cta.fromWaitlist`); the list claiming every free place, as in the example: the full card's „Mulțumim! Toate cele 10 locuri s-au ocupat — … așteaptă deja un loc.” (`Event.cta.fullThanks`) and «Intră pe lista de așteptare» (`Event.cta.joinWaitingList`) while the line still names the kept places (`fillKept`) — and that in both the places are free, handed out by the club with «Trimite-i oferta» on «Nu» or by the queue on «Da»; why that first number and «Cine vine» differ (the people who asked to appear); and what „1 loc oferit din lista de așteptare” on the card is (§612). «Descarcă și tipărește numerele de concurs» gains the «Nr.» column as §613 ended: before the approval the Administrator writes to those already registered with «Trimite un mesaj participanților», and a runner who does not want to appear presses «Nu vreau să apar pe lista de participanți & rezultate» in «Înscrierile mele»; from the approval the column shows every confirmed runner who has a number, whichever notice they registered under, «—» only for one without. «Ce face Administratorul, nu tu» names the bulk resend and «Trimite-i oferta».
- **The legal texts.** «Textele legale ale clubului» gains two steps that switch the «Nr.» column on, in the order of the `/admin/tasks` row `listNumbersNotice` after the owner's «forțat» (§613): first the message to those already registered — «Evenimente» → «Deschide» → «Înscrierile primite» → «Trimite un mesaj participanților» — saying their number will appear and naming the withdrawal control «Nu vreau să apar pe lista de participanți & rezultate» in «Înscrierile mele»; then the approval — the «GDPR» card → «Regenerează din șablon» → the draft → «Salvează ciorna» → «Aprobă și publică» — after which the column shows every confirmed runner who has a number, «—» only for one without, and the «Sarcini» → «Club» row until then. It sits beside the list-states line already there, in the task that walks the notice's approval.
- **The costs (§610).** «Setări» → «Costuri» → «Cât costă», and «Planul Vercel» → «Salvează planul Vercel», are one step of the Administrator's Mailgun task: the costs tab opens to the Administrator and the Vercel plan is `canManageClubSettings`, so it is not a Superadministrator's step, and the «Bugetul lunii» thresholds task stays as it was.
- **The participant (§614, §615, §616).** «Înscrierea, de la formular la codul QR» no longer says the declaration is «pe pagina care se deschide»: after the confirmation the page says it comes by email, and the email's «Semnează declarația» leads to the box «Am citit și accept declarația…» and «Semnează», which now says under the box what is missing. «Locul și termenele lui» says a place may come by itself or be chosen by the club, by the «S-a eliberat un loc» email. «O familie pe o singură adresă» says a family reserves nothing while anybody waits.
- «Primii pași» → the top bar's «Emailuri» names the hourly limit, the Gmail routes and the sending queue.

**How it is held.** `guide-words.test.ts` already holds every «…» to a label the screen shows in each language and the two guides to the same shape; a new case pins the four Administrator jobs and the new hard limit, each by its button words, in both languages, with no «Rol necesar» line. The "i" beside a refused button is an icon, not a string, so it is quoted „i” rather than «i». Gmail's «Promoții»/"Promotions" tab is Google's, not ours, and is left unquoted.

**Review round (2026-10-01).** The citations follow the landing's numbers (§607–§617). The two numbers-column steps no longer say «—» for runners registered under an older notice: the owner's «forțat» made the column every confirmed runner's, and the steps now say what the tasks row says, in its order. The Organizer's places-line step no longer quotes the earlier two-part line: the first number is the registrations holding places in every state, and a third part names the places kept for the waiting list. The guide's text carries no § number.

**Second review round (2026-10-01).** The places-line step implied the card says «Locurile se dau din lista de așteptare» whenever places are kept for the waiting list. It says so only while the free places outnumber the people waiting (`capacity.ts` counts a newcomer's places as capacity less the occupied and the waiting; `registration-cta.ts` shows the waiting-list line only while some remain); when the list claims every free place — the step's own example — the call-to-action is FULL, «Mulțumim! Toate cele 10 locuri s-au ocupat — … așteaptă deja un loc.» beside „4 locuri păstrate pentru lista de așteptare”, which an Organizer reading «Ghid» could not explain. The step is split: the line and its example, then the kept places in both cases the code produces, then «Cine vine» and the offered place. The full card's sentence carries two numbers, so it is quoted „…” as an example with the waiting count left as an ellipsis, as the places line is.

*Rejected:* a separate «Mailgun» section — the jobs belong to the Administrator, whose section the reader already opens; describing the Gmail takeover, the public delay notice and the replaced-link page, which other branches carry and this tree does not; quoting the places line as «…» — its catalogue value begins with a placeholder, so it is quoted „…” as an example; and shortening any task that is still true.

Baseline `BR-V2.56-2026-10-01`.

## 621. The «Înscrieri» badge says it counts people, not places, and splits each event by who holds a place (amending §255 and §476)

**The owner, 2026-10-01, the race's first evening, with a phone screenshot of the tab reading «Înscrieri 153» while the race has 150 places and the list's summary read «Înscrieri: 154 · Așteaptă confirmarea emailului: 9»:** "Why does it say 153 when I said I want 150...", then "Why does it show 153?? When in have 150 max", then "Update that tooltip man", then "Putem îmbunătăți acel tooltip?".

**What was wrong.** Nothing in the number: 153 was right, the people with a registration in progress, nine of them awaiting the email confirmation and holding no place yet. The badge did not say so, and a figure beside a race with a limit reads as places.

**Decision.**

- The tooltip's first line says what the number is and is not: people with a registration in progress at the upcoming events, not places («Oameni cu o înscriere în curs la evenimentele viitoare — nu locuri. Cine așteaptă confirmarea emailului sau e pe lista de așteptare e numărat aici, dar nu ocupă încă un loc.»); in English an event reads «144 of 150 places taken», or «144 with a place» when it has no capacity.
- Each event's line carries the split: «Cursa: 153 — 144 cu loc din 150, 9 așteaptă confirmarea emailului» (the owner's case, no waiting list; with one, «, 2 pe lista de așteptare» follows and the parts still add up). «Cu loc» is what the allocator's `computeOccupied` counts as people: CONFIRMED, PENDING_DECLARATION, an offer not yet lapsed and a family's reservation (§543, a PENDING_EMAIL_CONFIRMATION row with an unexpired `hold_expires_at`), found by the repository's own predicates; the rest of PENDING_EMAIL_CONFIRMATION is «așteaptă confirmarea emailului», and an offer that lapsed and is not yet swept counts with the waiting list; «din C» only when the event has a capacity; a zero part is omitted except the places. Only `family_place_holds` rows, which carry no person, are not in the tooltip.
- Still one indexed query: the grouping gained the bucket (a handful of rows for a few dozen events), the same minute memo and the same `null` on failure. The total is still the sum of the split, so the pill and the tooltip cannot disagree. `registeredBadgeHint` stays pure and is tested against both catalogues; the «și încă N» tail and the five-event limit stay. No number meets a noun that inflects, so no `countForm` was needed.
- The registrations list's summary says its scope: «Înscrieri: 154 (toate stările, anulate și expirate incluse)». The panel's own title already says «toate evenimentele» or «la {event}», so the label says only the states, not the event twice. It is every real registration in every state, not places.
- The event's box «Înscrierile primite» adds «locuri ocupate: 144 din 150» when the event has a capacity, from the allocator's own `countOccupied` and `computeOccupied`, the number the public line and the queue panel read. That count has `kind` in no condition (a test row occupies a place exactly like a real one, §30), while «înscrieri reale» beside it leaves tests out; on production there are no test rows, so the two agree. The page reads `countOccupied` once and hands it to the queue panel as an optional `counts` prop, so the box's places cost no aggregate beyond the one the panel already ran, for every role that reads registrations; an event without a capacity skips the page's read and the panel queries as before (§621); no query per row. The grouped query names the bucket column by its position, which the select's comment pins.

**Refused.** Calling PENDING_EMAIL_CONFIRMATION a place (the allocator does not count it; §214's `PLACE_HOLDING_STATUSES` does, for a different question); hiding the awaiting-email people from the badge (they are real registrations in progress and the club wants them); touching the public pages, the desk or any state.

Baseline `BR-V2.56-2026-10-01`.

## 622. Email fail-safes: Gmail takes over while Mailgun says stop, no message is ever lost, and the operator has buttons instead of SQL (amending §40, §100, §163, §443 and BR-V2.53's section)

**The owner, 2026-10-01**, the evening of the probation, asked for three things: that Gmail take over by itself when Mailgun stops, that no email ever be lost to it, and that he have buttons for it instead of SQL. His words: «Pe viitor trebuie să avem fallbacks», «Trebuie să fixam astfel de lucruri pe viitor», «Mai ales pe failsafes de retrimitere mail».

**The day.** Mailgun put the club's account on probation — a hundred messages an hour, the account «temporarily disabled» for faster — on the morning registrations opened (§605). BR-V2.53 paced the outbox to the hour and made a rate refusal a pause. What it could not do was move the queue while Mailgun said stop: 148 rows waited, the owner released them by SQL from a phone, and set Gmail by hand for the groups that could not wait.

**What BR-V2.53 already did, and what it left.** It paces Mailgun's road to «Limita pe oră» under an advisory lock, gives a pause its attempt back, and holds Mailgun's whole road while a marked row's pause is not over. Its review left three nits: *the pause held the road only with a pace set* — a club that cleared «Limita pe oră» knocked through a pause; *a family sitting could move a paused row* — «Da» held it to the sitting's window (the pause stretched to it), «Gata» released it at once (the pause cut short); and *a pause's mark lived only on the refused row* — once that row left, the road read open. Beyond the nits: a transient refusal still reached FAILED after six attempts (about an hour), a refusal of the account (401, 403, an unverified domain) was BOUNCED like an unknown address, and the operator's only tools were the database console and a phone.

**Decision.**

1. *No email is lost to a refusal that is not about the message.* A transient refusal (5xx, timeout, network, 404) never reaches FAILED: past `MAX_SEND_ATTEMPTS` the row stays PENDING and is retried hourly (the backoff's own ceiling), its attempt count kept for the record. Such a row is counted by `/api/health` as `retryingLate`, inside «overdue» — a PENDING row whose `last_error` is a plain provider error (no stop mark, not Gmail's cap), past `MAX_SEND_ATTEMPTS` — the backoff's own trying — whatever its age, its turn scheduled within the hour — so a message stuck for days on a 5xx, or on a 404 from a wrong API base or domain, answers 503 and turns «Sarcini» red as the FAILED row did before; a row whose turn has already passed by the allowance stays in `late` (and `hourPaced`), never counted twice. FAILED is only a permanent refusal that is not about the address — 401, 403, a 400 that does not name the address or the recipient, or that names the sender's own `'from'` parameter (an unverified or closed domain, a bad `MAIL_FROM`, a malformed message), a message that cannot be rendered — and the adapter says so (`notTheAddress`); BOUNCED stays the address's own refusal. Why: a message is the club's promise to a runner, and an outage is the provider's problem, not the runner's.
2. *Gmail takes over automatically.* The email-transport setting gains `fallbackToGmail` — «Gmail preia când Mailgun se oprește», on by default where the Gmail road is configured (`CONTACT_SMTP_USER` and `CONTACT_SMTP_PASSWORD`) **and the privacy notice in force names it** (point 10), greyed with the reason otherwise; a value stored before the switch reads as on. While Mailgun's road is stopped — a pause it asked for, or its daily or monthly allowance spent — and the switch is on, the claim takes nothing from Mailgun's road and claims **every** group's due rows on Gmail's road, Gmail's own cap and pace unchanged; the rows Mailgun held back (the pause mark, or the new allowance mark `allowance spent: `) are due at once there, their `next_attempt_at` being Mailgun's deferral. Every row of such a batch leaves by Gmail alone (`gmailOnly`): at Gmail's cap, or with Gmail refusing the login, it is handed back with its attempt, marked «mailgun stopped, gmail could not carry it», due at Gmail's room or in fifteen minutes and never past Mailgun's return — never sent to Mailgun during its stop. The stop is recorded (`platform_settings.mailgunStop`, kept for whichever stop ends later), so the road stays closed after the refused row itself has left by Gmail; when the pause ends or the reset comes, Mailgun's groups return to Mailgun on their own. A Mailgun refusal met mid-batch closes the road for the rest of the batch, and the refused message itself spills to Gmail at once (the §443 overflow, on whenever the switch acts); the stop rides on whatever the spill ends with — sent, paced, an address Gmail refused, a connection that broke where Gmail may have taken it — and is recorded before the outcome is handled. When Gmail cannot carry a held row and relabels it «mailgun stopped, gmail could not carry it», the batch first writes the stop it carries for as the record, so the relabel never removes the stop's only witness. The `transport` column records the road each row left on, and every count already reads it. Off, BR-V2.53's road exactly. Why: a provider's stop is the provider's problem, not the runner's, and the club already has a second road.
3. *The pause holds the road even with no pace.* The claim takes the advisory lock and reads the stop — the marked rows and the record, one query — whenever it claims, «Limita pe oră» set or cleared.
4. *A family sitting cannot stretch or cut a pause.* Its hold and release statements leave a row carrying a Mailgun stop's mark at its turn (`notHeldByMailgun`). Its replace deletes such a row like any never-tried one: the stop is recorded apart from the row (`platform_settings.mailgunStop`), so its going ends no pause, and the person gets the family message alone, never both. «Da» on a first form whose email Mailgun has already paused still takes that email into the sitting (`heldOutboxIds`) — tracked, neither held to the window nor marked — so the second form's family message replaces it.
5. *«Trimite acum» during a stop says what it did.* With the switch on and room in Gmail's day it sends through Gmail and the page says «N prin Gmail — Mailgun în pauză până la HH:MM» (or «cota Mailgun epuizată până la …»); with the switch off, Gmail not configured or Gmail's cap spent it is refused with its own sentence naming the cause and the remedy, and the emails page adds when Mailgun reopens — never «0 trimise» in silence. `assertRoomToSendNow`, behind every resend's «now», reads the same facts: Gmail carries it, or the same refusal. The day's counter spent with no stop recorded yet is still refused for «now» (§100): on a paid plan Mailgun bills the overage rather than refusing, so the press must not assume Gmail will catch it; the next drain hands the rows to Gmail once Mailgun's own refusal records the stop. The registrations list's «Trimite acum» says all of it as the emails page does (how many by Gmail and until when; when Mailgun reopens, if refused). A press that goes ahead during a stop nobody carries — the switch off, a row due on Gmail's own road — returns the stop all the same (`stop`, `carriedByGmail: false`) — and so does a press during which Mailgun announces the stop with nothing to carry it (the switch off, the notice missing): the press reads the recorded stop back after its batches, and the list, which has no queue header, adds «Cele de pe drumul Mailgun rămân în coadă: Mailgun e oprit. Mailgun reia la HH:MM.».
6. *«Reîncearcă emailurile eșuate».* An Administrator's button on the queue panel (`canManageRegistrations`, asserted in the service): every FAILED row of the last seven days — health's window — back to PENDING, attempt count 0, due now, `last_error` kept; BOUNCED untouched; one audit row `email_outbox.retry_failed` with the count and who, never an address; three presses an hour, the refusal with its own sentence («Nu s-a pus nimic înapoi…»); the question shows the count read with the page. After it, the ordinary drain. Why: a button beats a console.
7. *The alarm names the remedy.* «Sarcini» gains the row «Emailuri pe care nu le duce nimeni»: red while a Mailgun-road row stopped (paused, deferred, or waiting because Gmail could not carry it) was queued more than ninety minutes ago with nothing carrying it, a transient refusal keeps a row retrying (`retryingLate`, point 1), or a FAILED row exists in the last seven days; its steps name the switch, Gmail's cap, the refusal that does not pass (`MAILGUN_API_BASE_URL`, `MAILGUN_DOMAIN`), «Reîncearcă emailurile eșuate» and «Limita pe oră»; a row waiting because Gmail could not carry it counts only while a stop is in force that nothing carries — once the stop has ended it is back on Mailgun's road, judged as any waiting row (`late`, `hourPaced`), and counted once; green otherwise, and always on the list. `/api/health?deep=1`'s email block says the stop, until when and who carries for it; its status is `degraded` while Gmail carries every group, and `stalled` — the 503 the cron-job.org monitor emails the owner about, as before — once a row has waited ninety minutes with nothing to carry it. The email block's `degraded` does not move the endpoint's own status: a 503 every time Mailgun pauses for a quarter of an hour would email the owner about the platform doing what it was built to do. The queue panel's header says «Mailgun în pauză până la HH:MM — Gmail preia», «Cota Mailgun epuizată … — Gmail preia» or «… — Gmail nu e configurat», in both languages.
8. *Saving «Planul Mailgun» reopens the road.* An allowance stop is recorded until the next UTC reset, and a club that upgrades mid-day (§100) has the allowance back. Saving the plan deletes the `mailgunStop` record when it is of kind allowance and makes the allowance-marked waiting rows due now, in the same transaction, so the next claim sends on Mailgun's road instead of Gmail's capped day; a pause Mailgun asked for is not the plan's and stays. The operator has the button he already uses, never SQL.
9. *The newsletter is not Gmail's to carry.* During a stop the carried claim leaves `NEWSLETTER` and `NEW_EVENT_ALERT` on Mailgun's road, and the forced overflow does not spill them, unless the club itself routed that group to Gmail: §443 kept them off a personal Gmail because Google restricts bulk, and a restricted account would also stop the club's copies and the contact form. A bulk row met by a stop that begins mid-batch is handed back to wait for Mailgun, attempt given back. On a race morning the newsletter waits for Mailgun's return; the confirmations do not.
10. *The fallback waits for a notice that says so.* §443 kept participants' mail on Mailgun because the privacy notice names Mailgun as the sender and Gmail only as the club's mailbox; the switch sends a participant's name, single-use links and signed PDF through Google. So the privacy-notice template gains a sentence in section 6, both languages — when the club's email provider refuses or delays sending, a message may leave through the club's Gmail mailbox (Google Ireland Ltd.) with the same content and data, for the same purpose and on the same basis — carrying the merge field `{{gmailFallback}}`, filled with the switch's own words quoted (`fallback-notice-words.ts`), listed in the editor's legend. `fallbackActive` is true only while the notice in force names the field in every language (`noticeDescribesGmailFallback`, read by the claim's roads, the sender, `/api/health`, the emails page and «Sarcini»; the outbox reads it only where the switch could act, and no public page reads it, so it has no cached twin), the stored switch is not off (absent = on) and Gmail is configured. Until then the panel shows the switch greyed «Oprit până la aprobarea notei din șablonul nou…», a stop waits with its own reason (`noticeMissing`: the queue header «Gmail nu preia: nota de confidențialitate în vigoare nu o spune încă», «Trimite acum» refused with the sentence that names the notice), and «Sarcini» carries the row `gmailFallbackNotice` — what to approve and why — green once the notice in force names the field. Why: the repository's pattern for a feature that needs a disclosure (§396, §562), and §10.8: never send a person's data where the notice in force does not say it goes.

**Kept.** One claim and one send path (`claimOutboxBatch`, `processOutboxBatch`); BR-V2.53's pace, lock and pause semantics, but for point 3; Gmail's cap (at most 500) and pace; no new provider; `kind` in no condition; the adapter's sanitizer the one boundary for `last_error` (the audit carries counts only); server-asserted authorization; both message files, the same keys, no ICU plural. No migration: the switch lives in the transport setting's JSON, the stop in a `platform_settings` row.

**What it does not settle.** Whether the club's lawyer wants more than section 6's sentence; the club approves the notice from the template, and until it does Mailgun's stop holds participants' mail as BR-V2.53 did. QA shares the Gmail account and has the same default, inside its own smaller cap, once QA's notice names the field.

**Amends** §40 (a transient refusal is not FAILED after six attempts; a permanent 400 that is not about the address is FAILED, not BOUNCED), §100 (the plan's deferral is carried by Gmail with the switch on), §163 (QA's Gmail switch acts on QA's own queue, with QA's smaller cap), §443 (a group's road is the club's choice except while Mailgun is stopped, the switch is on and the notice in force names `{{gmailFallback}}`; the overflow is on with the switch) and §605 (the pause holds the road without a pace, and is recorded beyond the refused row).

**Tests.** Unit `notifications/mailgun-stop.test.ts`: the classification (a transient refusal hourly past six attempts, 401/403 and a non-address 400 FAILED, an address problem BOUNCED), the marks, a stop in force, the switch read from an old value, the retry instant, and the route decision — stopped × switch on/off × Gmail's room or none × Gmail configured or not. Unit `notifications/outbox-queue-panel.test.ts`: the header carried, not carried and absent, both languages, another day's hour; the retry button with its count, asking first, for whoever may send. Unit `diagnostics/owner-tasks.test.ts`: the row red and green. Integration `notifications/email-fail-safes.test.ts` (PGlite): Mailgun paused with the switch on — the paused and fresh rows claimed on Gmail's road and sent with `transport = gmail`, Mailgun never asked; a pause met mid-batch recorded, the road kept closed after the refused row left by Gmail, Mailgun's again when the pause ends; the switch off — nothing moves on Mailgun's road, Gmail's own group still goes; the allowance — deferred rows leave on Gmail, a live 420 marks and records and the rest go by Gmail, with the switch off nothing held back; Gmail's cap spent — rows held to Mailgun's return with their attempts and not retaken at once; the pause with `hourlyAllowance: null` and on the record alone; a transient refusal PENDING past eight attempts with an hourly turn; FAILED versus BOUNCED; «Trimite acum» sending through Gmail with its counts and audit, refused with the cap's and the switch's sentences; a resend's «now» in the same states; a paused newsletter row stays PENDING while a confirmation leaves by Gmail; saving the plan reopens Mailgun's road after an allowance stop; the retry verb (FAILED → PENDING, BOUNCED and an old FAILED untouched, the audit row, three an hour, FORBIDDEN for an Organizer); health `degraded` while carried, `stalled` with `stoppedLong` when nothing carries for ninety minutes; a row Gmail could not carry stalled while the stop is in force and uncarried, and not once the stop has ended and the hour is paced (counted once); `retryingLate`: a row past six transient attempts with its turn minutes ahead stalled with its reason, a third attempt not, an old row refused twice not (counted by attempts, not age) and stalled once past six; a spill Gmail refused for the address still records the pause and holds the batch's next Mailgun row; the relabel keeps the stop in force; the notice gate — no carrying, `noticeMissing` on volume, health and «Trimite acum» while the notice does not name the field, carrying with it, not with the switch off; «Trimite acum» with the switch off returning the stop with `carriedByGmail: false`, also when Mailgun pauses during the press. Unit `notifications/gmail-fallback-notice.test.ts`: the merge field, the legend, the clause, section 6's sentence in both languages; `mailgun-stop.test.ts`: the gate in its three states and `noticeMissing`'s order; `email-fail-safes-sender.test.ts`: the stop carried on a permanent and a possibly-accepted spill; `owner-tasks.test.ts`: `gmailFallbackNotice` open and done, `emailFailSafe` red for `retryingLate`. Unit `notifications/email-fail-safes-sender.test.ts` (stub adapters and ledger): `gmailOnly` at Gmail's cap and with Gmail down handed back and Mailgun never called; a 429 and a 420 spilled to Gmail carrying `mailgunStopped` (paused, allowance); a bulk message never spilled; `mailgun-stop.test.ts` also the refused `'from'` parameter FAILED. Integration `notifications/outbox.test.ts`: the attempt ceiling no longer FAILS a transient refusal. Integration `registrations/family-sitting.test.ts`: «Da», a second «Da» and «Gata» leave a paused row's turn as it was, and the family message replaces a paused first email (one message, never both), also when Mailgun paused it before «Da» was pressed. Concurrency: the claim now takes `pg_advisory_xact_lock` on every claim, not only with a pace set, and reads the stop under it (point 3); `yarn test:concurrency` (all six files, `hourly-pace.test.ts` among them) passed against the implementer's own database with that change. E2E `email-plan.spec.ts`: the switch on the emails page, compiled, not run.

**The review of the third round, 2026-10-01.** Four findings, all answered. *A first email Mailgun paused before «Da» was lost to the sitting:* the seed's hold had gained the stop's guard, so a paused seed was neither held nor returned, never reached `heldOutboxIds`, and the second form's family message did not replace it — the person would have had both, which point 4 rules out. The seed's tracking is now apart from its hold: the still-waiting, never-tried seed row is always the sitting's, and only a row no stop marks is moved to the window and marked. *The remedy named a variable that does not exist:* `MAILGUN_API_BASE_URL`, in both catalogues, point 7 and the test. *`retryingLate` counted age:* a row queued long ago and refused once rang for about ninety minutes and then went quiet in `late`, which the pace exempts; the orchestrator's decision — counted by attempts alone, past `MAX_SEND_ATTEMPTS`, whatever the age (point 1). *A stop announced during «Trimite acum» with nothing to carry it went unsaid:* the batch records the stop but carries nothing, so the press now reads the stop back after its batches when they deferred anything, and the list says «Mailgun reia la HH:MM» (point 5).

*Rejected:* the newsletter on Gmail during a stop — one bulk send could restrict the account the club's copies and the contact form depend on, and use up the 200-recipient day that confirmations need; a second SMTP provider — one more account, key and bill to keep; an automatic plan upgrade at Mailgun — money nobody reverses (§100); dropping the club's copies during a stop — they are the club's record of what was sent; a per-row transport override written by staff — a road is the setting's, not a row's.

Baseline `BR-V2.56-2026-10-01`.

## 623. The public pages say when the club's emails are late — how many wait, how long, and that the deadline runs from the send (amending §513 and §547)

**The owner, 2026-10-01:** «In caz că mai pică sau avem coadă de mailuri, userii trebuie să vadă».

**The day it answers.** On the day registrations opened, Mailgun's probation held the club's mail for hours (§605). The outbox lost nothing — a refusal is a pause, a spent hour waits — but nobody waiting for an email could tell: the screen after the form kept saying «pleacă la 10:15» (§536), the resend form «în cel mult 15 minute» (§513). People wrote to the club to say they were waiting, and some filled the form in a second time. `/api/health` and `/admin/tasks` knew (§98, §605); the person in front of the page did not.

**Decision.** The pages that wait for an email say, while it lasts, that the club's emails are late — how many messages wait, the oldest's wait, at most how long more when the platform can tell, and that the deadline runs from the moment the email leaves.

1. **One read, cached, public.** `notifications/public-delay.ts` → `readEmailDelay(db, now)` returns `{ late, reason, queued, oldestWaitMinutes, estimateMinutes }`, judged by one pure function (`domain/email-delay.ts`, `judgeEmailDelay`). It counts the messages a person waits for: not sent, due, being sent or held by a provider — never the newsletter or the new-event alert (they wait for the allowance by design, §445), never the club's own copies and archives, never a colleague's or a member's invitation, never a row the club holds for a family's window (§519), whose screen already named the hour. **The family's hold is told by its own markers, never by a row's shape**: the payload flags `sittingHeld` (a held verification email) and `familyHeld` (any other held message), as the queue panel reads them (`queue.ts`), and the family's one confirmation — the `REGISTRATION_CONFIRMED` that names its sitting (`familySittingId`) — each while its not-before is ahead and no provider gave it a reason; the club's copies carry the participant's payload, and so the same marks. Every other unsent row counts, from its `created_at`: a row Gmail's pace handed to the next run, a paused batch's batch-mates (handed back with no reason, exactly as before — `releaseForPause` writes nothing on them, so `/admin/emails` and `/api/health` read what they read before), a deferral, a retry. A hand-off never restarts a row's wait; only a family's row, its hold over, waits from the instant it was let go, because that is the hour the person was told — whatever came after, a failed attempt included. **That instant is recorded, never read off `next_attempt_at`**: a failed attempt rewrites the not-before to the retry's turn, usually ahead, so a row released half an hour ago and failing since would read a wait of nothing on every view, and `backlog` would never speak for that family. The family's path writes `heldUntil` (an ISO instant, `FAMILY_HELD_UNTIL`) into the payload in the same statement as every not-before it sets — the first form's message «Da» takes in (`holdSeedMessage`), «Da» moving the window, each form's settling of the sitting's held messages and the family message, a held verification email, a kept form's held message, the family's held declaration requests and its one confirmation (moved with each signature) — and «Gata» rewrites it to now; the club's copies carry the participant's payload. These are payload-only writes on the family path: the outbox's own writes — the claim, a retry, a pause, a deferral — are byte for byte what they were. A marked row then waits from `greatest(created_at, heldUntil)`: a sitting email released a minute ago and failing once reads a minute, one released thirty minutes ago and failing since reads thirty and is `backlog`. A marked row queued before this deploys has no `heldUntil` and keeps the earlier rule — its not-before while no provider gave it a reason, else its creation — which over-reports a failed one's wait by at most one hold window, and only for the rows already in the queue that day; the hold's exclusion (`clubHold`) still reads the not-before and the markers (the rule is the markers' alone; an unmarked row always counts from its creation). *Rejected:* inferring the hold from `last_error IS NULL AND next_attempt_at > created_at` — the pace's hand-off has the same shape, so every hand-off reset that row's wait and dropped it from the count, and on a Gmail backlog the notice stayed silent exactly when it should speak; and a mark written on the batch-mates (`last_error`) — it showed in red on `/admin/emails` as the provider's answer, in English, which it was not, and `/api/health` could name it as the reason instead of the refused row's. What the markers leave: a family's row that a pace or a pause hands back after its hold is, for those seconds or that pause, read as still held — the rest of its batch still counts, so the notice still speaks. It is **late** when (a) Mailgun has paused its road (§605) and one of them rides it — `paused`; (b) Mailgun's hour is spent with one of them on its road, or a provider put one off to its allowance's reset — `allowance`; or (c) the oldest has waited longer than the wait the platform promises (`emailWaitMinutes`, §513: the pinger's tick under `scheduled`, nothing under `immediate`) plus ten minutes — `backlog`. The reason named is the dominant one, in that order: a stopped road explains a backlog. The estimate is a ceiling and never optimistic: a spent hour leaves nothing until its first place frees (`hourFreesAt`, the oldest send in the 61-minute window plus the window, read in the same query), so it is that wait plus the queue at the pace (`waiting on Mailgun's road ÷ hourly allowance × 60`); a pause is its end (or the hour's freeing, if later) plus the queue at the pace when more waits than an hour carries; a deferral is the reset; a backlog while the pace binds is the queue at the pace; unknown otherwise. **Each known estimate then adds the scheduler's tick** — the promised wait, the pinger's tick under `scheduled`, nothing under `immediate` — because when a pause ends, an hour frees or an allowance resets, nothing leaves until the next run (`wakeJobs` only forgets the cached quiet): a pause ending at 01:05 under the hourly night cadence is «cel mult 65 de minute», not 5; a queue at the pace ends at a run too, so it carries the tick whether it fits in one pass or several. **The tick is the cadence at the instant waited for, not at the visitor's** (`judgeEmailDelay` takes a `promisedWaitAt(instant)`; the page passes `pingerCadenceMinutes(instant)` under `scheduled`, nothing under `immediate`): the allowance resets at 02:05 or 03:05 club time, always in the hourly quiet hours, so a daytime visitor sees reset + 60, not reset + 15; a pause or an hour freeing that crosses 23:00 is the same, and one ending by day keeps the day tick. The queue at the pace drains over the coming runs, so it keeps the tick of now. Rounded up to five minutes and never under five, because «cel mult» is a ceiling and a precise number would read as a promise. The numerator counts every non-newsletter row on Mailgun's road, the club's copies too: they ride the same hour.

   **Why ten minutes.** The promise is already the scheduler's tick; a run takes a minute or two, a retry's first backoff is a minute, and the pinger is a few minutes late at times. Ten minutes past the promise is a wait no schedule explains, and still well before a person gives up and registers again — the one thing the notice exists to stop. `/api/health`'s ninety minutes (§98) answer another question: when a person must be woken, not when a visitor should be told.

   **One query, a minute at most.** The facts are one statement: the outbox grouped by message type and club-copy flag, with the email plan and the transport setting as two scalar sub-selects beside them, classified in memory into the roads (§443) and the hour (§605) exactly as the claim reads them. `public-cache/reads.ts` → `cachedEmailDelay(now)` serves it from the data cache under its own tag, `public:email`, for sixty seconds (`publicRead` gained a shorter ceiling for it, stretched by the month's budget like the day's); the judgement runs per render against the cached promise (`cachedEmailWaitMinutes`). No last good copy is kept: an old «emailurile întârzie» is as wrong as an old silence, so a page that cannot ask says nothing. The outbox expires the tag once at the end of `processOutboxBatch` when the batch sent, deferred (a pause, a spent allowance), gave up on a message or withdrew one unsent — never per row, and not for a batch that claimed nothing or only scheduled a retry.

2. **The words**, Romanian and English, from `messages/*.json` (`Delay`), plurals by `countForm`: «Emailurile noastre întârzie acum: 23 de mesaje așteaptă, cel mai vechi așteaptă de 47 de minute; estimăm cel mult 30 de minute. Al tău pleacă când îi vine rândul — termenul lui curge de când pleacă, nu de acum. Nu te înscrie din nou.» / “Our emails are running late: 23 messages are waiting, the oldest for 47 minutes; we estimate at most 30 minutes. Yours leaves in its turn — its deadline runs from the moment it leaves, not from now. Do not register again.” The estimate clause is left out when unknown. A wait past ninety minutes is said in whole hours, never in hundreds of minutes: «cel mai vechi așteaptă de peste 4 ore; estimăm cel mult 24 de ore» (the oldest rounded down with «peste», the estimate rounded up). **Three shapes, by what the page's own email carries.** The full text (above) is for the pages whose email starts a deadline at its send: the screen after the form, the address confirmed, the family's links — and, closed by what the page itself asked for rather than by a registration nobody there made, «Înscrierile mele» («… Nu cere din nou linkul.» / “… Do not ask for the link again.”) and the newsletter's confirmation («… Nu te abona din nou.» / “… Do not subscribe again.”). The resend form says «Al tău pleacă când îi vine rândul. Termenul din primul tău email curge de când a plecat acela, nu de acum.» — a resend starts no deadline (§513's re-base moves nothing for it), so it does not say the new one's deadline restarts. The pages whose email carries no deadline (the newsletter's way out, the race declaration's done page, the group run's done page) say only «Al tău pleacă când îi vine rândul.», with no deadline and no «do not register again». **Why the full text names the deadline rule:** the fear that makes a person register again is that the link will expire before it arrives; §513's re-base already starts every deadline an email carries at its send, so the sentence only says what is true, and it is what makes waiting safe. The short line, for a person who has not asked for anything yet: «Confirmarea pe email întârzie azi; estimăm cel mult 30 de minute.» / “The confirmation email is running late today; …”. An MUI warning `Alert`, `data-testid="email-delay"`; nothing to press, so no client island.

3. **Where.** The full notice on every page that waits for an email, above the page's own wait sentence: the screen after the form (both shapes, §536), the resend form (its own shape) and «Înscrierile mele» once sent, the newsletter's two answers (the way out in the plain shape), the family's confirmation page (each answer that sends), the group-run declaration's done page and the race declaration's done page (plain), and the address-confirmed page. **Not the interest form's answer:** it only stores the address; the email comes weeks later, when the window opens, so nothing is in the queue for that person. The short line under the event page's registration button (open, or the waiting list's) and under the form's send button — never in the editor's preview, never where the club has no button. **Nothing is rendered when nothing is late**: each page's markup is then byte for byte its markup without the notice — a test cuts the notice out of the late page and compares. The notice is awaited by the page that draws it (`emailDelayNotice`, like `registrationForm`), not nested as an async component, so the tree stays one a synchronous render draws. **The event page is static (§549)**: its line reads the same facts under a key of its own at the day's ceiling, because a minute's entry would hold the whole page to a minute (`page-lifetime.ts`) — every event page rendered again each minute somebody looks. The `email` tag still expires that entry, and the page with it, at every batch that moves the queue; what the page misses until its own clock is a queue that stalls with no batch running at all. The pages that wait for an email are rendered per request and read the minute's entry.

4. **Nothing else moves.** The outbox's sending, pacing and deadlines are unchanged — not one column it writes, and nothing it reads: the family's path adds one payload key beside its marker (`heldUntil`, above), read by the notice alone (§513's re-base already starts a deadline at the send — the notice only says so); no admin screen changes; `/api/health` is unchanged.

**The cost.** At most one query a minute while somebody looks at a page that waits for an email, none while the entry is warm; the event page re-renders when a batch moves the queue, as it does when a registration moves its places.

**Tests.** Unit: `notifications/email-delay.test.ts` — the thresholds under both timings, the three reasons and their order, the estimate's arithmetic (a spent hour waits for its first place, a pause for its end, each plus the scheduler's tick: a 60-minute tick and a pause ending in five minutes is 65; unchanged under `immediate`), what counts. Integration (PGlite): `notifications/email-delay.test.ts` — seeded rows make the read late or not for each reason; a batch Mailgun paused still counts all its rows from their creation, with no mark on the batch-mates; a three-row batch paused for two hours leaves the batch-mates' `last_error` null and `/api/health` naming the refused row's reason; a Gmail-road row created an hour ago and handed off by the pace two minutes ago is `backlog` with an oldest wait of 60; an unmarked row with a future turn counts; the newsletter, the club's copies and a family's held row (by either kind of marker, club copies included) never count, and a released family row waits from the `heldUntil` its release wrote — a minute after one failed attempt with its retry ahead, thirty minutes and `backlog` after three — while a held one (`heldUntil` ahead) is left out and a marked row without it follows the earlier rule; and `processOutboxBatch` expires the tag once when it sends or pauses and not when it does nothing or only retries. Integration: `registrations/family-sitting.test.ts` — `heldUntil` written at the hold, moved with the window and with each signature, rewritten to now at «Gata». Unit: `public-cache/email-delay-cache.test.ts` — the minute's ceiling and the tag, the kept render's own key at the day's ceiling, null when the queue cannot be read. Render: `registrations/email-delay-notice.test.ts` — every listed page with the notice when late, above its wait sentence, and byte-identical markup when not, in both languages, each page in its own shape, the interest answer with none, and a long wait in hours; `registrations/email-delay-short-line.test.ts` — the event page's box and the form's line. No Playwright assertion: the quiet markup is pinned byte for byte by the render tests, and an e2e check would depend on the e2e database's outbox holding no waited-for row older than the promise plus ten minutes, which no spec guarantees.

*Rejected:* **a site-wide banner** — a visitor who is not waiting for anything should not be told the club's emails are late; **a live countdown** — a client island for a sentence, and a number ticking down reads as a promise; **writing the delay into the emails themselves** — the person who has not received the email cannot read it.

This amends §513 (the pages that state the wait now also say when it is broken) and §547 (the family's screens carry the notice above their own sentences).

Baseline `BR-V2.56-2026-10-01`.

## 624. The event's reminder can go four or five days before the start (amending §377)

The owner, 2026-10-01, from his phone: «De asemenea, pentru remiminderul evenimeukui, vreau și opțiunea de 4 și 5 zile ca să pot da sansa oamenilor care nu mai ajuns să elibereze locul pt alții».

**Why.** The reminder goes once to the confirmed and carries «Nu mai pot veni»; the earlier it goes, the more time a person who cannot come has to free the place for the waiting list.

**Decision.** `EVENT_REMINDER_CHOICES` is now 24, 48, 72, 96 and 120 hours, so the event editor's «Reminderul dinaintea startului» offers «cu 4 zile înainte de start» / "4 days before the start" and the same for 5. The words need no change: `leadPhrase` already says a whole number of days as days (a unit test pins 96 and 120 in both languages). A lead outside the list (a number a script stored, or the club's own default) is still added to the dropdown as it is. No migration: `events.reminder_hours_before` already allows 0–168. Criterion 63 of 2026-09-25, which lists 24, 48 or 72 hours, is superseded by this list. When the email is sent (`reminderHoursFor`, `eventReminderDueAt`) is untouched.

Baseline `BR-V2.56-2026-10-01`.

## 625. The race number's column is headed «BIB», not «Nr.» (amending §613)

**The owner:** "Aici în loc de Nr. Scrie BID, ăsta e termenul tehnic" (BIB, as the brief spells the term).

**Decision.** The public list's race-number column (`Event.startList.columnNumber`) and the desk's printable confirmed list (`columnBib`) are headed «BIB» in both languages, the technical term the backoffice already uses («Număr de concurs (BIB)»). The accessible full name stays `columnNumberFull`, «numărul de concurs» / «race number», and so does the legal merge value `listNumbersClause`, which names the column by its full words; the legal templates' visible text is untouched. The two guide texts and the two task texts that describe the column say «BIB», and the code comments that named it «Nr.» now name «BIB». BR-REQ-039-01 criterion 24 is amended to the new heading.

**Refused.** Keeping «Nr.»: it abbreviates a Romanian word, while «BIB» is what runners, timekeepers and the backoffice call the number. Changing the full accessible name: «numărul de concurs» is what a screen reader and the notice should say in words.

Baseline `BR-V2.57-2026-10-02`.

## 626. The «Înscrieri» badge counts the confirmed with the waiting beside it, and the summary's pills are filters (amending §255, §476, §621 and §246)

**The owner, 2026-10-01, the race's first evening**, on the tab that read 167 while the list's summary read 168 and 133 were confirmed: the badge should be the confirmed count, and beside it «pune pilluri cu iconițe și cu numerele» for the people waiting; then, looking at the list's summary strip, «Și aceste pilluri trebuie sa fie clickable (filtre)».

**What was wrong.** §621 made the tooltip say that the badge counts people with a registration in progress, not places. That was honest and still wrong for a club that reads the tab as «câți sunt siguri»: 167 mixed the 133 who are confirmed, the 10 who wait and 24 in between (awaiting the email, the signature, an offer), and the strip's pills below it, which say the same states one by one, could be read but not used: to see the ten on the waiting list a person had to open the filter fold and choose a state.

**Decision — Part A, the tab.**

- The badge number is the people with a **CONFIRMED** registration, real ones, at the upcoming events the breakdown already covers (not cancelled, not past, `kind` REAL; a test registration is in no figure, §12.6).
- Beside it a second, smaller pill: the waiting list's hourglass (the glyph `queue` wears on the «Coada» panel and the line title, registered as `waiting` in `shared/ui/action-icons.ts`, §318: one glyph table, no new import in a component) and the number of people waiting. Drawn only above zero; outlined in the club's secondary colour so it reads as the lesser figure; `role="img"` with the words «10 pe lista de așteptare» for a screen reader (the glyph and the number are drawn only). Both pills sit in the one focusable chunk the tooltip hangs on. At 320 pixels the tab bar is `variant="scrollable"`, so the pill lengthens the row, never the page; a rendered-markup test holds the pill's shape, and nothing was measured in a browser. No fallback to one badge was needed.
- «Waiting» is the allocator's bucket and not the bare WAITLISTED status: an offer that has lapsed and not yet been swept holds no place and is going back to the list, so it counts there, as the tooltip's per-event line has counted it since §621. The three figures — confirmed, waiting and **in progress** (everybody else with an active registration: awaiting the email, awaiting the signature, an unlapsed offer, a family's reservation) — add up to the old total, so nobody is dropped by the change and the tooltip cannot disagree with the tab.
- The tooltip's first line is the three figures in one line, replacing §621's sentence: «Confirmați: 133 · pe lista de așteptare: 10 · în curs: 24» («Confirmed: 133 · on the waiting list: 10 · in progress: 24»). The per-event lines stay as §621 wrote them («Cursa: 153 — 144 cu loc din 150, 9 așteaptă confirmarea emailului»); «cu loc» still includes the confirmed, so the two read the same people. No noun meets a number that inflects, so no `countForm`.
