- Still one grouped query with the one-minute memo: the bucket expression gained a `confirmed` branch (the confirmed split out of «place»), `RegisteredOnEvent` gained `confirmed`, and `registeredBadgeBreakdown` returns `{ total, confirmed, waitlisted, inProgress, events }`, each a sum of the split. `registeredBadgeHint` takes those figures and its `rule` word is a function of the three numbers. `countRegisteredForUpcoming` stays: it is the whole the three must add up to.

**Decision — Part B, the summary's pills.**

- Every pill of the «Cine s-a înscris» strip is a link to the same page with `status=<RegistrationStatus>` in the address, server-rendered (`SummaryStrip`, a Server Component; each pill a `ChipLink`, an `<a>` with the whole query, no island of its own, working with JavaScript off, like the start list's paging §250). The state in force is drawn pressed (filled, `color="primary"`, `aria-current="page"`) and links to the page without `status`, so a second press clears it; the total pill («Înscrieri: 168 …») links to the page without it too, and is the pressed one while no state is chosen. The pill of the state in force is drawn even when nobody is in it, so the filter that emptied the list can be pressed off. A press keeps the reader where they are (`keepScroll`): the list under the strip is what changes.
- `summaryPillHref(basePath, current, status | null)` (`registrations/domain/summary-filter-links.ts`) is pure and keeps an **allowlist** of the list's own keys — the event, the search, club-member, bounced, offers, the sort and the page size — and drops everything else: `saved`, `error`, `cancelled`, `erased`, `failed`, `sent`, `erase` (which would reopen the erase panel), `marked`, `voided`, `test`, `until`, `stop`, `gmail`, `held` and the page number (a filter lands on the first page). An allowlist, because a list of what to drop needs a new row for every message a screen invents.
- The strip stays blind to the status filter (§246): the page still groups without it, so no count moves when a pill is pressed. The test rows' pill stays a label: `kind` is no status. The «Caută și filtrează» select reads the same address through the page's own `isRegistrationStatus` (an unreadable `status` shows «Toate» there and presses no pill, instead of a value the select has no option for), and its fold opens and says «filtre active» while a state is chosen, as for every other filter (§269). **The form is keyed by the address the list was resolved from** (`key={listQueryString}`): a pill is a soft `next/link` navigation, the page's client tree stays mounted, and MUI's select reads its `defaultValue` once, so without the key the select kept saying «Toate» after a pill was pressed and the next «Filtrează» sent `status=` and dropped the state the pill had set. A new address is a new form; every field (the search, the event, the club-member, bounced and offers filters, the state) starts from what the address says, after a pill, after «Șterge» and after a toggle-off alike. `ChipLink` gained a `wrap` flag so the total's long sentence wraps at 320 pixels instead of being cut.
- Authorization is unchanged: the links lead to the same page under the same role checks.

**Refused.** Keeping the old badge and adding the confirmed beside it (two numbers for one tab is the confusion §621 spent a tooltip on); counting the bare WAITLISTED status and leaving the lapsed offer in no figure (the three would no longer add up, and a person would vanish between them); a client island for the pills or a `router.push` (the strip is a link, and a link is what survives a reload and a bookmark); carrying every query key a link was built with (the flash messages would come back); a new icon import in the tab (the registry is the one table).

**Tests.** Integration `registrations/nav-count.test.ts`: the confirmed figure and the waiting figure with a test row, a cancelled row and a past event in neither, the lapsed offer among the waiting, the three summing to the total, the per-event `confirmed` and the `withPlace` that still contains it, a zero waiting list; the hint's words in both locales with the owner's figures. Unit `registrations/summary-filter-links.test.ts`: the allowlist, the toggle, the total, an unreadable state, empty values. Unit `registrations/summary-strip.test.ts`: rendered markup, every pill an anchor with the expected href, the pressed one, the counts unchanged across pressed states, the zero state in force drawn, no script or button. Unit `staff/admin-tabs-waiting-pill.test.ts`: the pill's glyph, number, name, only above zero, inside the tooltip's chunk. `shared/action-icons.test.ts` holds that `waiting` is used and names no other glyph. End to end, `promo-filter.spec.ts` (320 pixels on the mobile project, the laptop on the other): a state pill narrows the rows, is `aria-current`, measures 44 pixels, leaves no sideways scroll; the select's value follows it; «Filtrează» keeps the state; a second press clears it and the select says «Toate» again. That step is what a rendered-markup test of the strip alone cannot see.

Baseline `BR-V2.57-2026-10-02`.

## 627. «Coada de înscrieri» says when each waiting person sent the form, and lists them in that order when the club hands places out by hand

**The owner, 2026-10-01:** "Problema e că mulți au stat să confirme mailul… au căutat în SPAM și s-au înscris mulți în același timp" — many sent the form together and confirmed their address late, after looking for the email in Spam, so the line (`waitlisted_at`, the moment the address was confirmed and the place refused) no longer follows the order the forms were sent in. "E ok să aștepte, ei nu vor afla când s-au înscris restul pe listă și noi putem alege pe cine să luăm din listă" — the club hands places out by hand (`events.waitlist_auto_offer` «Nu», §615), choosing from the list, and nobody else learns when the rest registered. The panel did not show the order the forms were sent in: it listed the line by `waitlisted_at` and wrote only that moment.

**Decision.**

1. **The time, on every waiting row.** A `WAITLISTED` row of «Coada de înscrieri» (the event page's queue panel) says «Formular trimis: {when}» / «Form sent: {when}» beside the moment the person joined the line (`waitlisted_at`), now labelled «pe listă din {when}» / «on the list since {when}» (it read «din {when}», unlabelled). **«Sent» is the current cycle's:** `greatest(submitted_at, privacy_acknowledged_at)`, the rule the journey column already uses (`domain/journey.ts`, `formSentAt`). A restart (a registration cancelled or expired and then sent again, as the late confirmers may do after their link lapses) rewrites `privacy_acknowledged_at` and never `submitted_at` (`service.ts`, `carriedFields`), so the raw `submitted_at` would date the second form by the first and put that person at the head of the hand-picked order. The registration page's timeline reads the same value. Both times go through `formatDay` in the event's own zone (§349, §369), like every other time on the panel — the club's zone for an event held in Romania. The registration's own backoffice page already carried both in its timeline («Pe lista de așteptare», and the form's time under «Trimisă»); the form's label is now «Formular trimis» / «Form sent» so the two screens say it alike. The panel's reader and the page are the Administrator's and the Organizer's, as before; the desk's rows are untouched.

2. **The order, by the setting.** `queueOrderFor(waitlistAutoOffer)` (`domain/waitlist.ts`, a pure function) picks the order the panel lists the line in: `SUBMITTED` — the form's time as above, then `id` — when the event's offers are off and the club picks by hand; `LINE` — `waitlisted_at ASC, id ASC`, `lockOldestWaitlisted`'s own order — when they are on, so the panel never shows an order the allocator will not honour. `listQueueForEvent` takes the order as a required argument. A lead line above the rows says which is shown: «În ordinea trimiterii formularului…» / «În ordinea intrării pe listă…». The open offers sit in the same list in the same order (they are part of the line, §92); only a `WAITLISTED` row carries the two times.

3. **Display only.** The allocator, the capacity formula, `lockOldestWaitlisted` and every automatic offer are untouched; `kind` is in no new condition; no migration.

4. **Never public.** The owner's «ei nu vor afla când s-au înscris restul pe listă»: the form's time is a backoffice line, for the club that chooses. The public list's select (`listPublicStartListOthers`) is not widened and `tests/privacy/public-surface.test.ts` stays as it was; the participant's own pages show nobody else's time.

**Refused.** Ordering and dating by the raw `submitted_at`, the first form ever sent: the club picks among forms that are alive, and a person who sent a new one after the link lapsed is not the earliest of them. Changing the allocator to offer by `submitted_at`: the line's position is the moment a place was refused, and the club's rule for offers on their own is §615's. Showing the form's time only on a hand-run event: the same fact helps either way, and the lead line already says which order is shown. Writing the clock in Romania's zone for an event held elsewhere: the panel reads the event's zone since §369, and a second clock on one row would be the confusion that section removed.

Baseline `BR-V2.57-2026-10-02`.

## 628. «Lista de așteptare e publică»: the public list's waiting list is a per-event switch

**Amends §396, narrowing it; §421's per-runner rule and §32's gates are unchanged.** The owner, 2026-10-01: "Acum mai am nevoie de încă o setare cu „lista de așteptare e publică”".

**What it is.** A per-event switch, `events.waitlist_public boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false` (migration `0119_waitlist_public.sql`, expand only), shown in the event editor under «Publică lista participanților» as an indented second box, «Lista de așteptare e publică» / “The waiting list is public”, with its note: on the public list also appear those on the waiting list who ticked «Vreau să apar», in the list's order, without a position — only while the privacy notice in force describes the states. It sits inside the same type and mode wrappers as the list's own box, so it exists only where a list can.

**What it changes on the list.** The waiting-list group — the `WAITLISTED` rows, the word «Pe lista de așteptare», its legend sentence, its count in the line above the table, and its clause in the caption and the note — is drawn only when the switch is on, on top of the two existing gates: the notice in force names `{{participantListStates}}` in every language (§396), and the runner ticked under a notice at or after the first one that did (§421). It is a third condition on that one group, never a way round the other two. The pending group («Înscris, în așteptarea confirmării») stays behind the notice's gates alone. It is implemented at the reader, not at the drawing: `listPublicStartListOthers` and `countPublicStartListOthers` take a required `includeWaitlisted`, which leaves `WAITLISTED` out of the SQL's state list when false, and `cachedStartListOthersCounts` / `cachedStartListOthersPage` carry it in their cache keys — so a switched-off event never reads or counts a waiting row, and a page read with the waiting list is never served to one without it. The select list is unchanged (`tests/privacy/public-surface.test.ts`). With the switch off and the notice describing the states, the caption and the note use sentences without the waiting list (`captionStatesNoWaitlist`, `captionStatesNumbersNoWaitlist`, `noteStatesNoWaitlist`).

**What it changes on the form.** The «Vreau să apar» caption (`Registration.listOptInStates`) named «Pe lista de așteptare» as a stage the runner would be shown in. On an event whose waiting list is not public it now reads `listOptInStatesNoWaitlist`: the pending and the confirmed stages only, and that a runner waiting for a place does not appear on the public list — «Cât aștepți un loc pe lista de așteptare, nu apari pe lista publică.», the public list named outright so that «ea» cannot be read as the waiting list itself (`form-view.ts#listOptInStatesKey`, from the view's new `listShowsWaitlist`). The staff entry form's line (`Admin.registrations.listOptInStates`) is left as it was: it speaks before an event is chosen.

**How it is stored.** True only beside `participant_list_visibility = NAMES` on an `INTERNAL` event; anything else stores false whatever was posted (`service.ts#waitlistPublicColumn`, beside the NAMES refusal's own pair), so the column never holds a truth the list cannot act on, and a list switched off and on again does not find the waiting list already public. Beside a published list, a caller that does not post the box writes nothing (the discipline `kitShirt` follows); the editor's checkbox always posts, absent meaning off. A duplicate never inherits it, as it never inherits the list (AGENTS.md §10.10); a series edit carries it with the list.

**The default, and what it does to existing events.** Off — and the owner said it in so many words, 2026-10-01 evening: «nu fac asta până nu punem bifa cu lista de așteptare privată», that is, the waiting list is not shown until the box that keeps it private exists. An event that publishes its list today, under a notice that describes the states, stops showing its waiting list until the club ticks the box — "with the switch off, the list is what it is today minus the waiting-list rows". That is the narrowing direction, chosen because a public waiting list is now a per-event decision.

**The notice is left as an upper bound.** The privacy notice's template still says, in section 4, that the list holds «cei de pe lista de așteptare» (and its English twin). With the switch off by default that sentence describes the most the list can show, not what every event shows — and it is deliberately not re-templated here: a changed template would make the club approve the notice again for a sentence that stays true (the notice promises a maximum, and the switch only ever narrows it). A later template change may add «unde clubul o face publică pentru eveniment» if the club prefers the notice to say it.

**Refused.** A position on the waiting list (still not printed, §396); a per-runner waiting-list consent separate from «Vreau să apar» (the tick and the notice already cover it, §421); the switch opening anything without the notice (it adds a condition, never removes one); a default of on (it would publish without anybody deciding for that event).

**Docs.** AGENTS.md §10.10 and its column list, CLAUDE.md's rules-table row on the public list, the backoffice «Ghid» step on the legal texts and «Sarcini»'s row on the notice's states (`listStatesNotice`: its done line names the switch, and its steps no longer say the stages need "no other setting") name the switch.

**Tests.** `tests/privacy/public-surface.test.ts` (the readers with the switch off: no waiting row, none counted, the pending row kept, the select list unchanged; on: §396's and §421's rows; the public event query carries the column); `tests/integration/registrations/start-list-states.test.ts` (the rendered list with the waiting list private, in both languages; the older notice shows the confirmed alone whichever way the switch is); `tests/integration/cms/participant-list-privacy-guard.test.ts` (stored true only beside NAMES; a hidden list stores false; an omitted box changes nothing; switching the list off switches it off); unit: `startListSummary`'s words, `waitlistPublicColumn`, `formViewOf`/`listOptInStatesKey`, and the register page's caption in both languages. `tests/e2e/public-list-states.spec.ts` seeds its main event with the switch on and a second event with it off (the default): there the pending row is listed and no waiting row, count, legend line or word appears, in both languages, and the form's caption names no waiting-list stage.

Migration: `0119_waitlist_public.sql`.

Baseline `BR-V2.57-2026-10-02`.

## 629. Each person waiting sees where they stand in the line, and the event page says how many wait (amending §348, §587, §612, §615)

**The owner, 2026-10-01**, in his own words. He asked: «Acum mai am nevoie de încă o setare cu "lista de așteptare e publică"». The dispatcher asked what that meant, and he answered two of its three options: «Fiecare își vede locul» and «Doar numărul, pe pagina evenimentului» (the third, «Setare pe eveniment: lista de așteptare publică», is the sibling branch `feat/waiting-list-public-switch`, not this one). He then narrowed the first: «E ok să aștepte, ei nu vor afla când s-au înscris restul pe listă și noi putem alege pe cine să luăm din listă».

**The rule as built.** Each person waiting is told where they stand **only while the event's `waitlist_auto_offer` is true**, because then a freed place really goes in order. With it false — the club decides whom to offer a place, on grounds it can state (the terms, §618; an invited runner; the order of the forms where it follows it), so nobody learns when the rest of the line registered — the person is told only **how many others wait and that the club chooses**: no position, no length of the line as a place in it. And the event page says how many wait. Nothing here makes the list of names more public.

### What happened until now

A person on the waiting list was told they were «Pe lista de așteptare» and nothing else: not how long the line was, nor how far they were from the front. The registration's own page showed no state at all for a single registration (only a family's card has the state chip), «Toate înscrierile mele» showed the chip, and the `WAITLIST_JOINED` email said «te-am adăugat pe lista de așteptare. Te vom anunța dacă se eliberează un loc.» The event page said how many wait in some states and not in others: «3 pe lista de așteptare» as a line of its own when places were free, «… — 3 așteaptă deja un loc» in the full state's lead, and nothing at all on the places line (§615: «150 înscriși din 150 de locuri — 133 confirmați, 17 în curs de confirmare, 4 locuri păstrate pentru lista de așteptare»), nor when the line was full or the event kept none.

### The decision

**A. Where a person stands.** With `waitlist_auto_offer` true: «Ești pe locul 3 din 10 persoane de pe lista de așteptare.» and «Locurile eliberate se oferă în ordine.» With it false: «Ești pe lista de așteptare, împreună cu alte 9 persoane. Clubul alege cui oferă un loc eliberat.» (alone in the line, in either reading: «Ești singura persoană pe lista de așteptare.» and then the setting's sentence, never «locul 1 din 1 persoană»). It appears in three places, from one reader:
1. **The registration's own page** (`/registrations/manage/<token>`): under the state — a one-person page gets the state's words as a heading, «Pe lista de așteptare», which it never had, and the sentence under it; a family's card has the state chip, so only the sentence.
2. **«Toate înscrierile mele»**: the same sentence on a `WAITLISTED` row, under the date.
3. **The `WAITLIST_JOINED` email**: with offers in order, «Când am trimis acest email, erai pe locul 3 din 10.» / "When we sent this email, you were number 3 of 10."; with the club choosing, no position: «Când am trimis acest email, pe lista de așteptare mai așteptau alte 9 persoane.» / "When we sent this email, 9 other people were on the waiting list." (alone, in either reading: «… erai singura persoană pe lista de așteptare.») — one sentence added after the body, in both halves, worded as of the moment of rendering because an email is read later and the line moves. Never «ești» in an email. It is a machine-added sentence after the body whoever wrote it, like the other facts of a send (§547, §588): a club that rewrote the message's words still sends it.

**One reader, the allocator's order.** `readWaitlistPosition(db, registrationId)` in `registrations/repository.ts` returns `{ position, length, autoOffer }`, or null when the registration is not `WAITLISTED`; it still computes the position whatever the setting — the surfaces decide whether to say it — but is null on a cancelled event. The position is `row_number() over (order by waitlisted_at asc, id asc)` among the event's `WAITLISTED` rows — `lockOldestWaitlisted`'s own order, the one the allocator offers places in, written as a window over the same rows rather than as a second statement of the rule — and the length is the count of those rows. An offered person (`WAITLIST_OFFERED`) has left the line; a cancelled or expired row never was; `kind` appears in no condition, so a `TEST` row stands in the line like a real one (`AGENTS.md` §12.6), as `countEligibleWaitlisted` counts it. Two statements, no lock: a number one place stale the instant it renders is the same as the public counts, and nothing is decided from it. `listManagedPeople` and `listActiveRegistrationsForParticipant` carry it (`waitlistStanding`) on a waiting row only, one read each; a row that is not waiting costs nothing.

**The position follows the setting (§615).** `autoOffer` — the event's «Ofertele din lista de așteptare pleacă automat» as it stands when the page is read or the email rendered, from the same read of the event row, so no surface makes a second query — decides what is said. On «Da» the position and «Locurile eliberate se oferă în ordine.»; on «Nu» the count of others and «Clubul alege cui oferă un loc eliberat.», and the position is not in the page's markup at all: the owner decided that with offers handed out by hand nobody learns the order. The email is as of the moment it was rendered and says the same in its own register, with or without a position.

**Alone, and on a cancelled event (round 3).** A person alone in the line reads «Ești singura persoană pe lista de așteptare.» followed by the setting's sentence («Locurile eliberate se oferă în ordine.» or «Clubul alege cui oferă un loc eliberat.»), and the email says the same alone in both readings; «locul 1 din 1 persoană» is no longer said anywhere. On a **cancelled event** (`events.event_status = CANCELLED`) none of the three surfaces says a sentence about the line: a cancellation keeps every registration in its state (§331.6) and `fillAvailableSpots` offers nothing (§331.7), so «Ești pe locul 2 din 5 … Locurile eliberate se oferă în ordine.» would promise what will not happen, and the page already says the event is cancelled. `readWaitlistPosition` returns null for a cancelled event — from the event row it already joins for `autoOffer`, no extra query — so the three surfaces skip the sentence (and the one-person page's state heading, which was only there to carry it) by the same rule, the email at render time. The registration itself is untouched.

**The words.** `Registrations.waitlist` in both catalogues: `position.{one,few,other}` through `countForm` on the line's length («din 1 persoană», «din 10 persoane», «din 20 de persoane»; English repeats its one form under the three keys), `others.{one,few,other}` through `countForm` on the number of others («cu o altă persoană», «cu alte 9 persoane», «cu alte 20 de persoane»; English «with 1 other», «with 9 others»), `alone` (also with offers in order, when the line is one), `orderAuto`, `orderClub`; `position.one` («din 1 persoană») is no longer reachable and stays only because the form is looked up by `countForm`. The email's words are in `templates.ts` as every email's are, through `countForm` and no ICU plural. No number is typed in code.

**The email reads the line at render time, and why.** The renderer already has the database and the registration the outbox row names (`registrationId`), as it has for every other fact of a send (`render.ts`); the template itself has none. A number written into the payload at queue time would be as old as the queueing — and an email is rendered at send time, again at every retry, and again on a staff resend, each after the line moved — so the payload carries nothing new and the sentence is «as of the moment I was rendered» — the setting is read then too. When the person is no longer waiting at render time (an offer was made, they cancelled) or the event is cancelled, the sentence is simply absent.

**Privacy.** The sentence is on the registration's own token page and in its own email, and says numbers about the line and nothing about anybody else: no name, no state of another person; with the club choosing, not even this person's own place. The public list is not touched (`StartList.tsx`, §396, §613): it still shows no position.

**B. The event page says how many wait.** The places line (`fillPhrase`) gains a last part, «10 pe lista de așteptare» ("10 on the waiting list"), whenever anybody waits: «150 de înscriși din 150 de locuri — 133 de confirmați, 17 în curs de confirmare, 4 locuri păstrate pentru lista de așteptare, 10 pe lista de așteptare». The number is `readPublicPlaces`'s `waitlisted` — the `WAITLISTED` rows with no offer yet, from the same count the door already reads and the public cache carries, with no second query; a test registration stands in it as in every public count (and cannot exist in production). It rides on `PublicFill` (`waitlisted`, set by `publicFill`, absent when nobody waits and in a cache entry from before the halves were counted). It reuses the existing `cta.waitingCount` words.

**Not twice in one card.** Each state of the page says the number once:
- **Open, with a places line** (a capped event): the places line carries it, and the separate «N pe lista de așteptare» line it used to have beneath the free-place count (§587, §612) is gone — the same words, moved into the line where the other counts are. **The order on the page changes with it:** the people waiting are now said on the places line, and the open offer's own line («N loc oferit din lista de așteptare», §612) follows it, so the event page reads waiting, then offered, where the listing card (`openLinePhrases`, which has no places line) still reads offered, then waiting. The two are the same words and the same counts in a different order; the card is not touched, and the order is not worth a second places-line part for the offer — the places line is the page's total, the offered line is its detail. SPECS: BR-REQ-035-01 criterion 14 (order «after the free places … then pe lista de așteptare») and BR-REQ-034-01 criteria 15–16 (the places line's «three parts») are amended in the same landing. An uncapped event has no places line and no waiting list, so nothing changes there.
- **Full, the line takes people:** the lead already says «… — 3 așteaptă deja un loc.» (§587, the owner's words of 2026-09-30), the places line leaves it out (`fillPhrase(…, { withWaiting: false })`), so the card does not say the same number in two registers. The lead's count is the whole line (waiting plus an open offer), as it was.
- **The line full, or no list at all** (a sentence and no button): there is no lead with a number, so the places line says it.
- **The listing card** (`CardRegistration`) has no places line and was already consistent: the open state's detail carries the offered and the waiting counts (`openLinePhrases`), the full state's lead the count. Unchanged.

### Rejected
- **A position on the public list.** The list shows the confirmed, and — behind the notice (§396) — the ticked pending and waiting, each with its state and no position; a position beside a name is a disclosure the privacy notice does not describe. Not touched.
- **A position written into the email's payload at queue time.** Stale at the first retry; see above.
- **A promise of order in the email.** The setting can change before the email is read; the email says only what the line was when it was rendered.
- **The position whatever the setting.** The first version of this branch told everybody their place and said, for the club's choice, that the club chooses; the owner's narrowing («ei nu vor afla când s-au înscris restul pe listă») makes the place itself the thing withheld.
- **A second count query for the event page.** `waitlisted` is already in the cached read.
- **A new setting for any of this.** None needed: the sentence follows the setting that exists.

### Consequences
`registrations/repository.ts` (`readWaitlistPosition`, null on a cancelled event); `registrations/domain/waitlist-standing.ts` (the type); `registrations/ui/waitlist-position-words.ts` (the two readings of the setting); `registrations/manage-family.ts` and `registrations/my-registrations.ts` (`waitlistStanding`); the two token pages; `notifications/render.ts` and `templates.ts` (`waitlistStanding`, `waitlistPosition`); `events/domain/registration-cta.ts` (`PublicFill.waitlisted`), `events/ui/counted-phrases.ts` (`fillPhrase`), `RegistrationCta.tsx`, `registration-door.ts`; `messages/{ro,en}.json` (`Registrations.waitlist`). The allocator, the capacity formula, `waitlist.ts` and the public list are untouched. No migration, no dependency. Tests: `unit/registrations/waitlist-standing-words.test.ts`, `integration/registrations/waitlist-position.test.ts`, `integration/notifications/waitlist-joined-position.test.ts` (new; the cancelled event on the page, «Toate înscrierile mele» and the email), `unit/events/counted-phrases.test.ts`, `unit/events/registration-cta.test.ts`, `integration/registrations/registration-fill-render.test.ts`.

Baseline `BR-V2.58-2026-10-02`.

## 630. The waiting-list setting says what it does, and the backoffice spells «BIB» one way

Two wording changes, no behaviour.

**A. The setting's name.** §615 named the editor's «Da»/«Nu» select «Ofertele din lista de așteptare pleacă automat». The owner (2026-10-01): «Nu îmi place cum sună 'ofertele din lista de așteptare merg automat'», then «Zi 'locurile din lista de alocă automat'». The label is now «Locurile din lista de așteptare se alocă automat» (en «Places from the waiting list are allocated automatically»). The label follows the owner's words, but the help still says the mechanism, because «alocă» on «Da» means an offer with a deadline that the person must accept and sign (`fillAvailableSpots` makes a WAITLIST_SPOT_OFFER), not a seat given outright: «Pe „Da”, un loc eliberat sau adăugat se alocă pe loc primului de pe lista de așteptare: primește oferta pe email și o confirmă până la termen. Pe „Nu”, locurile rămân libere până le dai tu.» (its English twin, shortened to the 200 characters §511 allows backoffice help: «On “Yes”, a freed or added place is offered at once, by email and with a deadline, to the first on the waiting list. On “No”, places stay free until you hand them out.»; neither names the button, `waitlistAutoOfferHelpMore` does); «Da»/«Nu» stay, and `waitlistAutoOfferHelpMore` keeps its content. Every place that quoted the old label follows: the guide's steps (§620) and the two guide sentences that said the offers «nu pleacă automat», `SETUP.md` §39's recipe, code comments and the tests that assert the words. The column `events.waitlist_auto_offer`, its values, the audit action `event.waitlist_auto_offer_changed` and the behaviour are untouched.

**B. «BID» becomes «BIB».** The backoffice's catalogue strings said «BID» for the race number. The owner, in the review of `fix/race-number-column-says-bib`: «BIB, ăsta e termenul tehnic». Romanian keeps the hyphenated forms of today's «BID-ul»: «BIB-ul», «BIB-uri», «BIB-urile». Changed in both catalogues (the printing mark, the desk guide, the start list's toggle and alt text, the guide's steps) and in the e2e assertions. Not touched, on purpose: the journey chip «nr. {number}» / «no. {number}» and the desk's «Salvează nr.» — the owner asked for the column's and the technical term's spelling, not every short form; and the owner's quoted words in code comments, which keep their original spelling. «FORBIDDEN» is not the race number and stays.

Refused: a new key, an ICU change, any migration.

**Supersedes in `SPECS.md`.** BR-REQ-034-02 criterion 18 quotes the old label «Ofertele din lista de așteptare pleacă automat», and BR-REQ-038-01 criterion 16 spells the chip «BID N tipărit — de retras»; both are read with the new words («Locurile din lista de așteptare se alocă automat», «BIB N tipărit — de retras»).

Baseline `BR-V2.58-2026-10-02`.

## 631. The cancel dialog says the person is emailed, what the reason does, and where the place goes

**The owner, from his phone (2026-10-01):** «De asemenea, dacă îi anulez, primesc mail? Atunci trebuie să îi înștiințez cumva. Adică eu ca admin trebuie să primesc în pop-up când anulez pe cineva că se va trimite și un mail».

The dialogs that cancel a registration must tell the staff member what the press does, in this order: the person is emailed at once; the written reason stays in the journal and travels only with the refusal box; the place is offered to the first in line or stays free, by the event's setting.

**What the code does (checked before the words were written).** Every staff cancellation (`cancelRegistrationByStaff`, and each registration of `bulkCancelRegistrationsByStaff`) goes through `unregister(..., "ADMIN")`, which queues `REGISTRATION_CANCELLED` to the participant at once, naming the state the registration left (§547). The reason is written to the audit journal; it reaches the email only when the «Clubul refuză înscrierea, potrivit termenilor» box is ticked (`refusedGround`, §618). The freed place is offered at once to the first in line when the event's automatic offers are on, and kept free until the club hands it out when they are off (`events.waitlist_auto_offer`, §615; labelled today «Ofertele din lista de așteptare pleacă automat», and renamed «Locurile din lista de așteptare se alocă automat» by the sibling branch fix/waitlist-setting-says-places-are-allocated; the dialogs name neither label, only «după setarea evenimentului», so no catalogue change follows the rename).

**Decision.** Words only, both locales, no behaviour change. `Admin.registrations.cancelBody` (the list row's dialog), `Admin.confirm.cancelRegistrationBody` (the registration page's dialog), `Admin.registrations.cancelHelp` and `Admin.confirm.bulkCancelBody` / `Admin.registrations.bulkCancelHelp` (the bulk cancel) now state the email, the reason's fate and the place's fate. `refusedByOrganizerHelp` keeps §618's list of objective grounds and adds that unticked, the person still gets the cancellation email, without the reason. What §618 recorded is kept: the list row's dialog still says, and the registration page's now says, that the cancellation cannot be undone; the row's dialog (which has no reason field, so it says only that the refusal, with its reason, is made from the registration's page, not that a reason stays in the log) and the bulk help («Un refuz potrivit termenilor se face din pagina înscrierii.») still point to the registration's own page for a refusal under the terms, and the grounds stay in the caption. The place's sentence reads «se oferă primului de pe lista de așteptare sau rămâne liber, după setarea evenimentului» («waiting list» said in full, shortened to «setare» only where the 200-character cap needs it) (offered, not given, in English too, «is offered to the first on the waiting list»; the bulk help says «după setare» / "by the setting" in short: with automatic offers on the first person gets an offer with a deadline). The row and the page do not carry the event's setting, so each text names both outcomes rather than reading the event again for one sentence.

**Refused.** Choosing the one applicable sentence by reading `waitlist_auto_offer` into the row and the page: a query and a prop for a sentence, against the standing rule that the list is cheap. The count line the dialog already adds (`confirm.email`) is kept.

Baseline `BR-V2.58-2026-10-02`.

## 632. The headline numbers count everyone with a place: «Cine vine (150)» and the «Înscrieri» badge with a pill per group in progress

**The owner, 2026-10-02, from his phone, three messages.** Production is live and the 21 November race is full. The public page read «150 de înscriși din 150 de locuri — 134 de confirmați, 16 în curs de confirmare, 10 pe lista de așteptare» above a fold titled «Cine vine (134)», and the backoffice tab read «Înscrieri [134] [⏳ 10]». He wrote: «Păi da dar atunci numărul ăsta de 134 nu e accurate, pune-o și pe cei care trebuie să confirme înregistrarea». Asked whether to change the public title, the badge, or both: «Amândouă». Then, with a screenshot of the tab, verbatim: «Tot pe acest pull [sic] trebuie să afișăm și pe cei care aștept [sic] confirmarea mailului sau semnarea declarației». «Pull» could mean this pull request; it is read here as the tab's pill — an interpretation, not his word, backed by the screenshot he sent with it (the tab and its pills) and by «afișăm», which only a screen does. On either reading the ask is the same: show those awaiting the email confirmation and those with a declaration to sign.

**Decision: a headline number that stands for «înscriși» is everyone with a place.** That is the allocator's occupied people — CONFIRMED, PENDING_DECLARATION, an open WAITLIST_OFFERED, a family's hold (§543) — the same people the places line on the event page and the card already count (§615). The split (confirmed / în curs de confirmare) stands beside the number. This amends §346's title (the confirmed) and §626's badge (the confirmed alone).

**The public «Cine vine» fold.** On a capped event whose cached public read knows the counts, `inProgress = taken − confirmed` (the places line's own «în curs de confirmare»). When it is above zero the title counts the confirmed plus them — «Cine vine (150)» — and the bold line under it reads «150 de înscriși — 134 de confirmați (120 cu numele afișat), 16 în curs de confirmare» / «150 registered — 134 confirmed (120 with their name shown), 16 completing their registration», each Romanian number in its own form (`countForm`) and the in-progress words the places line's own (`cta.fillInProgress`), so the page says one thing one way. With nothing in progress, on an uncapped event, when registration is not open (the door reads no counts then) or from a cache entry that predates the counts, the title and the line are exactly as before («Cine vine (134)», «134 de participanți confirmați — 120 cu numele afișat»). The figure comes from the same cached read the page's door already makes (`readRegistrationDoor` → `cachedPublicAvailability`): no query of the list's own, so the public cache keeps Neon as cheap as §250 and §333 made it. The confirmed in the title stays the list's own REAL-only count, while `taken − confirmed` is the places line's kind-blind count; on QA a TEST row can make the two reads differ, which §615's criterion 16 already accepts for the places line; production has no TEST row. The rows do not change: behind §396's gate the ticked pending appear by name with «Apar cu numele și: …», the waiting list stays behind §628's switch, and nobody pending appears without the gate. The note under the table now opens with the qualified clause — «Numărul din titlu îi cuprinde pe confirmați și, cât timp înscrierile sunt deschise la un eveniment cu număr de locuri, pe cei în curs de confirmare» / «The number in the title counts the confirmed and, while registration is open at an event with a set number of places, those completing their registration» — never «everyone with a place» bare, because once registration closes on a capped event the title falls back to the confirmed while declarations may still be unsigned; the same opening in the two states notes. With nobody confirmed yet and somebody in progress, the title counts them and the line stands above «Încă nu și-a confirmat nimeni participarea.» («Cine vine (2)», «2 înscriși — 0 confirmați (0 cu numele afișat), 2 în curs de confirmare»). When the door's cached read fails, the list's own call reads the database again and logs a second line after the card's, because the request memo forgets a failed promise; accepted, since the breaker fails fast once open, rather than threading the card's door into the list.

**Why an uncapped event keeps the confirmed alone.** §32 declined to publish a head count of held places with no «out of» beside it; an uncapped event shows no places line, so the page has no in-progress number to repeat, and the title would be the only place that discloses it.

**The backoffice «Înscrieri» tab.** The filled pill is everyone with a place at the upcoming events (`withPlace`, REAL rows only, from the query and the one-minute memo that exist). After it, outlined pills in the waiting pill's shape (glyph and number, a worded name for a screen reader, drawn only above zero, all inside the one focusable chunk the tooltip hangs on), in this order: those completing their registration with a place (`withPlace − confirmed`, the pen `Draw` the participant's own declaration step wears), those awaiting the email confirmation (`awaitingEmail`, the envelope `MarkEmailRead` of the email step), and the waiting list (the hourglass, as §626). «Înscrieri [150] [✍ 16] [✉ 7] [⏳ 10]». The first pill is part of the filled number; the other two are outside it. The two glyphs join the action-icon registry as `declaration` and `emailConfirmation`. The tooltip's first line says every figure, a zero included: «Cu loc: 150 — 134 de confirmați, 16 în curs de confirmare · așteaptă confirmarea emailului: 7 · pe lista de așteptare: 10»; the figures still add up to everybody with an active registration, and the per-event lines are unchanged.

**Why the pending email and the waiting list stay out of the headline.** A form whose address is not confirmed holds no place (unless a family's hold reserves one, which is counted), and the waiting list is not registered for a place either; counting them would make the badge disagree with the public places line and with the allocator. They have their own pills, beside the number and not inside it.

**Why the pills are not links.** The tab is already an anchor and a link inside an anchor is invalid HTML; the registrations list's summary strip is where the pills are filters (§626).

**Refused:** a new query for the public title (the cached read is enough); counting TEST rows anywhere a club reads (§12.6); words beside the tab's pills (three pills at 320 pixels lengthen the scrollable tab row, never the page, only while they stay glyph and number).

Baseline `BR-V2.59-2026-10-02`.

## 633. The waiting list's length is a choice in words: «Nelimitată», «Limitată la un număr de locuri», «Fără listă de așteptare» (amending §348, §350)

**The owner, 2026-10-02 morning, from his phone** — production live, the 21 November race full with twenty people waiting, and he wanted the list unlimited: «Trebuie tooltip și în back-office că 0 înseamnă listă de așteptare infinită + ceva bifă care să fie mai explicită, dacă pun 0 să se bifeze automat listă infinită».

### What the box meant until now, and the near-miss

«Lungimea maximă a listei de așteptare» (§348, beside the places since §350) stored an empty box as **no limit** (null) and **0** as **no waiting list at all**; its help said so in one line («Gol: nelimitat; 0: fără listă de așteptare.»). The owner read it the other way: he believed 0 meant unlimited. Had he typed 0 as he meant to, the race's list would have closed — every newcomer refused with «Locurile s-au ocupat, iar acest eveniment nu are listă de așteptare.» while twenty people were already in the line. The dispatcher told him not to type 0. One number carried two meanings, and the one a person guesses is the dangerous one.

### The decision: the meaning is chosen in words, never inferred from a number

1. **A select «Lista de așteptare»** (`event.waitlistMode`) beside «Număr de locuri», in the same row (§350), with three answers in this order:
   - «Nelimitată» / "Unlimited" — stores **null**;
   - «Limitată la un număr de locuri» / "Limited to a number of places" — reveals the number «Cel mult atâtea persoane pe listă» / "At most this many people on the list" (the same `event.waitlistCapacity` box, `inputMode="numeric"`, **min 1** — `optionalWholeNumber` through `waitlistLimitSchema`), and stores that number;
   - «Fără listă de așteptare» / "No waiting list" — stores **0**.
   The select opens on what is stored: null → «Nelimitată», 0 → «Fără listă», N ≥ 1 → «Limitată» with N in the box; a new event opens on «Nelimitată». Under it one short helper, «Ce se întâmplă când locurile s-au ocupat.», and beside it an «i» (`InfoTip`, also the button's accessible name) with the three meanings: «Nelimitată: oricine poate intra pe listă când locurile s-au ocupat. Limitată: cel mult atâtea persoane. Fără listă: evenimentul plin refuză pe toată lumea.» The number's helper keeps the old note that lowering it below the people already waiting removes nobody, and adds «Gol sau 0: lista devine nelimitată.» The select is native, like «Locurile din lista de așteptare se alocă automat» under it, so the island can change its answer.
2. **The owner's switch.** While the answer is «Limitată», a number box left empty or at 0 switches the select to «Nelimitată» there and then: the box hides, and the save stores null. A client island only as large as the switch — `WaitlistLimitOnly`, `OnlyForMode`'s sibling over the waiting list's select, through the same `ShownWhen` (so the box is read-only while hidden and its `min` never blocks the save). It judges when the box is **left** (`change`), not on every key, so emptying «20» to type «15» does not hide the box under the thumb; when it switches, it also empties the box, so «Limitată» chosen again opens on an empty box the save accepts rather than a 0 its `min` would refuse; a box the browser cannot read as a number (`badInput`) is left for the browser to refuse. **The server does the same without JavaScript**: a posted «Limitată» with an empty or 0 number (or no number at all) saves as null, never as 0.
3. **0 is stored only by the explicit «Fără listă de așteptare».** The service folds the answer and the number into the one stored value before its schema reads them (`service.ts#ignoreHiddenFields`, `waitlist-choice.ts#waitlistLengthPosted`), by §350's hidden-fields rule: the number shows only under «Limitată», so under the other two whatever it holds — wrong included — is never read. An answer that is none of the three is refused naming the select. The mode's rule still runs after it: «Fără înscrieri», «La organizator» and a group run (§111) store no length whatever the answer.
4. **Everything else is as it was.** No schema change, no migration: the three answers are the three values `events.waitlist_capacity` already holds, so the allocator, `domain/waitlist.ts`, `registration-cta.ts`, the public pages and the queue panel are untouched. A caller that posts neither box leaves the length alone; a direct service caller that sends only `waitlistCapacity` (a script, a fixture) keeps §348's meaning — empty no limit, 0 no list, N a limit. The create form, the duplicate, a repeat and the series' scoped save (`SERIES_COLUMNS`, §615) carry the stored value exactly as before. The refusal summary names «Participare și înscrieri › Lista de așteptare» and «… › Lista de așteptare › Cel mult atâtea persoane pe listă». The journal records no from/to for this field, so there were no raw «null»/«0» to reword there.
5. **The words that still taught the old reading are gone**: the «Ghid» («Deschide înscrierile la o cursă», «Alege tu cine primește un loc eliberat») in both catalogues, and `SETUP.md` §39's click list, which gains the row «Lista de așteptare» → **Nelimitată** for the race, with why in one clause that holds whichever way «Locurile din lista de așteptare se alocă automat» is set: the list is private (§628) and an open-ended line costs the club nothing.

### Refused

- **A checkbox «Listă infinită» plus the number** (the owner's own words, «ceva bifă»). The number would still have had two meanings under the box — 0 and empty would each need a rule beside the tick — and a tick with a number makes four states for three answers. A select of three answers in words is the same explicitness with one state per meaning, and the auto-switch gives him the behaviour he asked for («dacă pun 0 să se bifeze automat listă infinită»).
- **Changing what the column means** (making 0 mean unlimited). Every reader of `waitlist_capacity` — the allocator, the event page, the card, the form, the queue panel, the public cache, the emails — would change for no gain, and every event stored as «no list» would silently open. The words change; the stored values do not.

Amends §348's and §350's field «Lungimea maximă a listei de așteptare»: the length is now set through «Lista de așteptare», and the number box exists only under «Limitată la un număr de locuri».

Baseline `BR-V2.59-2026-10-02`.

## 634. «Arată public câți așteaptă»: a switch per event for the waiting list's count (amending §587, §615, §629)

**The owner, 2026-10-02 morning, from his phone** — the 21 November race is full, people are waiting, and he is making its waiting list unlimited: «Trebuie să avem mare grijă să nu afișăm lista de așteptare și să nu le zicem oamenilor al câtelea sunt în listă, pentru că astfel ne facem de râs», and then «O să avem o bifă și dacă să afișăm sau nu câți sunt pe lista de așteptare».

**What it was.** §628's «Lista de așteptare e publică» (off by default) hides the waiting list's NAMES. The NUMBER was said everywhere regardless: the full state's lead «Mulțumim! Toate cele 150 de locuri s-au ocupat — 10 așteaptă deja un loc.» (§587), the places line's last part «…, 10 pe lista de așteptare» (§629), the «Locurile se dau din lista de așteptare · … · N pe lista de așteptare» line while places are given from the line (§615), and each waiting person's own sentence — «Ești pe locul 3 din 10 persoane…» with automatic offers, «Ești pe lista de așteptare, împreună cu alte 9 persoane.» with the club choosing (§629) — on the registration's page, in «Toate înscrierile mele» and in the `WAITLIST_JOINED` email.

**Decision.** One more per-event switch, for the number alone: `events.waitlist_count_public boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true` (migration `0120_waitlist_count_public.sql`, expand only). In the editor's public-list card, directly under «Lista de așteptare e publică» and not indented — it does not depend on the names switch and is drawn whatever that says: «Arată public câți așteaptă» / "Show publicly how many are waiting", ticked by default, with one sentence of help: «Bifat: cardul, pagina și fiecare persoană de pe listă află câți așteaptă. Debifat: paginile spun doar că există o listă de așteptare și cum intri pe ea; clubul vede numărul în administrare.» It is read by its marker (`event.waitlistCountPublic.present`), so a form without the box changes nothing; a series' scoped save carries it (`SERIES_COLUMNS`), every date a series makes and a duplicate keep it — it publishes no name, so the list's never-inherited rule does not bind it; every change writes `event.waitlist_count_public_changed` with `from` and `to`, on each date it reached.

**Unticked, the public says no count of the line:**
- **The full state** (card, page, the join form's title): a third shape of the thank-you lead, «Mulțumim! Toate cele {capacity} de locuri s-au ocupat. Intră pe lista de așteptare.» / "Thank you! All {capacity} places are taken. Join the waiting list." (`cta.fullThanksJoin`, the three `countForm` shapes) — never «— N așteaptă deja un loc», and never «Fii primul pe lista de așteptare.», which would say nought.
- **The places line** (`fillPhrase`) drops «, N pe lista de așteptare». While places are still free beside the line it also drops «N locuri păstrate pentru lista de așteptare»: the formula keeps exactly one free place per person waiting, so that part is the count by another name. Once no place is free, the places kept are every free place the line claims — a number about places, the line being at least as long — and they stay, so «6 înscriși din 10 locuri — 4 locuri păstrate…» still adds up under «Toate cele 10 locuri s-au ocupat» (§615's consistency).
- **While places are given from the line** (§615): «Locurile se dau din lista de așteptare» and «N loc oferit din lista de așteptare» stay — an offer is a place, not a person waiting — and the people waiting go, on the card and the page.
- **The waiting person's own view**, page and email alike (the email says what the page says at the moment it is rendered, §629's rule): no position either, in both settings — «Ești pe lista de așteptare.» / "You are on the waiting list.", followed by the setting's sentence as before («Locurile eliberate se oferă în ordine.» or «Clubul alege cui oferă un loc eliberat.»). The line is ordered by when each person joined, so whoever has just joined is last and their place IS the line's length: «locul 47» on the joining email or the page right after is «47 așteaptă» in other words, told to every newcomer — exactly what the owner asked not to say («să nu le zicem oamenilor al câtelea sunt în listă»). «Ești singura persoană pe lista de așteptare.» says the line is one long, so it is not said either. The email: «Când am trimis acest email, erai pe lista de așteptare; locurile eliberate se oferă în ordine.» / "When we sent this email, you were on the waiting list; freed places are offered in order.", or «…, erai pe lista de așteptare; clubul alege cui oferă un loc eliberat.» Why the person too: someone on the list is outside the backoffice, so a count told to them is told to anyone who joins.

**What stays, and why.**
- **«Mai sunt N locuri pe lista de așteptare»** (§348's room line) stays: it is a fact about the event's size, like the capacity (§32's reasoning), not a count of people, and the `WAITLIST_FULL` state needs it. With an unlimited list there is no room line anyway.
- **The names** are §628's business: «Cine vine»'s waiting group is untouched — with the names published, how many they are is visible by nature.
- **The backoffice** keeps every count: the badge, «Coada de înscrieri», the editor's asides, `/admin/tasks`.
- **Ticked**, every sentence is today's, byte for byte (tested).

**How it is applied.** In one place per surface, never as a hidden element: `registrationCta` says `waitlisted` as nought on `OPEN` and `waiting` as null on `FULL` — after `fromWaitlist` and the door were chosen from the real count, so the switch decides nothing; `publicFill` leaves out `waitlisted` (and `kept` while places are free); `waitlistStandingPhrase` and the email's `waitlistPositionLine` read `countPublic` from `readWaitlistPosition`, the same read of the event row that carries `autoOffer`. The allocator, the capacity formula and every queue read are untouched; `kind` is in no condition — a `TEST` row counts in every count as a real one (§12.6) and the door still sends a newcomer to the line behind it.

**The cache rule.** No new query on a public page. The live door reads the switch from the availability entry the counts ride (`cachedPublicAvailability`, off the same internal row), so the count and its switch are one read at one moment; the entry's key gained `"count-switch"` with its shape, as §628's start-list keys gained their switch, so no entry written without the switch is read by code that asks for it. The public event read carries the column too (the editor's preview draws the door from it); an event save expires both, as before.

**Refused.**
- **Hiding the count by default.** It would have changed every live event overnight — the weekly run's page included — without anybody deciding for that event; default on keeps every existing event as it is, and the race changes only when the club unticks the box.
- **Tying it to «Lista de așteptare e publică».** That switch answers whether names are published; this one whether a number is. A club can want neither, either or both, and the names switch is off by default while the number has always been said.
- **Keeping the position with automatic offers.** It looked like the person's own and silent about the line, but it is not: the newest is always last, so every joiner's first «locul N» is the line's length, and anyone can learn it by joining. With offers in order a freed place still goes by the order the person cannot see; «Locurile eliberate se oferă în ordine.» says so. Keeping it would take the owner's explicit choice, knowing it tells every joiner the count.
- **Hiding the room line.** A fact about the list's size, like the capacity.

**Consequences.** Migration `0120_waitlist_count_public`; `db/schema/events.ts`; `content/events` (fields, `actions.ts`, the save and its trail, the series columns, the duplicate, `field-labels.ts`, `preview-view.ts`, `StartListBox.tsx`); `events/repository.ts` (the public read); `public-cache/reads.ts` (the availability entry and its key); `events/domain/registration-cta.ts`, `events/ui/counted-phrases.ts` (`fullThanksPhrase`), `events/ui/registration-door.ts`, the register page; `registrations/repository.ts#readWaitlistPosition`, `domain/waitlist-standing.ts`, `ui/waitlist-position-words.ts`; `notifications/templates.ts`, `render.ts`; the audit action `event.waitlist_count_public_changed`; `messages/{ro,en}.json` (`Event.cta.fullThanksJoin`, `Registrations.waitlist.onList`, `Admin.editor.waitlistCountPublic`/`Help`, a sentence in the «Ghid»). `CardRegistration.tsx` and `RegistrationCta.tsx` are unchanged: they draw what the door says. Docs: `SETUP.md` §39's row, `AGENTS.md` §10.10 and its column list, CLAUDE.md's rules row. Tests: `integration/cms/waitlist-count-public.test.ts`, `unit/events/waitlist-count-public.test.ts`, `unit/content/waitlist-count-box.test.ts` (new); `integration/registrations/registration-fill-render.test.ts`, `integration/notifications/waitlist-joined-position.test.ts`, `integration/registrations/waitlist-position.test.ts`, `unit/registrations/waitlist-standing-words.test.ts`, `integration/resilience/register-page-resting.test.ts`, `unit/shared/form-constraints.test.ts`. No dependency.

Baseline `BR-V2.59-2026-10-02`.

## 635. The backoffice says when each person loses the place

**The owner, 2026-10-02:** «Când pierde lumea locul? Trebuie să apară asta in back-office».

**What the backoffice said until now.** The answer was spread over code and settings, and shown in one place only: the registration's own page said «Rezervarea expiră: <date>». The editor's confirmation card says the window's two dates; the list's journey cell («3/6 · Loc rezervat») said nothing of a deadline, not even in its hover title. Two days before a race the club, looking at the event's list, could not see who was about to lose a place, nor when.

**The rules, as the code applies them.** This decision changes none of them; it says them.

- **The declaration hold** (`computeDeclarationHoldExpiry`). A place given before the event's participation window opens (§104: `confirmation_opens_days_before`, 7 by default; `confirmation_deadline_days_before`, 2) is the person's until the window's deadline — start minus the deadline's days, or the start itself when that is 0 (§407) — and is not capped by the close. Inside the window, and on an event without one, the club's `holdMinutes` («Termene», §377: 30 by default, 10–120), counted from when the declaration email leaves (§513) and capped by the close and the start.
- **Past its deadline (§160)** a hold is not released by the clock. `expireStaleHolds` releases `waiting − free` lapsed holds, the oldest deadline first, where `waiting` is the `WAITLISTED` rows (plus, §348, a newcomer the line has no room for) and `free` the places free without touching a hold. It runs under the event lock on every allocator path — a newcomer's address confirmed (`placeForNewcomer`, and the second pass when the line grows), a cancellation, «Trimite-i oferta» (`offerPlaceToByStaff`), «Dă-i un loc», the editor's capacity raise — and in the maintenance job, whose scan selects an event with a lapsed hold somebody waits for whatever its `waitlist_auto_offer` (`findEventsNeedingMaintenance`), and whose `fillAvailableSpots` sweeps before §615's gate. So **in both settings** of «Locurile din lista de așteptare se alocă automat» the hold is released as soon as somebody waiting has no free place. What follows differs: with «Da», before the close, the place is offered to the first in line in the same transaction; with «Nu» it stays free until the organizer hands it out with «Trimite-i oferta» (before the close) or «Dă-i un loc»; after the close, in either setting, no offer is made (§420) and the desk's «Dă-i un loc» gives it. With no waiting list (a limit of 0) the one who wants it is a newcomer who finds no other place free (§348); an uncapped event never wants one. At the start every unsigned hold is released, and the desk can still confirm a paper declaration into a place still free (§160). **Nothing is emailed** when a hold is released: `expireStaleHolds` writes `EXPIRED` with `DECLARATION_HOLD_LAPSED` in bulk and queues no message.
- **The first email's link** (`email_link_expires_at`): `confirmationHours` (48 by default, 12–168) from when it leaves (§513). A `PENDING_EMAIL_CONFIRMATION` row holds no place — a family's reservation excepted, until its sitting's deadline (§543) — and expires with the link (`expireStalePendingEmailConfirmations`, silently).
- **A waiting-list offer**: `offerHours` (24 by default, 6–72) from when its email leaves (§520), capped by the close and the start. Unsigned, it lapses silently (`WAITLIST_OFFER_EXPIRED` is never queued, §331); the place goes to the next in line with «Da» while registration is open, and stays free with «Nu».
- **A confirmed registration** never loses its place except by a cancellation.

**Decision: one sentence family, one builder.** `registrations/domain/place-deadlines.ts#placeDeadlineSentences` is pure: the event's window, limits, setting, close and status, the club's deadlines, counts of real registrations, the clock, the locale and the zone in; short sentences out — each under 200 characters (§511), every number the setting's (§377), every date through `formatDay` (short, with the time). In order:
- who has to sign, and until when: «16 persoane au de semnat declarația și își țin locul până joi, 19 nov. 2026, la 10:00 (cu 2 zile înainte de start).», or «…până la start.» for a deadline of 0;
- with the window open, who keeps its deadline («Cine și-a confirmat adresa înainte de … își ține locul până …») and how long a new hold lasts («Cine își confirmă adresa de acum are cel mult 30 de minute să semneze, de când pleacă emailul.» — not after the close);
- how many are past it: «9 persoane au termenul depășit; locul li se ține cât nu-l cere nimeni.» — counted as the sweep reads a lapsed hold: not one whose first declaration email is still queued, since its send moves the deadline forward (§513, `awaitingItsFirstEmail`, as `lapsedDeclarationHoldsToRelease` excludes it);
- what a passed deadline does, in the one variant the code does for this event: «Da», «Nu», after the close, no waiting list, no limit — e.g. «După termen locul nu se pierde singur: se eliberează doar când cineva de pe lista de așteptare n-are alt loc liber, și i se oferă primului din listă.»; not while every deadline is the start itself;
- the start: «La start, cine n-a semnat pierde locul; la masă poate fi confirmat pe hârtie, dacă mai e un loc liber.»;
- the email's link, with the family's exception when a reservation holds: «7 persoane n-au confirmat încă adresa: linkul e valabil 48 de ore de când pleacă emailul, apoi înscrierile expiră; până atunci nu țin niciun loc.»;
- the open offers, by setting: «…valabilă cel mult 24 de ore de când pleacă emailul; nesemnată la timp, trece la următorul din listă cât sunt deschise înscrierile.» / «…locul rămâne liber până îl dai tu.».

A count of zero drops its sentences; a cancelled or finished event gets none. English equivalents for each, in the same keys (`Admin.registrations.placeDeadlines.*`, counted through `countForm`).

**Where it shows, and why there.**
- **The registrations list scoped to one event**, right under «Cine s-a înscris», headed «Când se pierde un loc»: it is the screen the club reads two days before the race. Not on the list over every event, where no single window or setting is true of every row.
- **The event's «Înscrierile primite»**, under its buttons, beside the bulk resend of the declaration.
- **The queue panel**, the held places' sentences only, beside «Rezervate», in the event's own zone like every other time on that panel (§369). On the event's page they repeat what the box above says, knowingly: the queue's fold starts closed (§336), so the box's block is the answer read without opening anything, and the panel's lines sit beside the numbers they explain.

One grouped query (`admin-repository.ts#readPlaceDeadlines`: the event's row and its real registrations counted by filter), read once per page; the event's page hands it to the queue panel. Real rows only: a test registration is in no number the club is given (§12.6) — the allocator's `countOccupied`, which counts them by design, is not read for it. Every role that reads the registrations sees the sentences, the Organizer too (§289); the Tehnic role reads no list and gets nothing new.

**Every row.** The «Unde a ajuns» cell keeps its step and adds the deadline the row's state waits on: «ține locul până joi, 19 nov. 2026, la 10:00»; past it «termen depășit, locul se ține cât nu-l cere nimeni» (the journey's kept words, which said «cât nu așteaptă nimeni» — now the block's own, since a newcomer can want the place too, §348); «loc oferit, până …»; «linkul expiră …» or «linkul a expirat» on a row still waiting for its address, read from `email_link_expires_at`, a column of the row added to the list's select (no join, no query per row); «loc rezervat până …» on a family's reservation while it holds. The step stays on one line and the deadline wraps at 320 px; the hover title is unchanged; an ended row names no deadline. The registration's page says the same: its timeline's «Rezervarea expiră» reads «Ține locul până» on a live hold, with the kept words past a declaration's deadline, and stays on an ended row; a row waiting for its address gains «Linkul din email expiră».

**The guide.** «Retrimite declarația celor care nu au semnat» gains one step: where the deadlines show now.

*Rejected:*
- **Leaving the held places out of the event's box**, so they show only beside «Rezervate». That fold starts closed (§336): the box would answer every question but the owner's.
- **A countdown, or any new deadline.** The rules are the existing ones, and the owner asked to see them, not to change them.
- **A per-row query of the queue** to say whether a kept hold will survive the next visit: §160 already chose the condition in words for a list that spans events.
- **The block on the list over every event.** Its sentences would be true of some rows and false of others.
- **Reading `countOccupied` for the counts.** It is the allocator's, and counts test rows on purpose.

**Consequences.** New: `registrations/domain/place-deadlines.ts`, `registrations/ui/PlaceDeadlines.tsx`. Changed: `admin-repository.ts` (`readPlaceDeadlines`; `emailLinkExpiresAt` on the list's and the detail's rows), `domain/journey.ts` (the `link` detail, `reservedUntil`, an optional `emailLinkExpiresAt`), `ui/StaffJourney.tsx`, `ui/QueuePanel.tsx`, the registrations list, the event's page, the registration's page; both catalogues (`Admin.registrations.placeDeadlines.*`, `journey.holding`, `link`, `linkLapsed`, `reserved`, `heldKept`'s words, `holdKeeps`, `linkExpires`, the guide's step). No schema, allocator, deadline, job or email change; `kind` in no allocator condition. Tests: `tests/unit/registrations/place-deadlines.test.ts` (both languages; the window ahead, a deadline of 0, the window open, no window; «Da» and «Nu»; after the close; no list, no limit; a family; zero counts; past-deadline holds; every sentence under 200 characters), `tests/unit/registrations/staff-journey-deadlines.test.ts` (each row state, both languages, the full journey), `tests/integration/registrations/place-deadlines-screens.test.ts` (the list scoped to an event for the Administrator and the Organizer, real rows only, none over all events, the Tehnic refused; the queue panel; «Înscrierile primite» handing the panel its one read; a hold whose first email is queued not counted past its deadline; the registration's page — a live hold «Ține locul până», one past its deadline with the kept words, a row waiting for its address «Linkul din email expiră», an ended row keeping «Rezervarea expiră»).

Baseline `BR-V2.59-2026-10-02`.

## 636. The club's right to refuse a registration is visible on the form and the event page, once the terms in force carry it

**Amends §421 and §618.** The owner, 2026-10-02, from his phone, with production live: «La edițiile următoare trebuie sa aducă [= să apară] că organizatorul își rezervă dreptul de a refuza înscrieri». §618 put the clause in the terms' template (§3's last paragraph: the club refuses or cancels a registration only on objective grounds, says the ground by email, never on a ground the law forbids) and left to the lawyer whether the form's express-acceptance box (§421) must also name it. The owner has decided: it must appear where a participant reads.

**The gate, and why.** The terms in force on production are an older version without that paragraph; the club approves the new template in `/admin/legal` (the terms' card shows «Șablon nou»). §618's rule stands: nothing is said to a participant that the terms in force do not say. So every new sentence sits behind the terms in force, the mechanism the privacy notice's features already use — `{{participantListStates}}` (§396), `{{promotionalMaterials}}` (§562), `{{participantListNumbers}}` (§613): the club's approval of a text is the switch, with no setting and no deploy.

**The grounds stay words, and they are the switch.** §3's last paragraph keeps §618's text byte for byte, its five grounds written out in both languages — from «nu sunt îndeplinite condițiile de participare …» to «… înscrierea a fost făcută cu încălcarea acestor termeni» — never a merge field: the club and its lawyer read a draft on its version page in `/admin/legal` and in its PDF, which show a field as its raw token, and this is the paragraph the task row tells the lawyer to read first. The template's hash is §618's. `describesRefusal(body)` (`legal-documents/domain/refusal-clause.ts`) is the detector: the five grounds, joined as the paragraph joins them, found word for word in one paragraph, in either language; a test holds that module's words to the template's paragraph, so the two cannot drift. One ground reworded switches it off — the box names only a clause the terms state. `cachedRefusalDisclosed(now)` (public cache) and `termsDescribeRefusal(db, now)` (backoffice) answer true only while the terms in force carry it in **every** locale; a draft never counts.

**The form's express box.** While the gate is on, the box reads a second catalogue key, `Registration.terms.acceptWithRefusal`: «…clauzele despre anularea sau modificarea evenimentului de către club, refuzarea sau anularea unei înscrieri de către club, oprirea sau excluderea de pe traseu, …» / “…the clauses on the club cancelling or changing an event, the club refusing or cancelling a registration, being stopped or excluded on the course, …”. §421's string, `terms.accept`, is untouched and is what the box reads otherwise. The flag travels in the form's settings like `listStatesOn` (`refusalOn`; the editor's preview reads it from the database once, for the steps and the box alike, §579). The hidden `termsVersionShown`, the version recorded and everything written at submission are unchanged.

**The fold «Cum funcționează înscrierea».** While the gate is on, one more aside closes the list, after the waiting list and the family step, with the gavel glyph: «Clubul poate refuza o înscriere» — «Doar pe un motiv obiectiv din termeni (condiții neîndeplinite, date false sau incomplete, capacitate, siguranță, conduită, încălcarea termenilor), spus pe email — niciodată pe unul interzis de lege.» / “The club may refuse a registration” — “Only on an objective ground in the terms (conditions not met, false or incomplete details, capacity, safety, conduct, a breach of the terms), told by email — never on a ground the law forbids.” «Doar» makes it read as the whole list, so it names all five of the terms' grounds, briefly, and none they do not have. Without it, or when the read fails, the fold is exactly today's. It is the same component on the event page, the register page and the editor's preview.

**`/admin/tasks` and `/admin/legal`.** A row `refusalTerms`, the twin of `listStatesNotice`: open (amber), never blocking, while the terms in force lack the clause — it says the form's box and the steps say nothing of a refusal, and gives the click (`/admin/legal` → «Termeni» → «Șablon nou» → «Regenerează din șablon» → the lawyer reads §3's last paragraph → «Aprobă și publică»); done by itself once they carry it. It shows wherever terms are in force, whether or not a privacy notice is — its own gate, not the notice rows'. `/admin/legal`'s list says the same in an info line (`legal.refusalMissing`) while terms are in force without it. CLAUDE.md «Still owed» item 16 gains one sentence.

**Unchanged.** The refusal email (§618, `REGISTRATION_CANCELLED` with `refusedGround`) keeps its words and its link to the terms. The texts in force keep their words and hashes; nothing is seeded or approved by the platform (AGENTS.md §10.8, §29).

*Rejected:*
- **An unconditional sentence while the terms in force lack the clause.** It would tell participants of a right the terms they accept do not state (§618).
- **Editing §421's string.** Counsel fixed those words; they stay what the box says under terms without the clause, and a second key keeps them intact.
- **A per-event setting.** The right is the same for every event (§618), and it follows the terms, not the event.
- **A merge field for the grounds (`{{refusalGrounds}}`).** It would put a contractual clause's substance in code rather than in the text the club approves, and the draft's version page and PDF would show the lawyer a token where the grounds are. The literal words are already a switch the detector reads.

No migration.

Baseline `BR-V2.59-2026-10-02`.

## 637. «Dă-i un loc acum»: an Administrator vouches for an unconfirmed address and gives the place ahead of the line

**The owner, 2026-10-02, with the race full and a registration stuck at the first step:** a form sent during the launch, whose verification email the outage delayed; by the time the link was pressed the places and the capped waiting list were full, so the press was refused with §348's page («Locurile și lista de așteptare sunt pline, așa că adresa nu a fost confirmată și nu ți-am rezervat nimic») — the row stayed `PENDING_EMAIL_CONFIRMATION`, no place, not in the line. The owner asked for a way to seat such a registration directly and send its declaration, without another step from the person, and, on the direction, for a back-office way round the mails people lose or find in spam.

**What there was.** On such a row the staff had «Retrimite emailul» (the person presses the link again, and meets the full line again) and the desk's «Confirmă pe hârtie» (§67): the address vouched for in person *and* the declaration signed on paper, in one press — not usable without the paper, and the allocator would still have put the row in the line. What the owner wants is the first half of the desk's verb, remotely: the club vouches for the address and gives the place now; the person signs the declaration later, themselves, the one thing nobody may do for them (`AGENTS.md` §15.11).

**Decision: «Dă-i un loc acum».** A button on the registration's page, among the staff actions beside «Retrimite emailul», only on a `PENDING_EMAIL_CONFIRMATION` row, and only where the press can succeed — a local, `SCHEDULED` event with a date (§533) that has not started (`give-place-tip.ts#givePlaceNowAhead`); on a cancelled, started, external or date-to-be-announced event it is not drawn. The Administrator's alone (`canManageRegistrations`, asserted by the action, the admin service and the service). Its question: «Garantezi adresa {email} și îi dai un loc înaintea listei de așteptare. Primește pe loc emailul cu declarația; o semnează online oricând până la termen, sau pe hârtie la masă. Nu mai are de confirmat nimic.» — and, when the counts already show no free place (§592's forecast, read as the press reads them: a lapsed declaration hold is not counted against the row, since one may go for it, step 4; a family's live reservation is the row's own place), «Nu e niciun loc liber. Pe «Da» la alocarea automată, un loc adăugat merge întâi la lista de așteptare: pune «Nu», ridică «Număr de locuri» cu 1, apoi apasă din nou.» The result: «Loc dat; emailul cu declarația a plecat. Termen: {deadline}.» Both languages, each string under §511's 200 characters.

`registrations/service.ts#givePlaceNowByStaff` (through `admin-service.ts#givePlaceToUnconfirmedByStaff`), under the event lock, in one transaction:

1. **Refusals.** The row must be `PENDING_EMAIL_CONFIRMATION` (else `CONFLICT`), the event local, `SCHEDULED`, with a date (§533) and not started (the desk's own event checks, plus the start: after the gun only the desk can take a signature, and it has its own verb). The public registration window is not consulted, as at the desk.
2. **The address vouched for**, word for word as the desk writes it (§67, BR-REQ-037-07 criterion 2): `email_confirmed_at` and `email_confirmed_by_staff_user_id`; the participant's own `email_verified_at` stays unset — an attestation is not a delivered click. The desk's audit action says «declarație pe hârtie», which is false here, so the press writes a new one, `registration.address_vouched_by_staff` — «Adresă garantată de echipă; loc dat înaintea listei de așteptare («Dă-i un loc acum»)» — naming the Administrator, with how many waited at that moment.
3. **The old link.** The row's live verification link is spent (`used_at`) in the same transaction, so the old email can no longer confirm the row a second time, and its page says where the registration stands — «sign the declaration», with the resend path (§202's `ALREADY_USED` page) — never an error. §619's «replaced» page needs a newer link of the same purpose to point at, and none exists: the new email carries the declaration's link, not a confirmation's. A family's own sitting link (§543) is untouched and confirms the others on the address; this row it skips, already moved on. **A verification email not yet sent goes too** (the review of 2026-10-02): the outage's backlog, a Mailgun pause, the daily allowance's deferral or a family sitting's held seed (`SITTING_HELD`) would send it later with a link minted at render time, and after the declaration's email the person would read «confirmă-ți adresa, valabil 48 de ore» — the very step the owner wanted gone. So the press deletes, in the same transaction, the row's `VERIFY_REGISTRATION_EMAIL` outbox rows still waiting and never tried (`PENDING`, no attempt — `family-sitting.ts`'s own rule for taking a message back: one that may have left is not taken back), with their club copy; a sitting that held one reads the missing row as gone. One being retried after a provider's failure is withdrawn by the renderer instead (`render.ts`: a verification email whose registration has left `PENDING_EMAIL_CONFIRMATION` on the staff's vouching, the desk's paper included, throws `OutboxMessageWithdrawn` — nothing sent, nothing failed).
