4. **The place, ahead of the line.** The stale holds expire first (§10.6). A family's live reservation (§543) is the row's own place, exactly as the desk's allocator treats it (`allocateOrWaitlist`'s `reserved`), and the person's own family-held place is released before the count — so a family member is given the place the family already holds, even on a full race. Otherwise the place must be a counted free one: `computeOccupied(counts) < capacity` (or an uncapped event), with §160's rule for a person wanting a place who is not in the line — one lapsed declaration hold may go for the row, as `allocateOrWaitlist` lets one go for a newcomer the full line refuses. A lapsed hold is a place its holder let pass, kept only until somebody wants it (§160); the club wanting it for the row is that somebody, and the dialog's forecast says so beforehand rather than «full». Then the row is `PENDING_DECLARATION`, the ordinary `COMPLETE_DECLARATION` email is queued — `STARTS_DEADLINE` as anybody's (§513) and marked to leave now, sent by the drain after the response (§596; the owner said «ASAP») — the audit row is written, any other place the expiry released goes to the line as after an offer (`fillAvailableSpots`, a no-op on «Nu»), and the maintenance job is told the deadline.
5. **No counted free place**: the whole press is refused with `NoFreePlaceError` and §589's sentence, and nothing is written (§592: no overbooking from the backoffice, ever). Freeing one is the Administrator's, and the obvious way has a trap: with «Locurile din lista de așteptare se alocă automat» on «Da», a raised «Număr de locuri» goes at once, as an offer, to the first of the waiting list (`content/events/service.ts` → `fillAvailableSpots`), never to the registration, and the press is refused again. So the dialog and the guide say to put «Nu» first, raise by one, press, then put «Da» back; the sibling's supplementary place (below) will replace this detour.

**Why the line is not consulted.** «While anybody waits every newcomer joins the line» (§615, criterion 6) is the public door's rule: it keeps a stranger from walking past people who waited. This is the club naming a person on grounds it can state (an invited runner, an organizer who runs, a registration an outage disrupted; §618), the precedent of «Trimite-i oferta» (§615, criterion 19), which already gives a counted free place to the person the organizers name. Nobody in the line moves, nobody's count changes, and no place promised to anybody — a hold still within its deadline, an offer, a family's reservation — is taken. `AGENTS.md` §10.5 rule 3 names this exception; rule 7 is left as it was — it is not the first verb to give a place ahead of the line («Dă-i un loc» at the desk, `promoteFromWaitlistByStaff`, §15.11; «Trimite-i oferta»), and this one did not claim to be the only one.

**The deadline.** Before the participation window opens, exactly what a public confirmation gets: the window's deadline (§104, `computeDeclarationHoldExpiry`). From the moment the window opens the public door would give the club's minutes («Termene», 30 by default), which are made for a person who has just pressed the link and is reading the email — not for one whose emails went astray. So the place then waits for the window's deadline while it is still ahead, and otherwise (an event with no window, or a window whose deadline has passed) for the start, the latest a declaration can be signed anyway, on paper at the desk (`domain/hold-deadlines.ts#computeVouchedPlaceExpiry`). Not capped by the registration close: the close is the public door's. A deadline this long is the window's kind, so the email's send does not re-base it (§513). If the hold lapses, the usual rules apply (§160).

**The one risk, accepted.** A mistyped address holds a place until the deadline with nobody to sign for it: the club names the person, on grounds it can state (§618), the dialog names the address it vouches for, the audit names who pressed, and the bounce shows on the registration's page (§76). The guide says to check the address first.

**The sibling's supplementary place.** `feat/offer-a-place-any-time-with-a-supplementary-place` adds an audited place above the capacity for exactly the «no free place» case. It was not on this branch's base, so the press refuses there instead, and a comment in `givePlaceNowByStaff` names the sibling: once it lands, the «no counted free place» branch can take its helper (capacity + 1, audited, then the same steps).

**Refused.** Signing the declaration for the person — `AGENTS.md` §15.11 and §33: a declaration somebody else signed protects nobody. Skipping the allocator's count — a place beyond the capacity is overbooking by another name (§10.6, BR-REQ-034-01). A 24-hour offer («Trimite-i oferta» on a waiting row) — the owner wanted nothing more asked of the person until the signature, and an offer would need the row to be in the line first, which a full line refused. The Organizer pressing it — it changes a registration, which the Organizer reads and does not change (§289). A second confirmation email asking the person to press a link — the very step that failed.

**Not changed.** The allocator's formula and `allocateOrWaitlist` for the public door; the automatic offers; «Confirmă pe hârtie» and «Dă-i un loc» at the desk; the Organizer's rights; the email-link sweep for everybody else.

**Consequences.** `registrations/service.ts` (`givePlaceNowByStaff`, with the queued verification email's withdrawal), `registrations/admin-service.ts` (`givePlaceToUnconfirmedByStaff`), `registrations/domain/hold-deadlines.ts` (`computeVouchedPlaceExpiry`), `registrations/give-place-tip.ts` (`givePlaceNowAhead`: whether the button is drawn, and the forecast), `notifications/render.ts` (a retried verification email withdrawn), `audit/repository.ts` (`registration.address_vouched_by_staff`), `admin/registrations/actions.ts` (`givePlaceNowAction`), the registration's page, `messages/{ro,en}.json` (the button, its question, the banner, the toast, the audit label, the guide's Administrator task «Dă un loc cuiva care nu și-a confirmat adresa»); `AGENTS.md` §10.5 rule 3 and §15.11; CLAUDE.md's staff-verbs row. Tests: `integration/registrations/give-place-now.test.ts` (new), `unit/shared/confirmed-actions.test.ts`, `unit/registrations/single-row-test-kind-email.test.ts`. No migration, no dependency, no new message type.

Baseline `BR-V2.60-2026-10-02`.

## 638. The person whose held place lapses is told by email

**The owner, 2026-10-02:** «Da, fă emailul pentru cel care pierde locul» — his answer to the dispatcher's proposal, after §635 found the gap. His words of the day before, of cancellations: «dacă îi anulez, primesc mail? … atunci trebuie să îi înștiințez cumva».

**The gap.** Building §635 (the backoffice's place deadlines) showed that a declaration hold released past its deadline is written `EXPIRED` / `DECLARATION_HOLD_LAPSED` in bulk by `expireStaleHolds` and **nobody is emailed**: the person who loses the place learns it only by opening their own page. At the 21 November race, 16 people hold a place unsigned; on 19 November at 10:00 the window's deadline passes, and with 10 waiting, 10 of them lose the place silently.

**Decision.** A new message type, `DECLARATION_HOLD_EXPIRED` (migration `0121`, one `ALTER TYPE … ADD VALUE`, expand only), queued for the person whose hold was released to somebody who wanted the place.

- **Where.** In `expireStaleHolds` itself, right after the bulk `update … where id in (releasing)` — whose `returning` now gives each released row's participant, locale and deadline — through `registrations/hold-lapsed-email.ts#queueHoldLapsedEmails`: one read of the released people's delivery addresses, one `enqueueEmail` per registration, in the caller's transaction and under its event lock. The release stays a bulk update; the allocator, the deadlines and `lapsedDeclarationHoldsToRelease` are untouched, and `kind` is in no condition. `expireStaleHolds` now takes a `Transaction` (every caller already passed one), because `enqueueEmail` must.
- **Every path.** `expireStaleHolds` is the only place a declaration hold is released, so every path that releases one now emails: a newcomer's confirmation (`placeForNewcomer`; the second pass when the line grows; `allocateOrWaitlist`'s `wanting`, §348), a cancellation's refill, a late signature's sweep, «Trimite-i oferta», the desk's «Dă-i un loc», the editor's capacity raise, and the maintenance job (`fillAvailableSpots`).
- **Once per lapsed hold.** `idempotencyKey: registration:<id>:hold-lapsed:<deadline>` names the registration and the hold's deadline (`holdLapsedIdempotencyKey`): one email for each hold that lapses, whatever path released it and however many times a sweep runs — the release `PENDING_DECLARATION -> EXPIRED` happens once per hold. Not one per registration (found in review): the email's own buttons, «Înscrie-te din nou» and «Intră pe lista de așteptare», lead back to the form, which restarts the same row with the same id (`domain/family.ts`, §10.5); a key on the registration alone would leave that person's second lapse silent — the very gap this closes — and a message withdrawn at the send (below) would have used the key up for every later lapse too.
- **Never when the race is over.** Not when the sweep's `over` holds — the event has started or is no longer `SCHEDULED`: every hold goes then, nobody wanted the place, and there is nothing to do about it. A cancelled event is quiet as §331 says; its holds are not released anyway. At the send, a row whose event has since been cancelled or has started, or whose registration is no longer that lapsed hold — restarted or signed late in between (`signDeclaration`'s own sweep can release the signer's hold, then re-allocates them, §15.3 step 7), expired since for another reason (`expiry_reason` is not `DECLARATION_HOLD_LAPSED`), or lapsed again with a newer deadline than the payload's — is withdrawn (`OutboxMessageWithdrawn`), §331's rule at the moment of sending; a newer lapse has its own message under its own key, so an older one queued is never sent for it.
- **TEST rows** are released and told like real ones (`AGENTS.md` §12.6), as `REGISTRATION_CANCELLED` is: the `@test.invalid` address goes nowhere and `enqueueEmail` queues no club copy for a test registration (§320). A real one's message is copied to the club's per-message list like any participant message.
- **Never inline.** The outbox row commits with the release; the drain after the response sends it (§513), and a failed send never takes the release back (`AGENTS.md` §10.5 rule 10).

**Why a new type, not `REGISTRATION_STATE_NOTICE`.** The state notice is the staff's resend for a cancelled or expired registration, and says only «Înscrierea ta … are starea: Expirată»: it cannot say the deadline that passed, where the place went or what is left to do, and its catalogue line on `/admin/emails` says an organizer resends it. A type of its own gets its own words the club may rewrite (§247), its own road (group `confirmations`, §443, as the cancellation), its own card and line on `/admin/emails`, and its own row in the forecast.

**The words** (`templates.ts`, both languages, second person). Subject «Locul tău la {event} a expirat» / "Your place at {event} has expired". The body (editable): «Locul tău la {eventTitle}, {eventStartsAtFormatted}, **a expirat**: declarația nu a fost semnată la timp.» Then the platform's lines, after the words whoever wrote them, on the same band: «Termenul pentru semnare a fost {the deadline, in the event's zone, the month spelled out, `formatDeadlineInSentence`}.» (§377: a stated deadline carries its date; from the payload's `deadline`, the row's own column otherwise) and «Altcineva aștepta un loc, așa că locul tău a trecut la lista de așteptare.» when somebody was `WAITLISTED` at the release, or «Altcineva a cerut un loc, așa că locul tău a devenit liber.» when it was a newcomer the line had no room for (§348) — a fact of the release, written in the payload (`toWaitlist`). Then one sentence of what the person can do, one of three (`notifications/domain/hold-lapsed.ts#holdLapsedNext`, over the allocator's own rules `hasDirectAvailability`, `newcomerJoinsLine`, `waitlistHasRoom`, and `registrationState`): registration open and the line takes a newcomer — «Dacă mai vrei să vii, poți intra pe lista de așteptare.», with the button «Intră pe lista de așteptare»; registration open, a free place and nobody waiting — «Dacă mai vrei să vii, te poți înscrie din nou: mai sunt locuri libere.», with «Înscrie-te din nou»; closed, or full with no room in the line — «Online nu se mai poate face nimic. Dacă în ziua evenimentului rămân locuri libere, le dă masa de înscriere.», and no button. The button is the event's ordinary registration page, a plain URL from `APP_BASE_URL` (`AGENTS.md` §8) — no token (§12.8), no manage link and no «Nu mai pot ajunge» (§558): the registration is over. A club copy carries no button (§320).

**Read at the send, not at the queueing** — the one place this departs from the brief. Inside the transaction that releases the hold the place is free for an instant before the same transaction offers it to the line (`fillAvailableSpots`), so a reading taken there would say «te poți înscrie din nou» of a place that is already somebody else's. The drain sends seconds after the commit (§513) and reads the event as it then stands, like every other fact of a message (§331, §629's place in the line).

**A lapsed offer stays silent** (§331, not reopened): `WAITLIST_OFFER_EXPIRED` stays in `never-queued.ts`. An offer was never the person's place — they were on the waiting list, were offered a place and did not take it in its hours, and the offer email itself said until when. A declaration hold is a place the person had, kept past its deadline for as long as nobody wanted it (§160), so losing it is news.

**The forecast.** «Următoarele emailuri automate» gains its own row, «expiră un loc ținut; celui care nu a semnat, că locul a trecut la altcineva» (`holdLapsed`), for each declaration hold a lapse will release before the start, at the same instant and ahead of the «expiră un loc ținut; locul trece la următorul de pe lista de așteptare» offer row, which is unchanged — the job queues the first before it makes the second. Never for a lapsing offer.

**The privacy notice** (`legal-documents/templates/privacy-notice.ts`) is not changed: its emails clause is general — «Trimitem doar mesaje despre înscrierea ta: confirmări, legături, lista de așteptare…» / "We send only messages about your registration: confirmations, links, the waiting list…" — and this is a message about the person's own registration and its place, as the cancellation email (§547) is, which did not change it either. No new data is processed: the address and the deadline the platform already holds.

**Documents.** `AGENTS.md` §10.5 (the `PENDING_DECLARATION -> EXPIRED` paragraph says the person is emailed, once per lapsed hold, and that a hold the start releases is not) and §16.3 (the type in the list, with its paragraph and its key); `BUSINESS.md` BR-BUS-080 (the message in the list); «Ghid» → «Retrimite declarația celor care nu au semnat», the §635 step about who loses a place, gains one sentence; `/admin/emails`' catalogue (`Admin.emails.types`, `when`, `whenShort`, `forecast.sends.holdLapsed`).

**Refused.** An email *before* the deadline: the reminder of §104's window and the last call (§160) already exist. A manage link or «Nu mai pot ajunge» on an ended registration. Sending inline, in the transaction: the outbox's whole point (BR-REQ-080-02). An email for a hold the start releases: there is nobody who took the place, and the desk confirms a paper declaration into a place still free (§160). Reopening §331 for lapsed offers.

Baseline `BR-V2.61-2026-10-02`.

## 639. Administrators are emailed when a release moves a legal template

**The owner, 2026-10-02, in the morning:** «Și vreau mail de regenerează toate documentele ASAP». The email goes to the people who can do what it asks — the administrators: when a release changes a legal template, they are told at once, by email, to regenerate and approve, instead of finding «Șablon nou» by chance. A regenerate button is no substitute: while the texts in force carry the templates' words, `/admin/legal` rightly offers none (§532, §539), and when a release moves a template nothing says so outside that screen. CLAUDE.md's «Still owed» item 16 is the record of what happened without it: the approvals of §418, §445, §515, §523, §524, §550, §562, §564, §568, §613, §618 and §636 each waited in `/admin/tasks` for weeks, and nobody was told.

**Decision.** A new message type, `LEGAL_TEMPLATES_CHANGED` (migration 0122, expand only: one `ADD VALUE`), queued by a new step of the registration maintenance job (`legal-documents/templates-notice.ts`), the job the pinger already drives — no new schedule, no process, no deploy hook.

- **The trigger is `/admin/legal`'s own predicate.** The step reads `readLegalOverview` and takes the keys whose `templateNewer` is true — the «Șablon nou» chip of §539, never a second definition. The overview now also returns each key's `filledHash` (the template's words with the club's facts written in), which is what `templateNewer` already compared.
- **Cheap (§479, §549).** The overview is a dozen queries, read at most once an hour per environment: the step reads one `platform_settings` row (`legalTemplatesNotice`) and stops while its `checkedAt` is inside the hour. One exception makes it prompt: the row also remembers a stamp of the templates' own words (a hash computed from the code alone, no query), and the first run of a release whose templates differ checks at once. The email therefore goes at the maintenance job's first real run after such a release — within minutes on a day with activity, at the latest at the daily window (§577) on an idle one. The hour is claimed before the read, so a template that cannot be read is retried an hour later, not at every ping.
- **Once per change.** A change is a `key:filledHash` pair the last announcement did not carry; the fingerprint is a SHA-256 of the sorted pairs. Nothing newer: nothing sent, nothing recorded but the check. The same set, or a subset of it (the club approved some texts and not yet the rest): nothing. A new pair — another release moving a template, or a template moved again — announces the whole current set again with a new fingerprint. The row records `{ checkedAt, templatesStamp, fingerprint, announcedAt, keys, pairs }`, strict, in the same transaction as the emails. A change the club approves before the check is never announced: by then nothing is newer.
- **Who.** Every staff row whose role may approve a legal text (`canWriteLegalTexts`: the Administrators and the Superadministrator, §450) and has an address; never an Organizer, a Tehnic, a Redactor, a member, a participant or a subscriber. Each in the language of their own staff row. The idempotency key `legal-templates:<fingerprint>:<staff id>` makes it one email per person per change, whatever becomes of the settings row. Each environment has its own row and its own staff: QA announces QA's, production production's; QA's subject carries `[QA]` as every QA email does (§307).
- **The words.** Subject «Șabloanele textelor legale s-au schimbat: regenerează și aprobă» / "The legal templates changed: regenerate and approve", bilingual as every message (§96), the recipient's language first. A bold line names the texts — «Șablon nou: GDPR · Termeni de concurs», the names `/admin/legal` lists — and stays whatever a club text for this message says. The body: the texts in force keep their words until the club approves; the clicks «Documente legale» → «Versiune nouă» → «Regenerează toate», read and fill what is left written <…>, then «Aprobă ciornele»; a text with a waiting draft shows «O ciornă așteaptă deja» (approve or delete it first); a lawyer should read the texts that moved — the sentence names the declarations only when a declaration is among them and the terms only when they are, «textele schimbate, mai ales termenii» when the notice moved beside them, and never a section of any text, so a later change of the notice alone never sends the lawyer to the declarations or to §618's paragraph (`lawyerReads`); «Sarcini» shows the same rows. Every button name is read from the catalogue the screens read (`notifications/legal-templates-words.ts`), so a renamed button renames the email. One button, «Deschide documentele legale», to `/admin/legal/new` on `APP_BASE_URL`, in the recipient's language; no token — the backoffice's sign-in decides who opens it. Group `club` on the email roads (§443), like the staff invitation; not waited for on any public page, no club copy, no «Nu mai pot ajunge», no participant's privacy line.
- **Guarded.** A failure of the step is counted in the run's `errorCount`, logged by its kind and never its text, and is not retryable: the job's other work goes on and the pings are not told to hurry.
- **It asks; it never does.** `readLegalOverview` is read-only; the platform drafts, approves and writes no legal text (AGENTS.md §10.8, §29). `/admin/tasks`' rows about the legal texts stay: they are the standing reminder, this email is the knock.

**Refused.**
- *Emailing participants.* A person who accepted a version keeps it and has nothing to re-sign; the next registration signs whatever is in force then.
- *A deploy hook.* The platform has no process, and the job is the clock; a hook would be a second scheduler to keep alive and secure.
- *Repeating the email daily until the texts are approved.* `/admin/tasks` is the standing reminder; a daily email would teach the Administrators to filter it.

Baseline `BR-V2.61-2026-10-02`.

## 640. The paper confirmation says what it is for, what it does and what the person receives

**The owner, 2026-10-02**, on a registration still waiting for its email confirmation, after reading the «Ziua cursei» box: «Dacă fac „confirmare pe hârtie” primește mail de declarația și așa?» And, once told: «Pune tooltip și info in back-office pt asta».

### What the caption said, and what it left unsaid

The box's caption (`desk.fastTrackHelp`) read: «Înscrierea e confirmată pe loc, fără email; participantul semnează declarația pe hârtie, iar tu o înregistrezi. Dacă e plin, intră pe lista de așteptare.» It left four facts out, and its «fără email» read as if the person got none:

- **When.** The press is for the race-day desk, with the declaration the participant signed on paper in front of the staff member. The staff member records it on their own name — the declaration (`method = PAPER`, `attested_by_staff_user_id`) and, only on a registration still waiting for its address, the address too (`email_confirmed_by_staff_user_id`). Nobody on staff signs for anybody (§67, `AGENTS.md` §15.11).
- **The place — and which rows it concerns.** `confirmByStaff` goes through the allocator under the event lock (§67, §348, §615) only for a registration that has no place yet (waiting for its address, or a lapsed hold): it joins the waiting list when the event is full or somebody waits, and a full waiting list refuses the press, rolling the transaction back. A registration that already holds its place (`PENDING_DECLARATION`, `WAITLIST_OFFERED`) goes straight to `acceptDeclarationOnPaper`: no allocator, no waiting list, because the hold already occupies the place.
- **The email — and only with a place.** When the person gets the place, `acceptDeclarationOnPaper` queues `REGISTRATION_CONFIRMED` (the QR code, the race number, the declaration's copy as after an electronic signature, §95) and the club's copy and notice. No «complete the declaration» email is sent: there is nothing left to sign. When the press puts the person on the waiting list, `confirmByStaff` returns before that: no declaration is recorded and no email is queued at all: `allocateOrWaitlist` queues none, and `WAITLIST_JOINED` is queued only by `enqueueAllocationEmail`, which the public and restart paths call and the desk does not. The person receives the offer by email when they are given a place (automatically when a place frees with automatic offers on; with them off, when an Administrator presses «Trimite-i oferta»), and signs then. The address is another matter: on a registration that was waiting for it, `confirmByStaff` records it on the staff member's name (`email_confirmed_by_staff_user_id`) before it asks the allocator, and the `registration.confirmed_by_staff` audit row is written for a waitlisting too (to: WAITLISTED). So on the waiting list only the declaration stays unrecorded, never the address.
- **What it is not.** It is the desk's verb for a person standing there, not a way to skip the email confirmation before the race. For an address that never got its email, the Administrator's «Retrimite emailul» is the verb.

### The new words

Four catalogue lines (`Admin.desk.paperWhen`, `paperPlace`, `paperEmail`, `paperNot`, each under 200 characters, in both languages, quoting only labels the backoffice shows). Each says «who is concerned» where it is not everybody: the address clause is «if the address was not confirmed», the place line starts «someone without a place yet», the email line says that with a place the confirmation email goes (QR code, number, the declaration's copy), that on the waiting list no email goes now, the offer comes by email when the person is given a place and the declaration stays unrecorded, and that an unconfirmed address, and only that, is on the staff member's name (the fourth round restored the condition the third compression had dropped: «either way» was false on a registration whose address the participant had confirmed himself, and «when a place frees» was true only with automatic offers) (the first version said «nothing is recorded» there, which was false of the address and contradicted `paperWhen`; the second promised the waiting list «its own email», which the press never queues). The review of the first version found these stated without condition (a false promise of the email on a full event; the allocator's rule read on a row whose own hold fills the race), and the second round the email line's «nothing is recorded» and the dialog's unconditional sentence; the third found the waiting-list email promised in the email line, the dialogs and the guide, and the test now presses the button on a full event and checks that no outbox row is added, so the words cannot drift from the code.

- **The registration's page, «Ziua cursei».** An «i» beside the box's title (`ui/PaperConfirmationTip`, the four lines one under another, the tooltip's newline of §257) and, under the button, a caption of three of the four lines — when, what the person receives if they get the place, what it is not (about 500 characters; the owner asked for tooltip and info, and the caption is the always-visible «info», the «i» the full text with the place's rule). The place line is in the «i» only: the press itself answers it with the refusal's sentence. The «i» and the caption show only where the button does, on a registration that is not yet confirmed.
- **The registrations list's row menu.** «Confirmă pe hârtie» in the «⋮» menu carries the same four lines as its tooltip (`paperConfirmationText`, the one function `PaperConfirmationTip` uses, so the three places never drift), the way «Dă-i un loc» carries the refusal's sentence (§592). The item is offered there on a registration that already holds its place.
- **The confirm dialog** (`registrations.confirmOnPaperBody`, `…BodyMinor`): one conditional sentence added — «Apoi primește emailul de confirmare; dacă nu e loc, intră pe lista de așteptare, fără email acum.» (the minor's dialog, shorter still: «Apoi emailul de confirmare; dacă nu e loc, lista de așteptare, fără email acum.») — because the dialog is also shown on a registration waiting for its address, which the allocator may waitlist before any declaration is recorded: no confirmation email is queued then, and no waiting-list email either. The plain-words rule keeps a dialog under 200 characters, so the older lines were tightened to make room: «Primește locul și numărul» (as unconditional as the sentence) is gone from the participant's dialog, and the minor's dialog says «au semnat amândoi pe hârtie» without «la masă»; the rule, «doar cu hârtia semnată în față», stays.
- **The desk.** The same «i», once, beside `desk.rowHelp` — the page's always-visible line that says what the row buttons do and already names «Confirmă pe hârtie». Not on each row: twenty rows would be twenty identical «i» in a column the volunteer is scanning for names, and the help line is where the page already answers «ce face butonul ăsta». `DeskRow` is untouched. The volunteer reads the same four lines, and the last says that resending the email is the Administrator's.
- **The walk-in form's help** (`desk.fastTrackHelp`, the same fast track): the false-sounding «fără email» became «fără link din email»; the declaration is named («semnează declarația pe hârtie»); and the waiting list comes before the email — «dacă e plin, intră pe lista de așteptare; altfel primește emailul de confirmare».
- **The guide.** The desk's «Nu și-a semnat declarația» job gains the step about what the person receives — with the place, the confirmation email with the QR code, the number and the declaration's copy, and no email to sign; without one, the waiting list, no email now and the offer by email when they are given a place — in both languages.

### What was refused

A new verb, a new email or any bypass: the button, its dialog, the allocator and the audit are what they were, and the rule of `AGENTS.md` §15.11 stands — a staff member records what the participant signed; the press is not a way around the allocator, the declaration or the participant's own signature. Also refused: an «i» on every desk row (noise).

**Consequences.** `registrations/ui/PaperConfirmationTip.tsx` (new, with `paperConfirmationText`), the registration's page, the desk page, the registrations list's row menu, `messages/{ro,en}.json` (`Admin.desk.paper*`, `fastTrackHelp`, `Admin.registrations.confirmOnPaperBody*`, the guide's desk job). Test: `tests/integration/registrations/paper-confirmation-tip.test.ts` (both locales; the tip's four lines in order; the box's «i» and caption; one «i» on the desk however many rows; the list menu's tooltip); `tests/unit/i18n/plain-words.test.ts` and `tests/unit/staff/guide-words.test.ts` hold the words. No migration, no dependency, no behaviour change.

Baseline `BR-V2.62-2026-10-02`.

## 641. «Retrimite emailul» covers the waiting list too, and says which email each press sends

**The owner, 2026-10-02:** «Și vreau să pot retrimite orice pas, inclusiv declarația.»

**What stood.** The backoffice already resent each step's own message (`deriveAllowedResendMessageType`, `AGENTS.md` §15.8): `PENDING_EMAIL_CONFIRMATION` sent `VERIFY_REGISTRATION_EMAIL`, `PENDING_DECLARATION` `COMPLETE_DECLARATION`, `WAITLIST_OFFERED` `WAITLIST_SPOT_OFFER`, `CONFIRMED` `REGISTRATION_CONFIRMED` (§79; the reminder by hand, §81), `CANCELLED` and `EXPIRED` `REGISTRATION_STATE_NOTICE`; the bulk «Retrimite declarația celor care nu au semnat» exists since §606. Every step but one: `WAITLISTED` returned null, on the reasoning that nothing is waiting on the person, so there is no link to hand them again, and the registration's page and the list's menu offered no button.

**Why it has one now.** The reason held while the waiting-list email said only «te-am adăugat pe lista de așteptare». Since §629 it says where the person stands («Când am trimis acest email, erai pe locul 3 din 10», or with the club choosing, how many others wait and no position, and nothing of the count while §634's switch is off), and since §619 the pages tell people to look for the newest email. A person who lost the email, or never saw it, asks the club, and the club had no button. `BUSINESS.md`'s table already reads «Waiting list → Waiting-list status»; the code now agrees with it.

**The decision.** `deriveAllowedResendMessageType("WAITLISTED")` returns `WAITLIST_JOINED`. Nothing else is new on the send path: `resendRegistrationMessage` queues one `enqueueEmail` marked as a manual resend with the actor, under the hourly limit of the registration and with «Trimite acum» / «Pune la coadă» as they were (§540). The standing is not stored: the renderer reads it at send time with `readWaitlistPosition`, the same reader as the first send and the registration's own page (§629), so a resend after two people ahead have left says the new place, never the old one; the setting and §634's switch are read then too, nothing is said once the person is no longer waiting, and a cancelled event is refused before anything is queued (§331). The idempotency key is the manual resend's own (`registration:<id>:manual-resend:<instant>`), so it cannot collide with the first send's. A resend never changes state. The email carries the «Nu mai pot ajunge» link (`WAITLIST_JOINED` is one of the cannot-come messages, `cannot-come.ts`), so rendering it mints a fresh `MANAGE_REGISTRATION` token while the event is SCHEDULED and ahead, and that token supersedes the earlier email's, as every newer manage link does (`BR-REQ-036-02` criterion 5, §558); nothing else is minted and no state is written. The audit row of «Trimite acum» names the message type as before, and a TEST row follows the outbox's TEST rule. Administrator only, asserted on the server.

**The dialog says which email leaves.** The confirmation of «Retrimite emailul», on the registration's page and in the list's row menu, no longer says «emailul stării curente»: `Admin.confirm.resendWhat.<STATUS>` has one sentence per state in both languages, each under 200 characters, naming the person: the link to confirm the address, the link to sign the declaration, the offer of a place, the confirmation with the QR code, the waiting-list email with where the line stands now, the notice about the state of the registration; every state whose email carries a link that is minted again, the waiting list's «Nu mai pot ajunge» included, says the old one stops working; only the two that get the state notice (no token, `AGENTS.md` §16.3, `BR-REQ-037-02` criterion 4) do not. For the waiting list the words say «cu situația cozii de acum» rather than «cu locul în coadă»: with the club choosing whom to offer, or the count private, the email says no place. The guide's step «Nu a primit emailul» gains one clause for the waiting list, in both languages.

**One thing left as it was.** The public resend page's form (`/registrations/resend`, `requestRegistrationLink`) still sends nothing to a waiting person: it is a silent, throttled form for people who owe a step, and a waiting person who fills the registration form again is answered there with the same email (§217). Because it reads the one derivation, it now filters the waiting list out explicitly.

**Refused.** Resending a message that is not the state's own: a declaration link to a confirmed person, a verification to a waiting one, a reminder to anyone not confirmed (`AGENTS.md` §15.8's rule stands, and the reminder's own §81 guard). A position written into the payload at queue time (§629: stale at the first retry). A new audit action or message type: the existing ones say what happened. «Retrimite familiei» for a family that is all waiting (§588): each person's own press sends their standing. A migration and a dependency: none.

**Tests.** `tests/unit/registrations/resend.test.ts` (every status, and the dialog's sentences in both catalogues), `row-verbs.test.ts`, `tests/integration/registrations/resend-waiting-list.test.ts` (one `WAITLIST_JOINED` in the registration's language, the standing of the moment, the club's choosing, §634's switch off (no place and no count), the second resend superseding the first manage token, the refusals, the page's button and the dialog's words per state in both languages), `admin-resend.test.ts`.

Baseline `BR-V2.62-2026-10-02`.

## 642. «Trimite-i oferta» at any moment, with a supplementary place when none is free (amending §615, §420, §637)

**The owner, 2026-10-02.** The race was full (150), its waiting list capped, and a registrant the organizers wanted to seat — an invited runner, or somebody whose registration the email outage had disrupted — was waiting. The owner was told the by-hand path of §615 — open the list, set the automatic offers to «Nu», raise «Număr de locuri» in the editor, then «Trimite-i oferta» — and that the offer is refused after the registration close. He answered: «Vreau să pot „oferi loc” în orice moment, chiar și pe liste suplimentare». Asked what to change, he chose: «Trimite-i oferta» works at any time, and when no place is free it adds a supplementary place — the capacity grows by one, written in the journal, who and for whom — with no overbooking: the place is created explicitly by the Administrator's press. After the first launch he added: «vreau confirmare când depășesc limita» — the dialog says so beforehand and asks for an explicit confirmation whose button names the added place; a raise is never silent. His example: somebody who registered among the first but whose confirmation email was late in the outage, now on the waiting list.

### The detour it replaces

Under §615 a full race needed three screens to offer one named person a place: «Nu» in the editor (or the raise would offer the new place to the head of the line at once), «Număr de locuri» raised by hand, then «Trimite-i oferta» on the queue. After the close there was no way at all to send an offer by email: `offerPlaceToByStaff` threw `OFFER_AFTER_CLOSE`, because its deadline was capped by the close (§420) and would have been born lapsed. The desk's «Dă-i un loc» was the only verb left, and it needs the person standing at the table. §637's «Dă-i un loc acum» had the same detour on a full race («Nu», raise by one, press again).

### The decision

1. **After the close, the staff offer goes.** `offerPlaceToByStaff` no longer refuses after the close. Its deadline is the club's offer window («Termene», §377) from the moment of the press, capped by the **start alone** (`computeWaitlistOfferExpiry({ …, capByClose: false })`, used by this verb only). Its email carries `untilStart` beside `startsDeadline`, so the send's re-base (§513) moves it from the email's departure with the start as its one cap (`rebasedDeadline`'s `capByClose`), and the lapsed-offer guard of §520 (`offerAwaitingItsFirstEmail`) keeps it occupied while its email is queued until the start rather than the close. The maintenance job is woken for that deadline. The person accepts it by signing the declaration, as any offer. After the start the press is refused: an offer then would be born lapsed. `OFFER_AFTER_CLOSE`, `offerAfterCloseError`, `offerRefusalCode` and `Admin.errors.OFFER_AFTER_CLOSE` (both locales) are retired: this verb was their one thrower.
2. **The automatic offers keep §420's cap.** `fillAvailableSpots` and the maintenance sweep still cap an offer by the close and make none after it. An automatic offer is nobody's choice: made after the close it would go to whoever heads the line at a moment nobody watches, an email the club did not decide to send, and the list would be worked down one dead offer per run — the reason §420 gave. The staff offer is one press for one named person, by an Administrator who has just read the dialog.
3. **No free place → one supplementary place.** Under the same event lock, after the stale holds are expired (a lapsed declaration hold is released first, as far as the line wants its place, §160) and the places counted again: if a capped event has no free place (`computeOccupied(counts) >= capacity`) **and the press confirmed it** — the form posts `addPlace`, the capacity the dialog named, and it must be exactly the locked row's `capacity + 1` (`confirmsSupplementaryPlace`) — `addOneSupplementaryPlace` writes `capacity = capacity + 1` on **this one event row** (`repository.addSupplementaryPlace`; a series' other dates keep theirs; the row's `version` moves like any save's, so an editor opened before the press is told the event changed rather than writing the old number back; `updated_by_staff_user_id` is the Administrator), writes the audit row `event.capacity_raised_for_offer` — the actor, the event as the entity, `{ from, to, registrationId }`, no person — shown on that registration's page among «Ce a făcut echipa» as «Loc suplimentar adăugat pentru o ofertă («Trimite-i oferta»): 150 → 151» (`listAuditTrail` reads it with the registration's event as the key of `audit_logs_entity_idx` — entity type `event` and its id — beside the two actions and the registration's id in the metadata, so the page's query stays two index scans ORed together rather than a read of the whole trail on every view, §327, and another event's rows are never read), and, after the commit, expires the public count (`revalidatePublicContent("places")`), as the editor's capacity save does. Then it makes the ordinary offer to the chosen person, which occupies the new place **before** `fillAvailableSpots` runs in the same transaction: on «Da» the head of the line does not take it. Should the count still be full after the one place (a count above the capacity, which no path writes), §589's `NoFreePlaceError` refuses and the transaction writes nothing. An uncapped event never lacks a place and is never written. A press that did not confirm a raise — the page was read while a place was free, so its question and button were the plain ones, or before another Administrator's own raise, so it named a capacity that is no longer `capacity + 1` — is refused before anything is written, with `SUPPLEMENTARY_PLACE_UNCONFIRMED` (`Admin.errors`, both languages: «Nu s-a schimbat nimic: locurile s-au schimbat de când ai deschis pagina, iar întrebarea nu spunea că adaugi acest loc suplimentar. Apasă din nou: întrebarea spune acum cât devine capacitatea.»); the page it lands on asks again with the numbers of now. A confirmed raise that is no longer needed — a place freed in between — adds nothing and the free place is used. A second press for the same person is refused as before: the row is no longer `WAITLISTED`. Two Administrators pressing at once for two people on the last free place, both pages read while it was free, make one offer on the free place and one refusal, the capacity unchanged; the refused one, pressed again from the page drawn now, adds exactly one place — never two offers on one place, never a raise nobody was asked about. Two pressing at once on a full race, both pages naming «capacitatea devine 151», make one raise and one offer, and the other press is refused with `SUPPLEMENTARY_PLACE_UNCONFIRMED`: 151, never 152 (`tests/concurrency/capacity.test.ts`, both cases on real PostgreSQL connections).
4. **«Dă-i un loc acum» (§637) uses the same helper.** On a full race the press no longer refuses with §589's sentence: one supplementary place, the same `capacity + 1` on that one row under the same lock in the same transaction, audited as `event.capacity_raised_for_place_now` (same metadata, its own label: «Loc suplimentar adăugat pentru un loc dat acum («Dă-i un loc acum»): {from} → {to}»), on the same confirmation (`addPlace`, refused with `SUPPLEMENTARY_PLACE_UNCONFIRMED` otherwise), and the row takes it at once as `PENDING_DECLARATION`, before `fillAvailableSpots`. A family's live reservation is still the row's own place and adds nothing; a lapsed declaration hold may still go for the row first (§160).
5. **The question, before the press.** «Trimite-i oferta» is drawn on every `WAITLISTED` row of «Coada de înscrieri» and on the registration's page at any moment before the start, for the Administrator. The «i» that warned of a refusal on a full event is gone from it (it stays on «Dă-i un loc», §592). The dialog keeps §615's sentence with the deadline and adds, from the counts read for the page (`staffOfferIfMadeNow`, a lapsed declaration hold not counted as "full", as the server would release it): «Nu e niciun loc liber: apăsând, adaugi un loc suplimentar peste limită, capacitatea devine {n}.» when none is free, and «Înscrierile s-au închis: oferta e valabilă cel mult până la start.» after the close — each its own string under §511's 200 characters, both languages. When a place will be added the confirm button reads **«Adaugă un loc și trimite oferta»** instead of «Trimite-i oferta» (`staffOfferQuestion`). «Dă-i un loc acum»'s dialog says the same sentence on a full race (`confirm.givePlaceNowFull`, which no longer sends the Administrator through «Nu» and «Număr de locuri») and its button reads **«Adaugă un loc și dă-i locul»**. The server decides under the lock; the toast says what it did: «Ofertă trimisă; loc suplimentar adăugat: 151 de locuri.» (`registrationOfferedRaised`) or «Loc dat; loc suplimentar adăugat: 151 de locuri. Emailul cu declarația a plecat.» (`placeGivenRaised`), each counted through `countForm`; after «Dă-i un loc acum» the registration's own alert says it too: «Loc dat, pe un loc suplimentar: capacitatea e acum {n}. Emailul cu declarația a plecat. Termen: {deadline}.» (`registrations.placeGivenRaised`). **The confirmation reaches the server**: when the forecast names a raise, each of the three forms (the queue's row, the registration's offer, «Dă-i un loc acum») carries a hidden `addPlace` with that capacity, the actions read it (`confirmedCapacityOf`) and pass it as `{ addPlaceTo }` through `offerPlaceByStaff` / `givePlaceToUnconfirmedByStaff` to the service, which adds the place only for it.
6. **The words that said otherwise.** The «Ghid»'s «Alege tu cine primește un loc eliberat» no longer asks to raise «Număr de locuri» first, names the button that adds the place and says the offer works after the close; «Dă un loc cuiva care nu și-a confirmat adresa» drops the «Nu» + «Număr de locuri» detour; «Ce NU se poate face» says the one supplementary place is added in the open, after a confirmation, and written in the trail; «Când se pierde un loc» after the close names «Trimite-i oferta» beside «Dă-i un loc»; `SETUP.md` §39's margin recipe is «Trimite-i oferta» one by one, with «Nu» needed only to keep freed places for the club's choice; `AGENTS.md` §10.5 rules 3 and 6, §10.6 (the three places the capacity changes), §10.7 (the offer's start cap) and §15.11; CLAUDE.md's staff-verbs row.

**The added place stays.** If the person it was added for declines, lets the offer lapse, or — after «Dă-i un loc acum» — lets the declaration's deadline pass, the supplementary place stays in the capacity and is then like any freed place: on «Da», before the close, the first in line is offered it; on «Nu» it stays free until the club gives it; and on either, once nobody waits, whoever registers next before the close takes it — so a place added for one named person can end with someone else, which the «Ghid»'s step «Nu acceptă la timp?» now says in both languages (its next step already names the end of the line).

### Unchanged, on purpose

- **«Dă-i un loc»** (the desk's paper confirmation, §67, §589, §592) still needs a free place and says §589's sentence on a full race. It confirms at once, on a declaration signed at the table; a place created by a volunteer's press at the desk is a different trust than an Administrator's choice in the backoffice, and nobody asked for it.
- **The automatic offers**, their order and §420's cap (above).
- **The editor's capacity field**, its series scope and its own raise (§147), which offers the new places to the line on «Da». Raising the places there is still how they open to everyone.
- **«Adaugă o înscriere»**: still the list's door while anybody waits (§615 criterion 6); it adds no place.
- **The Organizer** reads and changes nothing (§289): both verbs are `canManageRegistrations`, asserted in the action, the admin service and the service.

### No overbooking

The allocator never exceeds `capacity`. The capacity grows only by the Administrator's explicit press, confirmed on the server (the capacity the dialog named, carried by the form, exactly the locked `capacity + 1`), by exactly one, under the event lock, in the transaction that gives the place, and the trail names who and for whom. `kind` is in no condition: a test registration holding the place or chosen for it counts as a real one.

*Rejected:*
- **Letting the allocator overbook** (an offer with no place behind it, or a place counted as «extra» outside the capacity formula): two people told «the place is yours» for one place, or a second formula every count would have to learn (§10.6).
- **A bulk raise** («add N places and offer them to these N»): the owner asked for one person at a time; a raise of many places is the editor's, with its own offers.
- **A silent raise** — the press adding a place with the ordinary button and no sentence: the owner asked for a confirmation that names the added place. That includes the stale page: a dialog read while a place was free, pressed after the last one went, must not raise the capacity, so the server checks the confirmation itself rather than trusting the count under the lock.
- **A bare yes/no confirmation** (`mayAddPlace`) instead of the capacity named: two Administrators each confirming «capacitatea devine 151» would raise it to 152, a number neither was shown.
- **Offering to somebody not on the waiting list**: a registration still waiting for its address has no verified address to send an offer to; «Dă-i un loc acum» (§637) is that person's door, and it now adds the same one place when the race is full.
- **The Organizer pressing it**: it changes the event's capacity and a registration, which §289 keeps from that role.
- **Capping the staff offer by the close and refusing after it** (§615 as it was): the very detour the owner asked to remove.
- **A separate «supplementary places» counter** on the event: the capacity is the one number every count reads; the trail already says which places were added, by whom and for whom.

**Consequences.** `registrations/service.ts` (`addOneSupplementaryPlace`, `PlacedByStaff`, `offerPlaceToByStaff`, `givePlaceNowByStaff`, `staffOfferDeadline`, `queueSpotOffer`'s `untilStart`); `registrations/repository.ts` (`addSupplementaryPlace`, `offerAwaitingItsFirstEmail`); `registrations/domain/hold-deadlines.ts` (`capByClose`); `registrations/domain/waitlist.ts` (`OFFER_AFTER_CLOSE` retired); `registrations/domain/capacity.ts` (`SUPPLEMENTARY_PLACE_UNCONFIRMED`, `confirmsSupplementaryPlace`, `confirmedCapacityOf`, `supplementaryPlaceRefusalOutcome`); `notifications/domain/deadline-rebase.ts` (`OFFER_UNTIL_START`, `offerLastsUntilStart`, `capByClose`), `notifications/deadline-rebase.ts`; `registrations/admin-service.ts`; `audit/repository.ts` (`event.capacity_raised_for_offer`, `event.capacity_raised_for_place_now`, `listAuditTrail` and its event's id); `registrations/give-place-tip.ts` (`staffOfferIfMadeNow`, `staffOfferQuestion`, `givePlaceNowAhead`'s `raisedTo`); `ui/OfferPlaceButton.tsx`, `ui/QueuePanel.tsx`, the registration's page; `admin/registrations/actions.ts` (`offerPlaceAction`, `givePlaceNowAction`, the form's `addPlace`); `messages/{ro,en}.json`; `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `SETUP.md` §39. Tests: `integration/registrations/offer-any-time.test.ts` (new), `integration/registrations/give-place-now.test.ts`, `integration/registrations/waitlist-offers-setting.test.ts`, `concurrency/capacity.test.ts`, `unit/notifications/deadline-rebase.test.ts`, `unit/registrations/hold-deadlines.test.ts`, `unit/registrations/place-deadlines.test.ts`. No migration, no dependency.

**Open for the owner.** A supplementary place added on the source date of a weekly series is copied into the dates the series makes afterwards, as any capacity on the source is — the raise touches one row, but a date generated later from that row reads its capacity; no test covers a date generated after a raise. The race is not a series, so this was left as it is: should a raise on a series' source stay on that one date, the generator would have to subtract the trail's raises.

Baseline `BR-V2.62-2026-10-02`.

## 643. «În afara locurilor»: a registration that consumes no place and enters no public number

**The owner, 2026-10-02:** «Vreau și o bifă de „ascunde la numărare” per fiecare participant.» Asked what the tick should do, he chose: **outside the places** — the registration does not occupy one of the 150 and enters no public number, but has a declaration, a race number and appears on the list if the person ticked; for organizers, pacemakers and invited runners; set by the Administrator and written in the journal.

**What there was.** The only row left out of any count was a `TEST` registration (§30, `AGENTS.md` §12.6) — which behaves as a real one in the allocator and cannot exist in production. Nothing let the club seat its own runners or a guest without taking a place from the ones it announced.

**Decision: one column and one exclusion.** `registrations.outside_capacity boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false` (migration `0123_registration_outside_capacity`, expand only). The capacity formula (`AGENTS.md` §10.6) gains one explicit exclusion: `countOccupied` leaves a row marked «În afara locurilor» out of every bucket — confirmed, a declaration hold (lapsed or not), an open offer, a family's reservation — so `computeOccupied`, the public places, the free-place count and every refusal's numbers (§589) leave it out too. The condition is on this audited column alone; `kind` is in no new condition (a `TEST` row can be outside the places too, and is marked exactly as a real one). **Why not the TEST rule:** a test row must behave as a real one in the queue precisely so the queue can be rehearsed (§30); an outside row is the opposite — a real person whom the queue must not count — so it needed its own column, never a new meaning of `kind`.

**The allocator.** `allocateOrWaitlist` gives an outside row its place directly whatever the counts — never waitlisted for want of one, never refused by a full line — with the ordinary declaration deadline and email; the stale holds still expire and the line is still served first (`placeForNewcomer`), as in every capacity-changing transaction. `expireStaleHolds` never releases an outside declaration hold for somebody wanting a place (it holds no counted place; it expires at the start like any hold), and the maintenance scan does not select an event for one. `countEligibleWaitlisted` and `lockOldestWaitlisted` read no outside row, so `fillAvailableSpots` never offers it anything. No offer is ever outside the places: marking an open offer makes it a declaration hold at once (below). «Dă-i un loc acum» (§637) treats an outside row as it treats a family's reserved one: it needs no counted place, so the press seats it on a full event and lets no lapsed hold go for it (the review of 2026-10-02 found the rebase onto §637 refusing it a place it needs none of).

**Marking and unmarking** (`setOutsideCapacityByStaff`, the registration's page, «Locurile evenimentului» → «Pune în afara locurilor» / «Numără între locuri», a confirm dialog that says what the press does in that row's state). Administrator only (`canManageRegistrations`, asserted in the action, the admin service and the service); everything under the event lock after the stale holds expire **and the line is served** — `fillAvailableSpots` at once, as `placeForNewcomer` does, before any other read and before a press that changes nothing returns (the review of 2026-10-02: a kept declaration hold `expireStaleHolds` lets go because somebody waits is that person's place, and without the refill an unmarking took it, the waiting runner offered nothing — `AGENTS.md` §10.6's «offered that place in the same transaction») — with the audit row `registration.outside_capacity_changed` (`from`, `to`, the state, and the state after when it moved) in the same transaction:
- a row holding a counted place (confirmed, a declaration, an offer, a family's live reservation): the place is released to the count and the usual refill follows — with «Da» the first in line is offered it, with «Nu» it stays free for the organizer (§615); a confirmed row or a declaration hold keeps its state, number and emails;
- a `WAITLISTED` row leaves the line and is given a place outside the places at once, through the one allocator: `PENDING_DECLARATION` with the ordinary deadline and the declaration email (the dialog says so). This is the first new transition, `WAITLISTED -> PENDING_DECLARATION`, allowed only for an outside row: the allocator's `fromStatuses` excludes `WAITLISTED` otherwise, so a counted place still reaches the line only as an offer (`AGENTS.md` §10.5 amended);
- a `WAITLIST_OFFERED` row the same (the review of 2026-10-02, round two, below): the place its offer held is released and refilled, and the row becomes a `PENDING_DECLARATION` hold with the ordinary deadline and the declaration email — the second new transition, `WAITLIST_OFFERED -> PENDING_DECLARATION`, guarded on the column the same way;
- a row waiting for its address: applies when the address is confirmed;
- unmarking a row that would then hold a counted place: only while `computeOccupied(counts) < capacity` under the lock, counted after the line was served — so it takes only a place nobody in line is owed — else §589's `NoFreePlaceError` and its sentence; the row then takes the place;
- a cancelled or expired row, or any row of an event not scheduled: the flag is read, never changed;
- **a restart clears it.** A cancelled or expired outside row the person restarts through the form (`carriedFields`) comes back counted, its end written to the journal as `registration.outside_capacity_changed` with no actor, `from: true`, `to: false`, `restarted: true`. The mark is an Administrator's act at a moment, and a seat beyond the announced places is given only by an Administrator acting at that time; kept, a restart would have seated a person on a full event without anybody choosing it, and the club could not clear it beforehand (the verb does not change an ended row). The club marks the new cycle again if it still wants to.

**The counts.** Public: `readPublicPlaces`/`publicFill` (`taken`, `confirmed`, `kept`), the places line, the free places, «Cine vine (N)» and «N confirmați — M cu numele afișat», the in-progress count and the others' «în curs de confirmare» leave outside rows out. The person's row stays in the table when they ticked, with no public marker; an unticked outside runner is not even a «Participant (nume ascuns)» row. Under the table, only while such a row is there, one sentence: «Organizatorii și invitații clubului apar în tabel fără să fie numărați: numerele de mai sus numără locurile.» The cached start-list counts gained `"outside"` in their keys with the new shape. Backoffice: the «Înscrieri» badge's `withPlace`/`confirmed` leave them out and the tooltip's event line gains «, N în afara locurilor» above zero; the registrations list's summary strip gains the pill and filter «În afara locurilor: N» (`outside=1`, a link like the state pills, §626; the strip's counts stay blind to it) and each row a chip; the event's «Înscrierile primite» says «în afara locurilor: N» beside the occupied places; the CSV and the spreadsheet gain «Outside the places» as their last column, and the export follows the pill (`outside=1`), as it follows every other filter on the list: the file is the rows on screen. The queue panel's figures were already the allocator's and needed no word. «Când se pierde un loc» (§635, `readPlaceDeadlines`) counts no outside row among the held places, the lapsed ones, the offers or a family's reservations — it holds no place to lose — and the automatic emails' forecast (`forecast.ts`) foresees no offer to the line and no «locul tău a expirat» at an outside hold's lapse, which the job never sends, while the row's own last call stays foreseen, as the job sends it. The desk shows them like anybody. The «Ghid» gains the Administrator's task «Un loc în afara locurilor: organizatori, pacemakeri, invitați».

**An open offer marked «În afara locurilor» (the review of 2026-10-02, round two).** `setOutsideCapacityByStaff` seated a `WAITLISTED` row but left a `WAITLIST_OFFERED` one a live offer with the line's short deadline, and `expireStaleHolds` lapses every offer at its deadline (§10.5) — so when the deadline passed the invited runner's registration ended `EXPIRED` with `WAITLIST_OFFER_LAPSED`, and the job's offer clause woke for it: against «no stale-hold sweep releases its hold», `AGENTS.md` §10.6 («it expires at the start like any hold») and the dialog's «Starea, numărul și emailurile rămân». Now marking an open offer seats it exactly as a waiting row is seated: the place the offer held is released to the count and refilled as the event's setting says (`fillAvailableSpots`, run before the allocator so the press's own count of offers is right), then the one allocator makes the row a `PENDING_DECLARATION` hold with the ordinary declaration deadline (the participation window's, for a race still far off, §104) and queues `COMPLETE_DECLARATION`, the hold's starting email (§513). The new transition `WAITLIST_OFFERED -> PENDING_DECLARATION` is guarded on the column as `WAITLISTED -> PENDING_DECLARATION` is: the allocator's `fromStatuses` excludes both origins unless the row is outside, so an offer of a counted place is still signed, cancelled or lapses. The offer's email, if still queued and never tried, is withdrawn — after the allocator, because while it is queued an offer past its stored deadline is not lapsed (§520) and the allocator's own sweep must still see it so — as «Dă-i un loc acum» withdraws a verification email (§637). The offer's link is replaced by the declaration's when that email is rendered: `issueActionToken` takes `alsoReplaces`, and the renderer passes `WAITLIST_OFFER` for a declaration link minted while the registration holds a declaration — both links open the same page and sign the same registration, so one stays working and the offer's page says a newer email has it (§619's «replaced», across those two purposes of one registration; the same holds for an offer that ended before the registration was restarted, whose link could otherwise still sign the new hold). The dialog says so in that state («În locul ofertei, {name} primește acum un loc în afara locurilor: emailul «{message}», cu termenul obișnuit. Locul ofertei se eliberează.»), and the Ghid's steps name the offer beside the waiting list.

**Why not keep the offer until the start** (leaving outside rows out of the lapsed-offers sweep and the job's offer clause, the review's alternative). An offer is a promise to the line with the line's deadline, and its email states that deadline and that length (§419); kept past it, the page and the email would name a deadline that no longer binds, and a third kind of hold — an offer that never lapses — would enter every reader of offers (the forecast, «Când se pierde un loc», the journey, the desk). A declaration hold outside the places is already what every other outside row holds, and every reader treats it so.

**A TEST row's dialog names no email in its body either** (§384, the same review). For a TEST row the bold email line was already dropped, but the waiting row's body still said the person gets the email «{message}». The waiting and the offered bodies now have a TEST form that names the declaration to sign and no email («… un loc în afara locurilor: declarația de semnat, cu termenul obișnuit.»), as the bold line does.

**Not changed.** The `TEST` kind and its rule; the race numbers' assignment (an outside confirmed row draws a number as any confirmed); the emails; the public list's disclosure gates (§396, §628, §634); the Organizer's rights (reads the chip and the pill, changes nothing, §289).

**Refused.**
- **Hiding the row from the public list.** The list is a disclosure the person chose (§143); hiding a ticked name because the club did not count them would make the tick mean something else. An outside runner appears exactly as any ticked confirmed runner does.
- **A second capacity** (a club reserve inside the formula, §615's rejected alternative). It would change the one formula every count reads; an exclusion on an audited row changes nobody else's count.
- **Letting the Organizer mark.** It moves a place, which is a change to registrations the Organizer reads and does not make (§289).

**Tests.** `tests/integration/registrations/outside-capacity.test.ts` (new): a full event still seats an outside row and the places line and `publicFill` do not move; an unmarking with a kept hold released for a waiting runner — the runner is offered it and the unmark refused, or, with a place left over, the runner offered first and the unmark given the other; a press that changes nothing still offers a lapsed offer's place to the next runner; «Dă-i un loc acum» seats an outside row on a full event while a counted one is refused; the export with `outside=1`; the forecast and «Când se pierde un loc» blind to an outside hold; a restart clearing the mark, with its journal row; the badge leaving an outside row's family reservation out of «cu loc»; an outside confirmed row in no public confirmed count, keeping its number; no stale-hold sweep releases an outside hold while the counted lapsed one still goes; marking a confirmed row on a full event — offered to the first in line on «Da», free on «Nu»; marking a waiting row seats it with the declaration email; marking an offered runner whose offer email left makes it a declaration hold with the ordinary deadline and one `COMPLETE_DECLARATION` queued, the line offered the freed place, the audit row's `statusAfter`, the offer's link replaced by the declaration's at render, and past the offer's deadline neither `findEventsNeedingMaintenance` nor `expireStaleHolds` touches it; marking one whose offer email is still queued, its stored deadline already behind, seats it and withdraws that email; unmarking refused when full with §589's numbers, allowed when a place is free; the audit rows; the Organizer refused; a cancelled row refused; a TEST row outside; the public start list's counts (named, outside named, the anonymous); the summary strip, the list filter and the badge's split and tooltip line. `tests/concurrency/capacity.test.ts` gains a case: one counted place free, ten newcomers and an unmarking racing for it on separate connections — the counted places end at the capacity whichever wins. Updated: the state machine's named transitions (22), the TEST-row email gates (nine on the registration page beside §637's, and a new case: the waiting and offered bodies for a TEST row name no email), the CSV and spreadsheet column positions, the privacy suite's others counts, the confirm-first classification of the new action, the TEST-row email gate on the registration page. Edited, not run: `tests/e2e/terms-on-registration.spec.ts` (the export's last column).

**Consequences.** Migration `0123_registration_outside_capacity`; `db/schema/registrations.ts`; `registrations/repository.ts` (`countOccupied`, `listPlaceCountInstants`, `countEligibleWaitlisted`, `lockOldestWaitlisted`, `lapsedDeclarationHoldsToRelease`, `findEventsNeedingMaintenance`, `isOutsideCapacity`, `writeOutsideCapacity`, `countOutsideCapacity`, the start list's counts), `service.ts` (`allocateOrWaitlist`, `setOutsideCapacityByStaff`, `givePlaceNowByStaff`, the restart's `carriedFields`), `notifications/forecast.ts`, `admin-repository.ts#readPlaceDeadlines`, `domain/state-machine.ts` (two transitions), `admin-service.ts#setOutsideCapacity`, `action-tokens/repository.ts#issueActionToken` (`alsoReplaces`), `notifications/render.ts` (the declaration link replacing the offer link), `domain/link-status.ts` (its comment), `admin-repository.ts` (the rows, the filter, the summary), `nav-count.ts`, `csv.ts`, `workbook.ts`, `ui/SummaryStrip.tsx`, `domain/summary-filter-links.ts`; `public-cache/reads.ts`; `events/ui/StartList.tsx`; the registrations list, the registration's page, the event's page, `BackofficeShell.tsx`, the export route, `admin/registrations/actions.ts#setOutsideCapacityAction`; audit action `registration.outside_capacity_changed`; `messages/{ro,en}.json`. Docs: `AGENTS.md` §10.5 (both transitions), §10.6, §15.11 (verb 6, and §637's line); CLAUDE.md's no-overbooking row and its staff-verbs row («Nothing else» now names the Administrator's mark); `BUSINESS.md` BR-BUS-034; `SETUP.md` §39. No dependency.

## 644. The hourly claim under four workers: what one CI run in eight showed, and the fix

**The failure.** On PR #341's CI run (job «e2e 1/8», step `yarn test:concurrency`, PostgreSQL 17.6 in a service container) `tests/concurrency/hourly-pace.test.ts` — §605's four workers claiming Mailgun's hour at once, an allowance of three — failed with `expected 6 to be 3`; the other seven shards ran the same commit green, and the batch under test touched no outbox code. One run in eight.

**The reproduction.** On a private local database (PostgreSQL 16) the file passed thirty times in a row. A probe running the test's round two thousand times, with each claimer's share recorded, went wrong from round 361 on and stayed wrong: 1 422 of 2 000 rounds, and the twenty recorded were all one claimer's: `6+0+0+0`, `4+0+0+0`, `8+0+0+0`, `0+7+0+0` — never two claimers with three each. The advisory lock was doing its work: the three claimers that waited counted the first one's rows as in flight and took nothing. What broke was the first claimer alone, taking four to nine rows under a limit of three — the most the probe saw, not a bound: the sub-select runs again once per outer row, so in principle one claim can reach every due row. Round 361 is where autovacuum ran on `email_outbox`: 57 646 dead rows, `reltuples` 0 over pages it could not hand back while the rounds kept going.

**The evidence.** `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` of the claim's statement in that state: `Nested Loop Semi Join` with an index scan of the primary key outside and `Subquery Scan → Limit → LockRows → Sort` inside, `loops=30` — the sub-select `SELECT id … ORDER BY created_at LIMIT 3 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` run again for every outer row. Each re-run meets the rows this same UPDATE has just changed; to the row lock they are "updated by the current command", which `LockRows` skips, so the `LIMIT 3` lets the next oldest through, and the outer row that is one of them is updated too. Made on purpose — 3 000 rows inserted and deleted, then `vacuum (truncate false, analyze)` — the same state is there on every run, in one session with no concurrency at all: twenty claims of a limit of three took 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 9 rows. In a healthy state the planner picks a hash semi join, which runs the sub-select once, and the claim is exact; that is why every earlier run passed, and seven shards of eight. The brief's other questions answered on the way: the lock, the count and the claim run on one connection inside one transaction (drizzle's `transaction` on a pool takes one client); the lock binds `pg_advisory_xact_lock(bigint)` with the same key every time; `readEmailPlan` before the transaction does not run when the allowance is passed, and changes nothing about the count when it does; the fixed `now` and the bounds compare as `timestamptz`.

**The cause.** A limited, locking sub-select inside an UPDATE is not a limit: PostgreSQL may run it more than once in one statement, and the second run does not see what the first one locked as locked. Not a race, a plan — chosen by the statistics, which the test's own deletes and autovacuum move.

**What production could have seen.** The same statement made every claim: the job's, the drain after a response, «Trimite acum». With the bad plan a claim could take more than the hour's room (§605 — over Mailgun's hour, what disables an account on probation), more than the batch size (twenty), and more newsletter rows than the reserve's cap (§445). The plan needs statistics that call the outbox nearly empty, which is a table that has just been drained — QA, or production in its first weeks, more than production with a season's sent rows; nothing proves it happened, and nothing proves it did not.

**The fix.** The claim is two statements inside the same transaction, under the same lock: `SELECT id … ORDER BY created_at LIMIT n FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, run once, returns and locks at most `n` ids; the UPDATE then changes exactly those ids, already ours, and returns them. An empty pick skips the UPDATE. The count, the lock, the order and the roads are unchanged. A second test in the same file, named by BR-REQ-080-02 whose new criterion it proves, makes the bad statistics itself and claims with a limit of three, then with a batch of five, five rounds, expecting exactly those rows, oldest first; on the old code it fails every run, and it puts the statistics back after (`vacuum analyze`) so the file's first test does not inherit them — with the old code it then failed with exactly CI's `expected 6 to be 3`. `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` says the rule for the next limited claim.

**Refused.** A retry of the test or of the claim — it would hide an over-claim that production can make. A weaker assertion ("at most the room") — the room is exactly what one claim may take. A wider lock (a table lock, or SERIALIZABLE) — the over-claim is inside one statement, so no lock between workers touches it. Planner settings (`enable_nestloop = off` in the transaction) or a `MATERIALIZED` CTE — they depend on what the planner does today; a SELECT run on its own is evaluated once by definition.

Baseline `BR-V2.62-2026-10-02`.
